# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision 39f2597a, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258,
975feb3 and a284420; waves L5 and L6 were anchored to 975feb3, waves L7 to L14 to
a284420.
Revision 39f2597a adds front matter, appendices and figures. The appendix-local
direct-bound constant `C_2` of `P:d1-upper`, `P:low-alpha-upper` and
`C:planar-range` is renamed `C_dir` (`C_dir^gen`); the intrinsic `C_2(Gamma,a)`
is unchanged. The attribution of the quoted source result `T:first` is clarified
(wording only; `T:first` is not formalized here). A front-guide paragraph
pointing readers to `L:white-test` and `P:nogo-05` is added. A readability pass
adds explanatory sentences to 207 of the 249 proofs (one more proof, of
`P:original-signed-point-upper`, changes only by an original-text correction
listed below); statements, displays, labels and references are kept, and old
proof lines are kept word for word except 50 reworded and 32 re-wrapped lines.
Six places of the original text are corrected (two unparsable sentences, a
garbled clause and three typographical errors in statements of results not
formalized here). An unused setup step is removed from the proof of
`P:symplectic-block-mean` (not formalized here).
Every cited label exists exactly once at 39f2597a. TeX line numbers were moved
to 39f2597a by the git diff of each file or, inside proofs rewritten by the
readability pass, by the pass's per-file line maps. A range moved by the git
diff has the same text at both revisions up to that rename; a range moved by a
line map keeps every cited line word for word, with explanatory sentences
inserted between them, except 1 range whose words are kept but re-wrapped around
inserted sentences. The 1593 ranges resolved by hand were read: each cites the
same object at both revisions, though its wording may have changed. The file of
every locator was checked against the labels cited next to it (script checks and
hand resolutions recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

## Scope

- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
- The rows cover every public theorem (3654) except
  `MaskedAuxiliaryReal.Cx.ext_iff`, which `@[ext]` generates (3653 rows), and 849 definitions whose
  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 113
  public definitions have no rows of their own: 107 (for example `kappa`,
  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,
  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`, `SpaceTimePositivity.timeMeasure`,
  `TerminalWick.chainMassReal`, `WaveGreenFourier.spherePhi`,
  `OccupationCeilingExact.stepG`, `HigherRieszTwo.dens2`,
  `FixedSplit.extTime`, `FockColumnBound.mulOp`,
  `TerminalWickInputs.chainMap` and `TerminalWickRegularization.regMap`; every
  public definition of the wave-L12, L13 and L14 modules has a row, the
  compiler-generated constructor declarations without a source range
  excepted) only
  name quantities or measures used in
  those statements, one is the structure `FockColumnBound.L2Map` (a
  Lean-route data structure), four are the instances that make
  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space, and one is the syntax
  constant `WhiteFour.tacticTw_close`; read their bodies in the
  Lean source or in `Audit/`. Counting convention: a public definition is a
  non-private `def`, `abbrev`, `instance`, `structure` or `inductive` written
  in the source of the `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` and
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules; declarations generated by Lean
  (structure projections, constructors, recursors, matchers, `noConfusion`
  and the instance `MaskedTrigProducts.instDecidableEqTrig` produced by
  `deriving DecidableEq`) are not counted. The inventory is taken from the
  elaborated environment (962 public definitions: 849 with rows, 100 `def`
  and 7 `abbrev` quantities, the structure `FockColumnBound.L2Map`, the
  four instances, and `WhiteFour.tacticTw_close`, the syntax constant of a
  local tactic macro, which has no row and no claim since release v0.10.0). Earlier versions of
  this page said 89 and 507: two definitions were left out of the running
  count, one when wave L2 was added and one when wave L5 was added.
- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
  inner-product and finite-word facts. The exception is `HermiteWordFock`
  (wave L9), which applies `HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` to the Fock model of
  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
  multi-mode case is the library module `FiniteWordCutoff` (wave L11).
- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
  The Index by label is a pointer table: each manuscript label (and one row
  for declarations with no direct label) points to the sections whose tables
  formalize it, each followed by the category phrase of that section's
  heading. It carries no per-declaration lists or qualifiers: what each
  declaration states and the analytic inputs it takes are stated once, in
  the section tables. Labelling convention: every backticked manuscript
  label in a section-table label cell is an assignment and creates an Index
  pointer; a label mentioned only as context goes in the "What it states"
  cell as "(Context: ...)"; a "no direct label" cell contains no manuscript
  label.
- Model-choice register. A registered model choice is a documented
  definitional choice that is the standard construction of a manuscript
  object, recorded with the identification that is not formalized. M1 (wave
  L6, Le's decision 4): the wave Green measure in `d = 3` is
  `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) volume.toSphere`, Mathlib's sphere
  measure scaled to the radius-`s` sphere; its identification with the
  surface (Hausdorff or Riemannian) measure of the TeX is not proved. Results
  whose only modelled object is M1 (`L:low-alpha-convolution`,
  `L:phase-contractions`, `L:higher-riesz` and `L:alpha-one-convolution`,
  and the sections `LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`,
  `L9Completed`, `HigherRieszThree`, `AlphaOneConvolution` and
  `L10Completed`; and, in wave L11, `L:uniform-series-tail` for the
  constructed chain measures in `TerminalWickInputs`; in wave L12,
  `L:terminal-wick` in `TerminalWickComplete`) are whole results;
  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (`DampedSmoothing`, wave L12) uses M1 and M3
  (below); `LowAlphaUpper` (wave L13) uses M1 with M4 in `d = 3`. The narrower section `HigherRieszTwo` also uses M1, only in the
  steps it shares with `d = 3`, and the proof-steps section
  `TerminalWickRegularization` uses M1 in `d = 3`. M2 (wave L11, item K10): the Gaussian
  space `L^2(Omega; X)` over finitely many independent standard Gaussian
  coordinates, with `X` a complex inner product space, is the space of
  normalized Hermite coefficient vectors `(Fin m -> N) -> X` (as in
  `HermiteFock`, `FockForm` and `FixedSplit`; the Hermite isometry
  `HermiteFock.integral_norm_sq_iota` is proved), multiplication by a
  coordinate acts by creation plus annihilation, and finite sums and Bochner
  integrals of words are taken coordinatewise in the Hermite basis; the
  identification of a Bochner integral in `L^2(Omega; X)` with the
  coordinatewise integral is not proved. `L:finite-word-cutoff` (section
  `FiniteWordCutoff`), whose only modelled object is M2, is a whole result;
  `FockSandwichModel` (wave L12) uses M2 for the cutoff Hilbert space and is
  narrower for another reason (the Fourier-side identification, below). M3
  (wave L12, item C1; accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the
  smoothed covariance `p_eps * Gamma` of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines
  1052-1053, `p_eps` the centered Gaussian density of covariance `eps I`) is
  the measure with Lebesgue density `gamma_eps(x) = int p_eps(x - y)
  Gamma(dy)` (`DampedSmoothing.smoothedCov`, as the TeX defines the
  convolution of a density with a measure); its identification with
  Mathlib's `Measure.conv` of `N(0, eps I)` and `Gamma` is not proved.
  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (section `DampedSmoothing`), whose only
  modelled objects are M1 and M3, is a whole result.
  M4 (wave L13, item DM0; decision 2 of wave L13, accepted by the author on
  2026-11-13): the two-chain diagram integrals
  `J_(m,n,D)(t)` of `E:mixed-diagram` (main TeX lines 808-832) are the
  deterministic integrals of `DiagramModel`: labels `Fin (m+n)` with a
  separate root for each chain, `Pi_k` as the fixed-point-free involutions of
  `FiniteWick` (self-pairings included), each pair evaluated once at its
  smaller label, the open simplices `[0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^n_<`, the temporal
  kernel in `[0, infinity]`, and the Green factors read as measures of the
  increments `y_l - y_(p(l))` (the TeX's generalized-kernel reading, which
  covers the `d = 3` sphere measure of M1); for a covariance measure `Gamma`
  the TeX's `J_(m,n,D)(t)` is `diagramLim`, the limit as a common noise width
  `eps -> 0+` of the diagrams with `p_eps * Gamma` (`covEps`). The
  identification of the increment form with the TeX's positions form is
  proved in `d = 1` (`DiagramBridge`) and not in `d = 2, 3`; the
  identification of the TeX's joint limit at arbitrary vertexwise widths
  (`L:joint-fixed-order`) with this common-width limit is part of the model
  M4 and is not proved; the common-width convergence of every diagram is the
  named input `DiagramLimits`, and with the finiteness of the limit a clause
  of `MixedMoment`; convergence and finiteness are proved for white noise in
  `d = 1` (`WhiteCollapse`, `D1Upper.diagramLimits_white`; `MixedMoment`
  itself stays supplied there), and the order-two Riesz limit is proved in
  `RieszFourDiagrams` (`rieszDiagramLimit`). Statements about `diagram`, `diagramLim`,
  `coeffA` or `coeffALim` whose only modelled objects are M4 (and M1) are
  whole results (`L:d1-spatial` in `D1Spatial`, `P:white-four` in
  `WhiteFour`); statements about the solution `u` or the chaos terms `X_n`
  rest on `MixedMoment` and are narrower (split modelled-object rule). M4 is
  used by `DiagramModel`, `DiagramBridge`, `D1Spatial`, `TwoSimplexTime`,
  `D1Upper`, `LowAlphaUpper`, `OrderTwoDiagrams`, `RieszFourDiagrams`,
  `WhiteCollapse` and `WhiteFour`. M5 (wave L14, items K1a and K1b; decision
  4 of wave L14, "K1 as `Lp G 2` completions, no tensor identification";
  accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the completion
  spaces of the occupation and source sections are `L^2` completions, not
  tensor products. `OccupationCompletion.HK p G`, standing for
  `H_t (x) G`, is the Hausdorff completion of Bochner `L^2(I; G)`,
  `I = (0,1)`, for the kernel seminorm
  `(int int_(I^2) |s-t|^(-a) <F(s), F(t)>_G)^(1/2)`, so `J_G` is defined on
  all of `L^2(I; G)`; `Ht p = HK p R` stands for `H_t`; `Hsp S` is the
  Hausdorff completion of `C_c^infinity(R^d)` for `B_Gamma` (the TeX's own
  definition of `H_sp`); `HI p S = HK p (Hsp S)` stands for
  `H_I = H_t (x) H_sp`; and `SourceHeatGram.HGamma mu`, standing for
  `H_Gamma`, is the closure in `L^2(mu; C)` (as a real Hilbert space) of the
  transforms of the real tests, a completion of the tests for
  `B_Gamma(f,f)^(1/2)`, with `H_I` over it `HK p (HGamma mu)`. Not proved:
  the identification of `HK p G` with a tensor product, of `Ht` with the
  completion of `C_c^infinity(I)`, of `HI` with the completion of smooth
  space-time tests and with the Hilbert tensor product of
  `L:cameron-supported-tensor`, and an isometry between `Hsp` and `HGamma`.
  M5 is used by `OccupationCompletion` (`L:positive-raw-embedding`,
  `L:occupation-raw-square`, both narrower for other reasons) and
  `SourceHeatGram` (`L:source-spatial-heat`, a whole result over M5, and
  `L:positive-physical-gram`, narrower for another reason), and by
  `ClassOH1`, whose two `Q` rows (`continuous_Q`,
  `occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper`, steps of `L:occupation-raw-square`)
  map into `Hsp`. M6 (wave L14,
  item O; accepted by the author on 2026-11-13): the real Sobolev space `H^1(R^d; R)` is
  `ClassOH1.H1R d`, the graph of the weak gradient
  (`WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient`) in `L^2(R^d; R) x L^2(R^d; R^d)` with the
  product topology, the TeX's own description in the proof of
  `P:spatial-four-linear` (`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` lines
  356-358); its topology is proved to be that of Mathlib's Bessel-potential
  space `H^1` (`ClassOH1.isEmbedding_toMH1`, `topology_eq_induced`); not
  proved is that every real element of Mathlib's `H^1` comes from `H1R d`.
  The class `O` of strongly `H^1`-measurable fields (`ClassOBridge.IsClassO`)
  is defined over this space, with a.e.-strong measurability for Lebesgue
  measure on `(0,1)`. Results whose only modelled object is M6
  (`P:spatial-four-linear` in `ClassOH1`; `P:occupation-physical-class` and
  `P:raw-occupation-energy` in `ClassOBridge`) are whole results; M6 is also
  used by `OccupationCompletion` (via `ClassOH1`) for `L:occupation-raw-square`.
  Missing constructions are not model choices: they make a result narrower (for
  example the noise `W` of `P:masked-quotient-obstruction`, the ground
  family of `L:raw-block-indexed-cone`, the chain measures used for
  `L:uniform-series-tail` before wave L11 (constructed in
  `TerminalWickInputs`), the operator paths of `P:radius-mean-anchor`, the
  solution moments of `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and
  `C:static-moment-constant-continuity`, the cutoff evolution, propagators
  and coefficients of `L:fixed-split`, and the identification of the
  Fourier-side operators of `FockColumnBound` with the physical-space
  operators of `L:fock-form` and `L:interval-contractions`, also for the
  operator form of `L:fock-form` in `FockSandwichModel`; and, from wave L13,
  the solution `u` and its chaos terms `X_n` of `P:mixed` (statements about
  them rest on `MixedMoment`), the abstract `ThreeMomentModel` of
  `C:three-product-riesz` and `C:three-finite-images`, the uniform mean `T_R`
  and the multiplier form `v_L` of `L:positive-physical-gram`, and the
  operator `H_V` and the pairing `v_V` of `P:signed-closed-form`).
- The 115 `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules: 40 are whole-result
  modules (every whole result with nothing supplied, the two named inputs of
  `AlphaOneConvolution` being discharged in `L10Completed` and the two of
  `EndpointLemmas` in `RieszPositiveDefinite`, except
  `P:tube-rayleigh-transfer` in `SourceTube`, a whole result with two named
  inputs; `FiniteWordCutoff` also carries a step row of
  `P:interval-coefficients` with named inputs, and `ClassOH1` a step row of
  `L:occupation-raw-square`), 48 are narrower-result modules, and 27 are
  foundations or proof steps (`WaveKernel`, `SpectralHomog`,
  `TimeFractional`, `DampedNorms`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest`,
  `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalFloor`, `SeriesType`, `H1Density`, `FiniteWick`,
  `GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`, `WaveGreen`, `WaveGreenFourier`,
  `SpaceTimePositivity`, `IntervalScalar`, `StaticPhaseCauchy`,
  `FixedSplitCore`, `WhiteModel`, `TerminalWickRegularization`, and from
  waves L13 and L14 `DiagramModel`, `DiagramBridge`, `TwoSimplexTime`,
  `WhiteCollapse`, `PhaseShiftControl`, `H1Mathlib`). Some
  modules without a section of their own are covered in the section of the
  module they serve. Together they model `H:homog` and give, by labelled
  result, 44 whole results with the manuscript's hypotheses alone, one whole
  result with named inputs (`P:tube-rayleigh-transfer`, wave L12), 16
  narrower results with the manuscript's hypotheses, and steps, parts or
  narrower forms of 34 further results with named inputs supplied (see
  `COMPLETION.md`), to the scopes specified below (the narrower conclusions
  are stated per result). Sixty-four (the 44 whole and 16 narrower results
  with the manuscript's hypotheses, and
  `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters`, `E:masked-time-schur` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`) need no supplied input:
  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also
  stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers
  `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the Rayleigh
  lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not
  formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under the
  full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` models
  clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses
  (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top
  of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (`GaussianIBP`).
  `L:variational-control-dilation` is stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its integral form
  and the rate defined as the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum
  `E:variational-real-rayleigh` (over a weak-gradient `H^1(R^d)` built in
  `WeakSobolev`, identified with Mathlib's Bessel-potential `H^{1,2}` in
  `H1Mathlib`, wave L13); the identifications
  with `E W(Psi)^2` and `sqrt(-E_s)` are not formalized.
  `P:masked-spectral-growth` is stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_spectral_growth_paper`, and the
  homogeneity of the spectral measure, which the TeX derives in the proof of
  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, is derived from `H:homog`
  (`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Hence `P:clock-copy-obstruction` and the
  finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (with `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`)
  are stated with nothing supplied by the `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers. The
  rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (`N_0`, the scaling identities, the
  tails `E:damped-tail-norms`, and the upper bounds of
  `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`, for a measurable multiplier in `[0,1]` on
  the spectral measure and measurable Laplace domains `S subset S'`) is
  `DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper`, for an arbitrary family
  `G` with the mass identity `GreenMass G` as hypothesis, and is stated with
  `H:homog` alone (no `Gamma != 0`) and nothing supplied by
  `WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave`: `WaveGreen` builds the wave
  Green measures `G_s` for `d = 1, 2, 3` (in `d = 3` with Mathlib's
  `Measure.toSphere` taken as the surface measure, a definitional choice)
  and proves their mass `G_s(R^d) = s`, finiteness, support in the closed
  radius-`s` ball and the scaling `G_s(sA) = sG_1(A)`.
  `L:masked-time-completion` is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (`0
  < a < 1`, `T > 0`; no `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_time_completion_paper`: the
  completion `H_a` is built (`TimeCompletion`, Mathlib's completion of
  `L^2(0,T)` under the temporal form, over `C`), with positive
  semidefiniteness, separability, the continuous extension, the complexified
  norm identity, interval amplitudes, and density of the real compact smooth
  tests on `(0,T)`. `E:masked-time-schur` and `L:masked-temporal-modulation`
  are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by `time_schur_paper` and
  `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` for the defining double integral, and
  `E:masked-time-schur` also for the norm of `H_a` (`emb_norm_sq_le`).
  `L:masked-trig-products` and `L:masked-continuous-wave` are stated in this
  `H_a` with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied
  (`masked_trig_products_completed_paper`,
  `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper`). `P:frequency-row` and
  `C:frequency-time` are stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog`
  with `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`, and of `beta` for the corollary)
  by `frequency_row_paper` and `frequency_time_paper`, with the constant
  chosen before `d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h`. `L:occupation-kernel-row` and
  `L:spatial-physical-pair` are stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `D = q - 2a`) by `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
  and `spatial_physical_pair_paper`. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` is stated
  with the manuscript's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by
  `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper`, and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier` is
  proved for any complex Banach space; its clause for a real `H` after
  complexification is stated in wave L13 (`MaskedAuxiliaryReal`, below). `L:variational-heat-envelope` and the
  display of `L:variational-global-mean` are stated with the section's
  hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `variational_heat_envelope_paper` and `variational_global_mean_paper`; the
  latter's first sentence (all mixed derivatives bounded) is proved in wave
  L13 (`VariationalMeanDerivatives`, below).
  `L:phase-bessel` is proved for any measure space and any complete complex
  inner product space and stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by
  `phase_bessel_paper` (separability carried and not used).
  `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` is stated with the proposition's
  hypotheses by `masked_quotient_obstruction_paper`, which also proves that
  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` satisfies `H:homog` (with `alpha = 1`) and
  `Gamma != 0`; `E W(F)^2` is read as the covariance functional of `E:cov`
  (the noise is not constructed, so this is a narrower result: the
  identification with noise variances is not formalized). The Rayleigh-form part of
  `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz
  bounds and `0 < I_Psi < infinity`, for the rate defined by
  `E:variational-real-rayleigh`) is stated with the section's hypotheses by
  `variational_unmasked_rate_paper`; its operator half (`H_s` self-adjoint,
  `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`) is not formalized. `L:spatial-static-controls` and
  `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` are stated with the section's hypotheses
  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
  `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper` and
  `spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper` (`SpatialOccupationCompleted`),
  with the score displays `E:spatial-static-score` and
  `E:spatial-smooth-score` in an existential form; their supremum forms take
  the named input `S1Bdd` there and are stated with nothing supplied in
  `L8Completed` (wave L8); `R_0` is positive and
  finite with nothing supplied, by the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <=
  2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2)` of `SpatialFourierBound`
  (`L:spatial-fourier-bound`, which the manuscript uses for the same purpose
  since `a284420`), so `R_0 < infinity` does not depend on `T:full-upper`. `L:positive-series-type` is stated with the
  lemma's hypotheses by `positive_series_type_paper`.
  `C:white-relative-width` and `L:white-clock-laplace` are stated with the
  section's hypotheses by `white_relative_width_paper` and
  `white_clock_laplace_paper`, the latter with the damping parameters
  `eta_1, eta_2 > 0` of `E:white-self-clock-transform` made explicit (the

  `\|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2` (used for manuscript constants, decision 5)
  equivalent, and proves the density of real test and Schwartz functions.
  `ResolventForm` (narrower result) ports complex Lax-Milgram over `RCLike`
  and builds, for an abstract bounded self-adjoint operator standing for the
  pairing `v_V` with `E:signed-multiplier-form` supplied as the named input
  `SignedMultiplierForm`, `E:signed-form-bounds` and the bounded resolvent
  `R_V = (H_V + c)^(-1)` of the form (self-adjoint, positive, injective,
  `\|R_V\| <= 1`; `signed_closed_form_resolvent_paper`). `P:signed-closed-form`
  is therefore a narrower result with inputs supplied (coverage
  inputs-supplied, weaker): `H_V` itself is not constructed (no
  `LinearPMap`), and `D(A^(1/2)) = H^1`, `E:signed-quarter-phase`, the
  negative dual completion `H^(-1/2)`, the commutation with real conjugation
  and `L:signed-limiting-multiplier` are not formalized.
  In wave L14: `P:spatial-four-linear` is stated with the section's
  hypotheses and nothing supplied, every conclusion, by
  `ClassOH1.spatial_four_linear_whole_paper` (joint continuity of `C_4` on
  `(H^1)^4` in the product topology, `H^1 = H1R d`, M6), a whole result. The
  class `O` of strongly `H^1`-measurable fields is formalized
  (`ClassOBridge.IsClassO`), the joint representatives of lines 534-540 are
  constructed and the converse proved, so the suprema over `O` equal those
  over joint representatives; with nothing supplied
  `P:occupation-physical-class` and `P:raw-occupation-energy` are stated over
  `O` itself with every conclusion (`occupation_physical_class_whole_paper`,
  `raw_occupation_energy_whole_paper`), whole results over M6;
  `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` with `g_eps` in `O`
  (`occupation_rayleigh_selection_whole_paper`) stays narrower (the rate in
  Rayleigh form and the cost in integral form), and so do
  `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` and `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` over `O`
  (`intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_classO_paper`,
  `intrinsic_spatial_comparison_classO_paper`; `C_2 <= U_2` missing, `S_2^pos`
  in place of `C_2`). The zero-covariance cases are
  `ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper`, except `C_2 = 0`, the vanishing of
  `S_c^pos` and of the original means, `Q = 0` and the free moment model.
  `L:positive-raw-embedding` is stated with the section's hypotheses and
  nothing supplied by `OccupationCompletion.positive_raw_embedding_paper`
  (`E:positive-bochner-inclusion` for every real Hilbert space `G`, and
  `\|Psi\|^2_(H_I) = v_Psi`, over M5); the mean identity of
  `E:positive-raw-mean` and the canonical versions are not formalized
  (narrower; wave L15-UM, not started). `L:occupation-raw-square` is stated
  with nothing supplied by `OccupationCompletion.occupation_raw_square_paper`
  (`Q : H^1 -> H_sp` with `<Q(f), Q(h)> = B_Gamma(f^2, h^2)`, continuous on
  `H^1` by `ClassOH1.occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper`, and `rho_g` in
  `H_I` with both identities of `E:occupation-raw-identities` and
  `<Psi, rho_g> <= sqrt(v_Psi A(g))` for fields of `O` modelled by joint
  representatives); narrower, since the field statements are not restated on
  `O` itself. `L:source-spatial-heat` is stated with the section's hypotheses
  and nothing supplied, every conclusion
  (`SourceHeatGram.source_spatial_heat_paper`), a whole result over M5;
  `L:positive-physical-gram` (`positive_physical_gram_paper`) is narrower:
  the label row `E:positive-label-row` and the entrywise order (left out by
  wave L14 decision 5) are not formalized. `L:product-endpoints`,
  `L:plane-endpoints` and `L:endpoint-closure` are whole results with nothing
  supplied (`RieszPositiveDefinite.product_endpoints_paper_proved`,
  `plane_endpoints_paper_proved`, `EndpointLemmas.endpoint_closure_paper`;
  the `EndpointLemmas` wrappers take positive definiteness as the named
  inputs `RieszProductPD` and `PlaneRieszPD`, which `RieszPositiveDefinite`
  proves by Gaussian subordination, together with `RieszIsoPD`).
  `C:three-product-riesz` and `C:three-finite-images` are stated with the
  endpoint hypotheses discharged and the moment and asymptotic bounds from the
  named input `ThreeTransfer` (the statement of `P:three-transfer`) for an
  abstract `ThreeMomentModel`, the asymptotic clause only for a supplied
  spectral measure of the low endpoint (none is constructed for product and
  Riesz low endpoints)
  (`RieszPositiveDefinite.three_product_riesz_paper_proved`,
  `three_finite_images_paper_proved`), narrower results.
  Side conditions the TeX leaves
  implicit (a probability measure, integrability, measurability) are
  explicit hypotheses (besides the added hypothesis `hQ` above, one
  hypothesis is not implied by the TeX: the joint
  measurability of the covariance in the general form
  `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper` of `L:terminal-wick`, recorded there as
  an added restriction; the wave-L11 wrappers for the constructed chain
  measures do not take it). Integrability is proved where a statement says so
  (as a conjunct or in a companion theorem); totalized integral identities
  (such as the continuous-`F` Gaussian bridge of `FiniteWick` and the
  `SymplecticFree` cancellation for arbitrary functions) and auxiliary
  bounds do not by themselves guarantee integrability, and extended
  nonnegative integrals (such as the physical pairing of
  `L:spatial-physical-pair`) need not be finite.
- Named inputs of waves L12-L14 (each a `Prop` with a doc comment
  "Supplied input"; true for the manuscript's objects; Lean checks the
  deduction from them, not the inputs; inputs of earlier waves are named in
  their sections). Not discharged in the package:
  `SourceTube.TubeAttained` and `TubeTail` (wave L12; the two conclusions of

  `DiagramModel.MixedMoment` (wave L13; the statement of `P:mixed`, main TeX
  lines 834-849, with the convergence of every diagram as a common noise
  width tends to zero and the finiteness of the limit (the common-width
  reading of the diagram limits of `L:joint-fixed-order`, lines 1853-1966,
  model M4), about random variables standing
  for the solution and its chaos terms, which are not constructed; taken by
  `mixed_moment_paper` and the moment wrappers of `D1Upper`,
  `LowAlphaUpper`, `OrderTwoDiagrams` and `RieszFourDiagrams`);
  `D1Upper.DiagramLimits` (wave L13; the common-width convergence of every
  diagram, the reading of `L:joint-fixed-order` invoked at line 5534, without
  finiteness; proved for white noise in
  `d = 1`, `D1Upper.diagramLimits_white`, not for the Riesz case; implied by
  `MixedMoment`); `LowAlphaUpper.FirstMomentSeries` (wave L13; `X_0 = 1`,
  `u` integrable and `E u = sum_n E X_n`, main TeX line 796 and lines
  5856-5857; taken by the `C:d1-first-calibration` wrappers);

  `integrated_signed_static.tex` lines 16-18, the conclusion of

  potentials, `potOp_signedMultiplierForm`); and
  `EndpointCorollaries.ThreeTransfer` (wave L14; the statement of
  `P:three-transfer`, main TeX lines 7536-7556, for an abstract
  `ThreeMomentModel`). Discharged in the package:
  `EndpointLemmas.RieszProductPD`, `EndpointLemmas.PlaneRieszPD` and
  `EndpointCorollaries.RieszIsoPD` (positive definiteness of the product,
  plane-supported and isotropic Riesz measures; proved in
  `RieszPositiveDefinite`, whose `_proved` wrappers take none of them) and

  `RieszFourDiagrams.rieszDiagramLimit`). `DiagramModel.SpectralSpatial` is a
  true statement recorded in the source and taken by no theorem.
- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures (beyond finitely
  many independent standard Gaussians, `GaussianIBP`, the centered
  Gaussian laws `N(0,A)` on `R^m` of the finite comparison in
  `GaussianComparison` and `SourceTube`, and the finite Wick formula for centered Gaussian
  vectors and finitely many values of a centered Gaussian field in
  `FiniteWick`, and the normalized Hermite polynomials and the finite
  Gaussian Fock layer of `GaussianHermite` and `HermiteFock`, the Gaussian
  comparison of covariance measures and the heat mixtures of `EndpointLemmas`,
  and the Gaussian subordination of Riesz powers in `RieszPositiveDefinite`),
  deterministic two-chain diagram integrals (beyond the model M4 of
  `DiagramModel` and the results stated on it), Fourier analysis (beyond the Gaussian transform of
  `P:masked-spectral-growth`, the auxiliary mask norm of
  `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, the wave-kernel and two-time Laplace
  transforms, the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in
  `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`, `WaveGreenFourier`), of
  Mathlib's sphere measure on `S^2` and Archimedes' law for it
  (`WaveGreenFourier`), the Gaussian spectral representation of `gamma_eps`
  and of the smoothed pairing (`LowAlphaConvolution`), the Gaussian Fourier
  pairing of `PhaseContractions`, the Fourier Fubini step and the polar
  decomposition of the spectral measure of `AlphaOneConvolution`, the
  white-noise spectral measure of `WhiteModel`, the spectral identity of
  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`P:masked-quotient-obstruction`), the
  spectral form of the autocorrelation integral in
  `SpatialFourierBound`, `L:spatial-fourier-bound`, the spectral-mass
  identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` of `SpectralMassIdentity`, the
  Gaussian Fourier multiplier of `DampedMultiplier`, and the spectral
  identification of the smoothed covariance with Fourier uniqueness of
  tempered spectral measures in `DampedSmoothing`, the identification of the
  weak-gradient `H^1` with Mathlib's `H^(1,2)` and its Plancherel norm in
  `H1Mathlib`, the transform of a complexified real-Hilbert-valued map in
  `MaskedAuxiliaryReal`, the white-noise approximate-identity limit of the
  `d = 1` diagrams in `WhiteCollapse`, the spectral form of the covariance
  pairing on tests and the heat multiplier of `SourceHeatGram`, and the
  projection-slice spectral identity of the plane-supported endpoint in
  `EndpointLemmas`),
  infinite-dimensional spectral analysis and operator theory (beyond the
  finite-matrix results of `FiniteGaussianMatrix`, the abstract
  compact-operator facts of `SymplecticFree`, and the diagonal and
  multiplication operators with their functional calculus on the finite
  Fock model of `FockSandwichModel`, complex Lax-Milgram and the bounded
  resolvent of a coercive Hermitian form on `H^1` in `ResolventForm`, the heat
  operator on `H_Gamma` of `SourceHeatGram`, and the `L^2` completions of M5
  in `OccupationCompletion`) and limits in time or in a
  regularization of the equation or its solution are outside Lean; the
  scalar and norm-tail limits stated in their sections are formalized (for
  example the tails `E:damped-tail-norms` and `K_M(r) -> 0` as
  `M -> infinity` in `DampedNormsHomog`, the limit of the decay bound of
  `P:radius-mean-anchor` as `delta -> 0+`, and the abstract `L^2`
  regularization limit `u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` of `L:uniform-series-tail`
  in `UniformSeriesTail`, for an abstract family with the two facts of
  `L:terminal-wick`, which `TerminalWick` proves for nonnegative
  covariance, and its version for the constructed chain measures in
  `TerminalWickInputs`; the Green-regularization limit of the proof of `L:terminal-wick` in
  `TerminalWickRegularization`; the noise-width limit `eps -> 0+` of the
  `d = 1` white diagrams in `WhiteCollapse` and of the order-two Riesz
  diagrams in `RieszFourDiagrams`, deterministic integrals of M4). Where a Lean statement needs an
  analytic fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis
  of the theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
  yet public.
- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
  labeled statement of the revision cited above, or is a Lean-only
  auxiliary or example (such as a non-vacuity instance) with no
  counterpart in the manuscript. Such rows make no claim about the
  manuscript.

Declarations of the step modules live in `StratonovichHAMAudit.<Module>`
(file `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`); those of the library
modules in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.<Module>` (file
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean`). Status is assigned per
`claims.yaml` entry and need not coincide with this ledger's category
"auxiliary to the Lean proof route": helper lemmas have status
`internal` in `claims.yaml` (the four `PositiveGram` declarations and the
helpers of `TemporalEquilibrium`, `RadiusMeanAnchor`,
`MaskedTrigProducts`, `WeakSobolev`, `VariationalDilation`, `IndexedCone`,
`GaussianIBP`, `FiniteGaussianMatrix`,

route auxiliary that a coverage row names, such as
`VariationalRate.rawCost_genuine`, is credited to that row and stays

`H1Density.mollify` is `reusable`).

Totals: 4502 declarations (3653 theorems, 849 definitions); 2263 are listed
against a manuscript label and 2239 have no direct label.

Comparator accounting (since v0.10.0). The comparator checks all 3653
theorems in two configurations. `comparator.json` holds the 1553 theorems
that are the declarations of claims a `coverage.yaml` row names. 1134 of
them were named by the rows at the wave-L13/L14 gate, as reviewed with their
waves (243 of these have a "no direct label" cell or only labels without a
coverage row: the row names them as steps of the result it covers). The
other 419 were credited in v0.10.0 by one rule: to the row of every direct
manuscript label in the label cell of the theorem's section-table row that
has a coverage row (an `outside` row names no claims); this appended 433
claim ids to 52 rows. `comparator-helpers.json` holds the other 2100
theorems, to which neither applies: 1967 whose label cell is "no direct
label", 106 whose label cell names only equation, hypothesis or section
labels without a coverage row of their own, and 27 whose claims lean-pkg
0.29.0 cannot match to a declaration of their file, because its scanner
does not list structure fields or `@[ext]` lemmas (the fields of
`VariationalMeanDerivatives.Good`, `OccupationCompletion.TParams` and
`SpData`, `EndpointLemmas.IsCov`, `EndpointPair` and `ProductParams`,
`ClassOBridge.IsClassO`, and `MaskedAuxiliaryReal.Cx.ext`).
`lean-pkg-signoff.json` declares the helper configuration a smoke check:
its theorems are checked against their restatements in `Challenge.lean`
like the others, but they are credited to no manuscript result. Status in
`claims.yaml` follows: every theorem of the helper configuration is
`internal`.

## ActualEvent (proof steps)

Checks two scalar steps in the lower bound obtained from restarted time
blocks (Section `S:actual-raw-block-lower`). The first is the elementary
error-accumulation estimate for differences of ordered products, used in
the proof of `L:raw-block-restart`; the second is the normalization of the
linear Gaussian penalty in the proof of `P:raw-block-original-lower`.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `L:raw-block-restart` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.ActualEvent.finite_error_accumulation` | If `1 <= C`, `0 <= e`, `d 0 <= 0` and `d (n+1) <= C d n + C^n e` for all `n`, then `d n <= n C^n e`. | The recurrence itself (operator-norm submultiplicativity for the product factors), extension of finite factor lists by identities, moments of `C` and of the error. |
| `P:raw-block-original-lower` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.ActualEvent.moderate_penalty` | For `delta > 0`, `delta (delta^(-1/4) / sqrt delta) = delta^(1/4)`. | The Gaussian change of law, the event on which the penalty bound holds, and the limit `delta -> 0`. |

## AllAlphaMoment (proof steps)

Checks a scalar lower bound for a second moment from a mean identity and a
quadratic bound, together with an exact rational gap. These belong to a
damped lower-endpoint comparison from the development of the manuscript
and are not stated in the revision cited above.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.AllAlphaMoment.moment_lower` | If `a, D > 0`, `x + y = a` and `x^2 <= D y / 2`, then `2 a^2 / (D + 4a) <= y`. | Both relations are supplied hypotheses (normalization of a positive density, integration by parts, Cauchy-Schwarz for its moments). |
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.AllAlphaMoment.rational_gap` | For `a, D > 0`, an exact difference of two rational expressions equals `a^2 / (2 (D+4a)(D+2a)) > 0`. | Any derivative, Gamma-function or integral representation of the compared quantities. |

## ClockFilter (proof steps)

Checks the scalar core of the obstruction to copying the cross-pair time
transform by analytic clocks (Section `S:two-clock-screen`): the partial
fraction identity for the resolvent product, the bound
`0 < 2 theta / (2 theta + ell) < 1`, and the resulting strict integral
inequality `J < K` in `P:clock-copy-obstruction`. The whole proposition is
formalized in the section `ClockCopy` (whole result) below; the cross-pair
and self-pair transforms of `L:white-clock-laplace` are in
`WhiteClockLaplace`.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P:clock-copy-obstruction` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter.resolvent_partial_fraction` | For `theta, ell > 0` and real `r`, the weighted resolvent product `(2 theta + ell)/(2 theta (theta^2 + r^2)((theta+ell)^2 + r^2))` equals the divided difference of `1/(theta^2 + r^2)` and `1/((theta+ell)^2 + r^2)` over `2 theta ell` (equivalently, the bare product has denominator `ell (2 theta + ell)`). | None for this step; the whole proposition is `ClockCopy.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`. |
| `P:clock-copy-obstruction` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter.clock_filter_bounds` | For `theta, ell > 0`, `0 < 2 theta / (2 theta + ell) < 1`. | None beyond the parameter signs. |

## DimensionalMatrix (proof steps)

Defines the backward, coupling and forward 2x2 phase matrices of a single
interaction and computes their product with all four entries retained, in
unweighted coordinates. At fixed frequencies `r`, `rho` the matrices are
the factors of `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` in `E:variance-physical-adjoint` of
`P:actual-wave-form` (`backward` = `S(-t)`, `coupling` = the force
`B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)`, `forward` = `S(t)`, with `cp = cos(rt)`,
`sp/p = sin(rt)/r` and the coefficient `H` in place of `b`), and
`full_interaction` is that unweighted product. It is not yet the normalized
kernel `E:variance-normalized-kernel`: there `b_r = <r> sin(rt)/r`
(`L:masked-continuous-wave`; defined in Lean as `MaskedContinuousWave.bFn`), and passing to it needs the Bessel-weighted
change of coordinates on the phase space `E` together with the weight
`1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)`. That conversion, the Fourier interpretation and the
zero-frequency case (where the manuscript uses the continuous sine quotient)
are outside Lean. The free matrix also appears in the proof of
`L:complex-phase` and, in balanced coordinates, as `W_t` in
`L:symplectic-free`, which also defines the force `B(b)`.

| Paper label | Lean declaration | What it states | Inputs left outside Lean |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.backward` | Definition: `[[cp, -sp/p], [p sp, cp]]`, the backward free matrix `S(-t)` at one frequency. | The interpretation of `cp, sp` as cosine and sine of a phase, and the continuous extension at zero frequency. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.coupling` | Definition: `[[0, 0], [H, 0]]`, the force `B(b)(u, v) = (0, b u)` with `H` for `b`. | The meaning of `H` as a covariance coefficient. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward` | Definition: `[[cq, sq/q], [-q sq, cq]]`, the free matrix `S(t)` at one frequency. | As for `backward`. |
| `P:actual-wave-form` | `StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.full_interaction` | For all real parameters (field division), `backward * coupling * forward = [[-(sp/p) H cq, -(sp/p) H (sq/q)], [cp H cq, cp H (sq/q)]]`, the unweighted product `S(-t) B(b) S(t)` at fixed frequencies. | The Bessel-weighted coordinate change and the weight `1/sqrt(<xi><eta>)` that turn it into `E:variance-normalized-kernel`; Fourier multiplication and covariance integrals; the zero-frequency case. |

## HermiteWord (proof steps)

Checks the combinatorial core of `L:finite-word-cutoff` (exact cutoffs for
finite Gaussian words), which is applied in `P:static-phase-all-orders` and
`L:fixed-split`: if the initial vector has degree zero in every color, each
step raises a degree bound by one in its color and
the projection fixes every vector within the cutoff, inserting the
projection around each step does not change the word. The statements are
abstract (arbitrary types and maps). The companion file
`HermiteWordConsumer.lean` instantiates them with the scalar Hermite
recurrence `x He_n = He_(n+1) + n He_(n-1)` as private worked examples; it
adds no public declarations. The Hermite/Fock realization is proved in
`FockForm` (`goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame`, `truncC_eq`, one
Gaussian coordinate per color) and applied in
`HermiteWordFock.cut_eq_raw_fock` (next section).

## HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)

Applies `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord.cut_eq_raw` (the finite-word
induction of `L:finite-word-cutoff`, `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `39f2597a`, statement lines 3036-3058, display `E:finite-word-cutoff`
lines 3048-3055, proof lines 3060-3076) to the concrete Gaussian Fock model
of `FockForm`. `HermiteWord` predates the module system and is not a
`module`, so a `module` file cannot import it; this audit file is not a
`module` and imports both `StratonovichHAMAudit.HermiteWord` and
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.FockForm`. In this one-mode special case
nothing is supplied: the four hypotheses of `cut_eq_raw` are
`FockForm.goodDeg_vac`, `goodDeg_insert`, `goodDeg_frame` and `truncC_eq`.
The lemma itself is not formalized in full: with `m_i` modes in color `i` the
insertion is `J_i = sum_(j=1)^(m_i) M_(g_ij) (x) K_ij` (lines 3037-3043),
whereas Lean has `J_i = M_(g_i) (x) K_i`; this is a restriction of the
admissible operator data, not an omitted side condition. The multi-mode
lemma, with the cutoff on the total degree of each color and the sentence on
finite sums and integrals of words, is `FiniteWordCutoff` (wave L11, a whole
result over the model choice M2); this section is unchanged.

Model (that of `FockForm` and `HermiteFock`). Coefficient vectors
`(Fin m -> N) -> X` over `m` colors with one standard Gaussian mode per
color (the TeX allows `m_i` modes in color `i`); the insertion of color `i`
is `J_i v = gmul i (K_i v)`, multiplication by `g_i` tensored with a
continuous linear operator `K_i` on `X`; the frames `F_b` act on `X` only;
the cutoff `P = truncC Nc` projects each color onto Hermite degree at most
`N_c`; the start vector is `vac u = 1 (x) u` (the TeX's
`(I (x) F_0)(1 (x) v)` with `u = F_0 v`). A word is a list of
(color, frame) pairs, read as in `HermiteWord` (`raw`, `cut`). The
statement is in normalized Hermite coefficients, where multiplication by
`g_i` is `a_i^* + a_i` (`HermiteFock.coord_smul_iota` identifies this with
multiplication of the Hermite expansion by the coordinate).

Narrower than the TeX: one mode per color; a single finite word (the
sentence on finite sums and Bochner integrals of words, lines 3056-3057, is
not formalized); `X` is a complex inner product space in `Type` (the
universe of `HermiteWord`), with no completeness used, which is more
general than the TeX's Hilbert space.

## InteractionDriver (proof steps)

Checks parameter ranges, exponent bookkeeping and margins used in building
the operator-valued driver (Section `S:actual-operator-driver`). The ranges
and the Holder margin correspond to `E:driver-parameters`,
`L:driver-interval-limit` and `L:driver-holder-limit`; the Lean statements
make one explicit choice (the midpoint between `theta` and `H`) of the
exponent the manuscript only requires to lie in an interval. The
manuscript's `L:driver-holder-limit` lets that exponent be any point of the
interval; `holder_parameters` and `dyadic_ratio` check the midpoint
instance only. The Gaussian mixture and box statements belong to a
preliminary derivation; the Gaussian mixture rows are not stated in the
revision cited above. The box rows are the dimension-two case of a step of
`P:radius-mean-anchor`: its proof divides `Q(1-a) > 2d` by `2Q` to get
`e_anchor = (1-a)/2 - d/Q > 0` and combines `g_delta` with the radius
power. With `d = 2` and the Lean parameter `p` taken as the manuscript's
even moment exponent `Q` (not its averaging exponent `p`), `box_margin` is
that margin and `box_scale` that power bookkeeping. The general margin and
the proposition for abstract random paths are formalized in the section
`RadiusMeanAnchor` (a narrower result) below; these two rows remain as dimension-two instances.

## PhaseResponse (proof steps)

Checks the choice of a phase index and its strict margins, two
trigonometric identities, and a two-sided frequency window, for a first
Gaussian response computed in a physical phase norm in the development of
the manuscript. These are not stated in the revision cited above, with one
exception: `two_frequency_average` is the real form of the cosine-cosine
case of the expansion in the proof of `L:masked-trig-products`, which
writes the product of two trigonometric factors as four complex exponential
modes with frequencies `+-r +- rho` and coefficients of absolute value
`1/4`; pairing conjugate modes gives the Lean identity with `x = r t`,
`y = rho t`. The complex form, the sine cases and the Hilbert-space bound
are formalized in the section `MaskedTrigProducts` (whole result) below.

| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.PhaseResponse.balanced_phase` | For `alpha + a < 2`, the two margins `2s + alpha + a < 3` and `alpha + a - 3 < -1` hold at `s = 1/2`. | As above. |
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.PhaseResponse.energy_boundary` | `2 + alpha + a < 3` iff `alpha + a < 1`. | None. |
| no direct label | `StratonovichHAMAudit.PhaseResponse.four_component_gram` | A sum of four products of sines and cosines equals `cos(r1-r2) cos(k1-k2)`. | The temporal covariance integrals. |
| `L:masked-trig-products` (cosine-cosine case, real form) | `StratonovichHAMAudit.PhaseResponse.two_frequency_average` | `cos x cos y = (cos(x-y) + cos(x+y))/2`. | None for this identity; the full lemma is `MaskedTrigProducts.masked_trig_products_paper`. |

## AlphaOneConvolution (whole result)

Registered model choice: M1 (the `d = 3` wave Green measure via `volume.toSphere`; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

`L:alpha-one-convolution` (Degree-one convolution bound) of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/AlphaOneConvolution.lean`: statement lines
5635-5643 (display `E:alpha-one-convolution`, lines 5638-5641), proof lines
5645-5708 (display `E:alpha-one-polar`, lines 5674-5681), with the standing
assumptions of the subsection (lines 5552-5563: `H:homog`, `d` in {1,2,3}, `mu`
the spectral measure in the convention `gamma(x) = int e^(i xi . x) mu(dxi)`,
`V = mu{norm(xi) <= 1}`, `G_h` the wave Green measure,
`G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h`, `G_{h,0} = G_h`).

Objects. `gamma_eps = Gamma * p_eps` is `VariationalDilation.conv Gamma
(VariationalMean.heatK eps)` (a Bochner integral; `p_eps` has covariance
`eps I` and multiplier `e^(-eps norm(xi)^2/2)`, the TeX's Brownian convention,
line 5671), definitionally `LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps Gamma eps`
(`conv_heatK_eq_gammaEps`). `G_h = WaveGreen.waveGreen d h`;
`G_{h,eta} = LowAlphaConvolution.smoothedGreen (waveGreen d) h eta =
DampedMultiplier.gaussKernel eta * G_h` (`N(0, eta I)`); this module defines no
Gaussian law or smoothed Green measure of its own (wave L10-A1i removed the
local duplicates `gaussLaw` and `smoothedGreen`). `G_h hat = WaveKernel.waveHat
h` (the function `sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, value `h` at `0`). `I_a(h,v)` is
`Ia a h v`; `g_h`, `p_(2a)^(1)` and `g_h * p_(2a)^(1)` are `gBox h`, `gauss1 a`
and `boxConv a h`. The angular measure `sigma` (line 5657) is
`sphereMeasure mu`, realized as a measure on `R^d` concentrated on the unit
sphere, not on the sphere subtype (a representation choice; the integral over
`S^(d-1)` in `E:alpha-one-polar` is the integral against this measure).

Formalized (nothing supplied). (i) `polar_decomposition` (lines 5653-5665):
for locally finite `mu` with `mu(cA) = c mu(A)` (`SpectralHomogeneous mu 1`):
`mu{0} = 0`, `V < infinity`, `sigma` has mass `V` and is concentrated on the
sphere, and `mu = (theta, r) -> r theta` of `sigma (x) dr|_(0,infinity)`
(uniqueness on rectangles, as in the TeX); `sphereMeasure_apply` (the defining
formula), `sphereMeasure_even`, and `alpha_one_polar_decomposition_paper`
(under `H:homog` with `alpha = 1`, including the evenness of `sigma`). (ii)
`alpha_one_radial` (lines 5682-5683, 5691-5703): absolute convergence of the
radial integral, `I_a(h,v) = pi (g_h * p_(2a)^(1))(v)` and
`0 <= I_a(h,v) <= pi/2` for `a > 0`, `h >= 0`. (iii) `alpha_one_polar`: the
spectral side of `E:alpha-one-polar`,
`int waveHat h xi e^(-a norm(xi)^2) cos(xi . z) mu(dxi) = int I_a(h, theta . z)
sigma(dtheta)`, with both integrability statements and the bound `pi V/2`.

On named inputs. (iv) `alpha_one_convolution` (general form),
`alpha_one_convolution_paper` (`H:homog` with `alpha = 1`; no `Gamma != 0`, as
in the TeX) and `alpha_one_convolution_one` (`d = 1`, the Fourier identity
discharged by `waveGreenFourier_one`): `V < infinity`, and for `h > 0`,
`eps > 0`, `eta >= 0`, `z`, with `a = (eps+eta)/2`: integrability of
`y -> gamma_eps(y + z)` against `G_{h,eta}`, absolute convergence of the
radial integrals, `sigma`-integrability of `theta -> I_a(h, theta . z)`,
`E:alpha-one-polar` and `E:alpha-one-convolution`. The two named inputs are
`SpectralPairing Gamma mu` (the Fourier Fubini representation of the pairing
with the integrability of its integrand, lines 5610-5612, used at line 5673;
it contains no Fourier transform of `G_h` and no homogeneity) and
`WaveGreenFourier d` (`G_s hat = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, lines 5614-5618).
Both are discharged in `L10Completed` (`spectralPairing_holds` from
`LowAlphaConvolution.smoothed_pairing_spectral`, `waveGreenFourier_holds` from
`WaveGreenFourier.waveGreen_fourier`); they stay hypotheses here so that this
module does not depend on `WaveGreenFourier`.

Hypotheses made explicit. The general form assumes `mu` locally finite and
tempered and `mu(cA) = c mu(A)`; in the wrapper the homogeneity comes from
`H:homog` by `MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog` (the TeX:
"Fourier uniqueness, applied to the distributional homogeneity", line 5653).
In the lemma's statements (the general form and the wrappers) and in
`alpha_one_radial`, integrability of the integrals is part of the
conclusion; the route identities such as `conv_heatK_eq` are definitional
identities of Bochner integrals and assert no integrability. `V < infinity`
is proved before `V.toReal` is used.

Differences from the TeX (route; statements unchanged). (ii) uses
`sin(hr)/r = (1/2) int_(-h)^h cos(ru) du`, Fubini and the Gaussian cosine
integral (from Mathlib's `fourierIntegral_gaussian`) instead of Fourier
inversion of `g_h hat p_(2a) hat`; in (iv) the passage from `e^(i xi . z)` to
`cos(xi . z)` takes the real part of an identity with real left side instead
of using the evenness of `sigma` (lines 5683-5685; the evenness is proved
separately and not used); the Gaussian factor of `G_{h,eta}` comes from
Mathlib's `charFun_conv` and `charFun_stdGaussian`
(`charFun_smoothedGreen`). The sector-mass step (lines 5659-5660) is the route
lemma `cone_measure`. `Ia_neg_h` and `boxConv_zero_ge` are not TeX steps (used
by the refutations).

Narrower than the TeX: nothing. Not stated: the commentary sentences "No
isotropy or angular density is required" (line 5642) and lines 5704-5706 on
the oscillation (they are reflected in the absence of such hypotheses). The
route definition `nrm` (`xi -> xi/norm(xi)`) has no row. Route-only helpers
are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Refutations (`refutations/alpha-one-convolution/`), classified; none relies on
a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: `FactorTwoSphereMass`
(`sigma(S^(d-1)) = 2V` is false; witness: Lebesgue measure on `R`, the
spectral measure of the white model, `alpha = d = 1`) and
`WrongRadialConstant` (the radial bound with `pi/8` in place of `pi/2` fails
at `a = 1/4`, `h = 1`, `v = 0`). Control outside the manuscript domain:
`DroppedPositiveH` (`I_a(h,v) >= 0` fails at `h = -1`; the lemma assumes
`h > 0`).

## ClassOBridge (narrower results: `P:occupation-physical-class` and `P:raw-occupation-energy` whole over the class `O` itself; `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` with the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral form, their identification not formalized; `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` without the `C_2` sentence and `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket`, its energy comparison only, for `S_2^pos` in place of `C_2`, the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral form; in the zero-covariance case `C_2 = 0`, the vanishing of `S_c^pos` and of the original means, `Q = 0` and the reduction to the free moment model not formalized)

Wave L14 item O (part 2), in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ClassOBridge.lean`:
the class `O` of strongly `H^1`-measurable fields, its bridge to the joint
representatives used since wave L7 (debt D3), the results that range over
`O` re-issued on the class itself, and their zero-covariance cases (debt B9).
Anchors at `39f2597a`: `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (the class
`O`, lines 497-500; `P:occupation-physical-class`, statement lines 503-521,
proof lines 523-575, the joint representatives constructed in lines 534-540;
the zero-covariance remark, lines 577-582) and
`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` (`E:raw-occupation-definitions`,
lines 4-21; `P:raw-occupation-energy`, statement lines 111-131, proof lines
133-177; `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection`, statement lines 180-188, proof
lines 190-236; `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling`, statement lines 249-264,
proof lines 266-316; `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket`, statement lines 319-333,
proof lines 335-371; the direct zero case, lines 379-385).

The class and the bridge (nothing supplied). `IsClassO u`: `u : R -> H^1`
with `H^1 = ClassOH1.H1R d` (registered model choice M6, accepted by the author on 2026-11-13),
a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure on `(0,1)`, `\|g_s\|_2 = 1` at
a.e. time and `T(g) < infinity`. "Strongly `H^1`-measurable" is read as
a.e.-strongly measurable (Bochner), the reading of the TeX's own proof ("use a
separably valued strong representative", line 534); the topology of `H1R d`
is Mathlib's `H^1` topology (`ClassOH1.isEmbedding_toMH1`). `exists_joint`
constructs a strongly measurable joint representative of an a.e.-strongly
measurable `L^2`-valued field (lines 534-540), `exists_aesm_of_joint` gives the
converse, and so `O` corresponds to the earlier model
`OccupationPhysicalClass.IsOccField` up to versions at a.e. time in both
directions (`isOccField_of_classO`, `classO_of_isOccField`). Every functional
unchanged by such changes takes the same values on both (`values_eq`), so the
value sets and suprema over `O` (`energySetO`, `EstarClassO`; `ratioSetO`,
`CoccO`; `rawEnergySetO`, `EOO`) equal the joint-representative ones of the
earlier modules (`*_eq`).

1. `P:occupation-physical-class` (`occupation_physical_class_whole_paper`):
   with the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: `H:homog` with
   `a = alpha0`, `Gamma != 0`, `D = q - 2a`), every conclusion on `O` itself,
   nothing supplied: measurability and representative independence of the
   pairings `B_Gamma(g_s^2, g_t^2)` (the physical integrals),
   `E:occupation-physical-bound` with `J(g) < infinity`, and
   `E:occupation-own-energy` with `0 < E_sp` and the energy set nonempty and
   bounded above. A whole result.
2. `P:raw-occupation-energy` (`raw_occupation_energy_whole_paper`): with the
   section's standing assumptions (`H:homog` with `a = alpha0`, `Gamma !=
   0`), every conclusion on `O` itself, nothing supplied: `0 < C_occ <= K_0
   R_sp` (`R_sp = R_0` finite by `ClassOH1.spatial_four_linear_whole_paper`),
   `E:raw-occupation-energy`, `E:raw-occupation-ratio`, `E_zeta^O > 0` (a
   finite real supremum of a set bounded above) and `E_zeta^O =
   zeta^(-alpha/(2-alpha)) E_1^O`, together with the proof's facts
   `0 < T(g)`, `E:raw-occupation-bound` and the dilation `U_l` on `O` (stated
   up to versions: some `u'` in `O` with `g'_s = U_l g_s` a.e.) with
   `A(U_l g) = l^alpha A(g)`, `T(U_l g) = l^2 T(g)`. A whole result.
3. `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` (`occupation_rayleigh_selection_whole_paper`):
   `g_eps` in `O` itself, nothing supplied, with `I_Psi` built from `lambda`
   the square root of the real Rayleigh supremum `E:variational-real-rayleigh`
   and `v_Psi` the integral-form cost; their identification with
   `sqrt(-E_s)` and `E W(Psi)^2` (the operator half of
   `P:variational-unmasked-rate` and the stochastic variance) is not
   formalized, so the result stays narrower (the class-`O` clause is gone).
4. `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (`intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_classO_paper`):
   both forms of `E:occupation-score-ceiling` with `C_occ` and `E_zeta^O`
   over `O` itself, nothing supplied; narrower: the moment sentence
   `C_2(Gamma,a) <= U_2` (line 261) needs `T:intrinsic-second-moment`, and
   `I_Psi`, `v_Psi` are as in 3.
5. `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` (`intrinsic_spatial_comparison_classO_paper`):
   the comparison `S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O)` with
   `E_(1/2)^O` over `O` itself; narrower: `S_2^pos` in place of `C_2(Gamma,a)`
   (`T:intrinsic-second-moment`); the bracket `E:intrinsic-spatial-bracket`
   itself is `SpatialBracket.intrinsic_spatial_bracket_paper` and the
   `L8Completed` wrappers.
6. The zero-covariance cases (no label: the remark after
   `P:occupation-physical-class`, lines 577-582, and the direct zero case,
   lines 379-385), `zero_covariance_paper`: under `H:homog` with `Gamma = 0`,
   every physical pairing vanishes, `R_sp = 0`, `E_sp = 0`, `J = A = 0` on
   `O`, `E_star^O = C_occ = E_zeta^O = 0` with nonempty value sets (small
   dilations of one fixed unit compact profile, constant in time; no
   zero-gradient unit state is used), `F_b(0) = 0` (computed), and the ceiling
   `U_c` and its `E_zeta^O` form are both `0`. Not formalized: `C_2 = 0`, the
   vanishing of the original means and of the variational values `S_c^pos`
   (line 379; `C_2` needs `T:intrinsic-second-moment`), `Q = 0` (line 380)
   and the reduction of the moment model to the free case (lines 581-582).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Nothing is supplied. Carried and
unused: in `zero_covariance_paper` only `alpha < 2` of `H:homog` is used; the
other wrappers use all their hypotheses. `T(g)` and the energies are extended
integrals; the finiteness of `T(g)` is part of membership in `O`
(`IsClassO.energy_lt_top`), and its integral representation and the
finiteness of `J` and `A` are concluded; every `sSup` is used with
nonemptiness and boundedness proved. The time measure is Lebesgue measure on
`(0,1)` (finite, `isFiniteMeasure_volI`). The pairings and the dilation are
stated on the spatial versions `gO u` (representatives of the `L^2` classes),
which the TeX's representative independence makes harmless. Proof route: the
wrappers transfer the joint-representative results of
`SpatialOccupationL7Completed`, `RawOccupationEnergy` and
`OccupationCeilingExact` through the bridge and representative independence
(`sqPair_Jlin_congr`, `Tlin_congr`, `Araw_congr`). Measurability of the
pairings is by Tonelli on the joint representative, not by the continuity of
the pairing map on `H^1 x H^1`; the field is first normalized to `F/max(1,
\|F\|)` and its bounded simple approximations are shown Cauchy in `L^2((0,1)
x R^d)`, instead of the TeX's summable `L^2(0,1; H^1)` errors. The witness of
item 3 is the finite-cell field of `OccupationCeilingExact` moved into `O`
(`classO_of_isOccField`), not the TeX's countable first-index selection.
Registered model choice: M6 (accepted by the author on 2026-11-13; see Scope). Junk values: `sSup` of a
set not bounded above is `0` in Lean; no statement relies on it for `zeta >
0` (refutation `ZetaZeroJunk`).

Refutations (`refutations/class-o-bridge/`, wave L14 item O), classified.
Manuscript-domain perturbation: `ZeroCovarianceEnergy` (`0 < E_star^O`
without `Gamma != 0`; fails for the white model with amplitude `c = 0`, a
model of `H:homog` with `d = alpha = 1`, `a = 1/2`, whose covariance is zero).
Control outside the manuscript's parameter class (the penalty `zeta = 0`,
outside `zeta > 0` of `integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` line 16), a
counterexample to extending the boundedness to zero penalty:
`ZetaZeroUnbounded` (the value set of `E_zeta^O` is bounded above at
`zeta = 0` instead of `zeta > 0`; fails for the white model with `c = 1`,
`a = 1/2`, by dilation). Control of Lean's totalized arithmetic outside the
manuscript domain: `ZetaZeroJunk` (`0 < E_0^O`; Lean's `sSup` of the unbounded
set at `zeta = 0` is `0`). Lean-route control: `EmbeddingTwoPi` (for
`ClassOH1`, see that section).

## ClassOH1 (whole result)

Wave L14 item O (part 1), in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ClassOH1.lean`: the
real Sobolev space `H^1(R^d; R)` as a topological space, and
`P:spatial-four-linear` with every conclusion. Anchors at `39f2597a`:
`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (`P:spatial-four-linear`, statement
lines 297-315, proof lines 317-398; the joint-continuity sentence lines
307-308, proof lines 374-376; the graph description of `H^1`, lines 356-358)
and `notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` (`L:occupation-raw-square`,
lines 24-43, continuity of `Q` in lines 26 and 64-66).

The space (registered model choice M6, accepted by the author on 2026-11-13). `H1R d` is the graph
`{(f, grad f)}` of the weak gradient (`WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient`) inside
`L^2(R^d; R) x L^2(R^d; R^d)` (Mathlib's `Lp` classes), with the subspace
topology and metric of the product: the TeX's own description of `H^1` in the
proof of `P:spatial-four-linear` ("its closed isometric image `f -> (f, grad
f)` in `L^2(R^d)^(d+1)`", lines 356-358). Its topology is proved to be that of
Mathlib's Bessel-potential space `H^1(R^d)` of wave L13 item K5a
(`H1Mathlib`): `toMH1 p = H1Mathlib.toH1` satisfies `\|toMH1 p - toMH1 q\|^2 =
\|f_p - f_q\|_2^2 + (2 pi)^(-2) \|g_p - g_q\|_2^2` (`norm_toMH1_sub_sq`), is
`2`-Lipschitz and `7`-antilipschitz, hence a uniform embedding
(`isEmbedding_toMH1`, `topology_eq_induced`). Not proved: that every
real-valued element of Mathlib's `H^1(R^d)` comes from `H1R d` (surjectivity
of `toMH1` onto real elements), which no statement here needs. Every `H^1` pair
`(f, g)` of the earlier modules has a class `ofPair` in `H1R d` with a.e.-equal
representatives.

1. `P:spatial-four-linear` (`spatial_four_linear_whole_paper`): with the
   section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: `H:homog` with `a = alpha0`,
   `Gamma != 0`), every conclusion, nothing supplied: the conclusions of
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed.spatial_four_linear_paper_completed` for `H^1`
   pairs (`E:spatial-homogeneous-bound`; finiteness and
   `E:spatial-square-CS`; `E:spatial-four-linear` with absolute convergence;
   the sequential form of joint continuity, kept as a conjunct; `R_sp = R_0`;
   `A_sp(f) > 0` for nonzero `f`), together with the topological joint
   continuity of `C_4` on `(H^1)^4` with the product topology
   (`continuous_C4`) and the continuity of the square pairings, hence of
   `A_sp`, on `(H^1)^2` (`continuous_sqPair_toReal`), for `H^1 = H1R d`. The
   density of test functions in `H^1` is proved (`H1Density`), so
   `SquareBound Gamma alpha R_0` holds with nothing supplied
   (`SpatialFourLinear.squareBound_R0`).
2. A step row of `L:occupation-raw-square` (a narrower result of
   `OccupationCompletion`, wave L14 item K1a): `Q : H^1 -> H_sp` is
   continuous on `H1R d` for its topology (`continuous_Q`,
   `occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper`, under `H:homog` and
   `Gamma != 0`); K1a proved only the sequential form.

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. Nothing is supplied and no hypothesis
is carried unused. The topology on `(H^1)^4` is the product topology.
Continuity is deduced from the sequential continuity of
`SpatialFourLinear.C4_tendsto` (telescoping, as in the TeX) because `H1R d` is
a metric space; the TeX's step `N(f) <= \|f\|_(H^1)` is replaced by the
continuity of `N` along `H^1` convergence. The multilinearity of `C_4` (proof
line 373) is not restated (the statement does not list it). Registered model
choices: M6 (accepted by the author on 2026-11-13; see Scope) and, for the two
`Q` rows (`continuous_Q`, `occupation_raw_square_continuous_paper`), M5 (the
codomain `H_sp` is `OccupationCompletion.Hsp`). Junk values: none relied on.

Refutations: one file for this module, in `refutations/class-o-bridge/`
(wave L14 item O): `EmbeddingTwoPi` (`toMH1` is an isometry for the
manuscript norm `\|f\|_2^2 + \|grad f\|_2^2`; fails for the `d = 1` test function
`cutoff 0`, where Mathlib's norm weights the gradient by `(2 pi)^(-2)`), a
Lean-route control (b): it concerns Mathlib's `2 pi` convention of the
embedding used for the topology, about which the TeX makes no claim.

## ClockCopy (whole result)

Formalizes `P:clock-copy-obstruction`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, lines
9033-9207) in full, with its displays `E:cross-clock-lambda-weight`,
`E:clock-copy-obstruction` and `E:degree-one-clock-loss`, together with the
finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 1010-1154) and
`N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`. The module `ClockCopy` rests on four foundation
modules of the D4 layer (Fourier and Laplace analysis of the wave kernel
and the time kernel), whose rows are marked "[D4 foundation: <Module>]":
`WaveKernel` (`G_s hat` as `waveHat s xi = s sinc(s|xi|)`, which is
`sin(s|xi|)/|xi|` with value `s` at `0`; its bounds, scaling and Laplace
transform), `TimeFractional` (subordination
`r^(-a) = Gamma(a)^(-1) int l^(a-1) e^(-r l) dl`, the kernel `Psi_a` of
`E:averaged-clock-kernel` and its properties, and the two-time Laplace
lemma `int int e^(-as-bt-lam|s-t|) = (a+b+2lam)/((a+b)(a+lam)(b+lam))` for
complex `a, b` with positive real part), `SpectralHomog` (consequences of
the spectral homogeneity, `R_Gamma`, `h_Gamma`, and `Gamma != 0 => mu != 0`)
and `DampedNorms` (`N_1`, `N_2^2` of `E:damped-norm-definitions` and their
finiteness). `H:homog` is `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` with temporal
exponent `a = alpha0`; the wrappers `clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
`damped_norms_finite_paper` and `damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the results
with the manuscript's hypotheses (`Gamma != 0`, `theta > 0`,
`-1 <= rho <= 1` for the proposition; `Gamma != 0` is not assumed for the
lemma). These wrappers take ONE further input as an argument:
`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`, `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for Borel `A` and
`c > 0`, which the TeX derives from the scaling of `Gamma` and Fourier
uniqueness in the proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lines 1067-1068; the
same derivation is in the proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines
5582-5593). This input is now derived under `H:homog` by
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and
`ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper` and
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper` state the three results with
nothing supplied (see "MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)"); the
statements of this section are unchanged. Its consequences
`mu{0} = 0`, `mu(B_r) = r^alpha mu(B_1)`, `int (1+|xi|^2)^(-1) dmu < inf`
(by the layer-cake formula), and the homogeneity of `R_Gamma` and `h_Gamma`
are proved; Lebesgue measure on `R^1` satisfies the input (see
`refutations/clock-copy/WrongDegreeOneConstant.lean`). Implicit hypotheses
made explicit: integrals over `(0,inf)` and `(0,inf)^2` are Bochner
integrals for Lebesgue measure (`TimeFractional.L0`, `TimeFractional.P2`).
Since the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, every integral
the paper asserts to be finite (`w_theta`, the `N_1` and `N_2` integrands,
the outer integrand of `N_2^2`, the `J` integrands and `2 theta/(2 theta +
l) w_theta`) comes with a proved integrability conclusion; the auxiliary
scaling identities `SpectralHomog.integral_comp_smul` (measurable `f` only)
and `ClockCopy.integral_rpow_div_add_scaling` (`c > 0` only, any `a`) are
identities of Lean's totalized integrals with no integrability conclusion,
and are used only where integrability is proved separately
(`ClockCopy.integrable_rpow_div_add` needs `0 < a < 1`). `G_s hat` is real,
so the complex conjugate in `N_2` is dropped. `Psi_a(theta|u-v|, .)` and
`|s-t|^(-a)` take Lean's junk values on the diagonal, a null set (the TeX
notes the diagonal is irrelevant). Hypotheses carried but unused: in
`clock_copy_obstruction_paper`, `rho >= -1` and the fields `dim`,
`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`
and the `Gamma` scaling of `HomogCovariance` (the latter replaced by the
supplied input); in `damped_norms_finite_paper`, the fields `dim`,
`Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`,
`mu_tempered`, `spectral`, the `Gamma` scaling and `alpha_range`; in
`damped_N2_nonneg_paper`, the fields `dim`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`,
`Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and
the `Gamma` scaling. The `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers use `mu_tempered`,
`spectral` and the `Gamma` scaling to derive the input. The proof route differs from the TeX, though the
statements do not. On the `K` side Lean does not smooth the covariance and
pass to a monotone limit: it expands `|s-t|^(-a)` by subordination and
applies Fubini on `(0,inf) x R^d x (0,inf)^2`, justified by an absolute
majorant built from `|G_s hat G_t hat| <= 2(1+s)(1+t)/(1+|xi|^2)`. This is
a different route, not the one after "Alternatively" in the TeX (lines
9116-9118), which bounds the density `w_theta` by homogeneity; Lean's
proof that `w_theta` is integrable (`weight_integrable`) does use bounds of
that shape, `C l^(a-1)` near zero (from `resolvent_sub_le`) and
`C l^(a-2)` at infinity, but derives them without homogeneity. The time
integral of the first display of the proof is the complex two-time lemma
at `theta -+ i|xi|`, and needs `mu{0} = 0`. On the `J` side the `(w,q)` substitution and the
resolvent identity are replaced by the real two-time lemma at
`c = (theta^2+|xi|^2)/2` and rate `theta l + l^2/2`, and `J_rho` is
dominated by `J_1` (the TeX's majorant through `Psi_a <= r^(-a)` and the
homogeneity of `h_Gamma` is not needed). For `alpha = 1` only the scaling
`int l^(a-1)/(c+l) dl = c^(a-1) int l^(a-1)/(1+l) dl` is used, not the
Beta value. Partial fractions and the strict inequality reuse
`StratonovichHAMAudit.ClockFilter`. Not formalized in this section: `N_0`,
the scaling identities of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, the tails
`E:damped-tail-norms` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (all in
the section `DampedNormsHomog`, `N_0` with the mass identity
`G_s(R^d) = s` supplied), the identity
`Psi_a(r,v) = E (r+iZ)^(-a)`, the probabilistic interpretation of the
clocks and of `h_Gamma` as a heat average, and the remark
`R:clock-copy-scope`. The full wrapper hypotheses with `Gamma != 0` are
not instantiated in Lean (the audit examples use the zero witness of
`HomogCovariance`); the general theorems are instantiated at Lebesgue
measure on `R^1`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the
Lean proof route)"; the definitions `L0`, `P2`, `subKernel`, `psiKernel`,
`twoTimeC`, `twoTimeR`, `FK`, `MK` and `FJ` only name integrands and
measures and have no rows.
