## HigherRieszTwo (narrower result: `L:higher-riesz` in `d = 2` only, with the steps shared with `d = 3`; the `d = 3` clause and the whole lemma are in `HigherRieszThree`; `H:spatial-maximum` for a covariance with a density)

Registered model choice: M1 (the `d = 3` wave Green measure via `volume.toSphere`; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope), used only in the steps shared with `d = 3`.

`L:higher-riesz` (Riesz spatial maxima) of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/HigherRieszTwo.lean`: the dimension-two clause in
full and the proof steps shared with dimension three (statement lines
6103-6112, proof lines 6114-6190), and Hypothesis `H:spatial-maximum` (lines
5919-5929, display `E:higher-convolution` at lines 5922-5925) with the
section's notation (lines 5912-5917). The dimension-three clause and the whole
lemma are in `HigherRieszThree` (its own section), which reuses these steps
unchanged.

Objects. `gamma(x) = c norm(x)^(-alpha)` is `riesz c alpha`, an
`[0, infinity]`-valued function (value `0` at `x = 0` for `alpha > 0`,
Lean's `0^(-alpha) = 0`; the point is null for every measure `gamma` is
integrated against: Lebesgue measure, the absolutely continuous `G_h^(1)` and
`G_h^(2)`, and the atomless sphere measure `G_h^(3)` (M1; the scaling
`G_h(hA) = h G_1(A)` carries the null singleton)).
`gamma_eps = p_eps * gamma` is `smoothCov g eps` and `G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h`
(`G_{h,0} = G_h`) is `smoothGreen nu eta`, both through lower Lebesgue
integrals, with `p_eps = VariationalMean.heatK eps` (covariance `eps I`, line
5915); `pairing` is `int G_{h,eta}(dy) gamma_eps(y + z)`. `G_h` is
`WaveGreen.waveGreen d h`. `M_2` is `M2 c alpha`; `F3 v rho` is the closed form
`((1+rho)^v - abs(1-rho)^v)/(2 v rho)` of lines 6136-6138 as a function of
`v = 2 - alpha` and `rho = norm(w)` (value `0` at `rho = 0`, never used).

`H:spatial-maximum` is `SpatialMaximum d g delta M`: `M > 0` and
`int G_{h,eta}(dy) gamma_eps(y + z) <= M h^(-delta)` for every `h > 0`, `z`,
`eps > 0`, `eta >= 0`, for `G_h = waveGreen d h` and a covariance with density
`g`. NARROWER than the TeX's hypothesis in one respect: the TeX's `gamma` is
the covariance of `H:homog` (in general a measure, lines 5554-5557); here it
must have a density. This is no narrowing of `L:higher-riesz`, whose
covariance `c norm(x)^(-alpha) dx` has a density. The lower bound `0 <=` of
`E:higher-convolution` is automatic for the lower integral, and the upper bound
forces finiteness; `SpatialMaximum.real_form` gives the display as written
(real-valued, with integrability) for a measurable density. `smoothGreen` and
`smoothCov` are defined independently of `LowAlphaConvolution.smoothedGreen`,
`LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps` and `VariationalDilation.conv` (same objects
mathematically; no bridge lemma is stated).

Formalized, nothing supplied. Step (a) `ball_mass_two`
(`G_1^(2)(B(w,R)) <= 2R^(3/2)` for every `w`, `0 < R <= 1/4`); step (b)
`layer_cake_le` (for any measure of mass at most one with that ball bound) and
`F2_le` (`F_2(w) <= M_2/c`, uniform in `w`); step (c) `unsmoothed_scaling`
(`int G_h(dy) gamma(y + z) = c h^(1-alpha) F_d(z/h)`, `d = 1, 2, 3`); step (d)
`average_le` and `smoothed_average_le` (a bound uniform in the shift passes to
both Gaussian widths, any `d`, any s-finite measure); `riesz_two_unsmoothed`,
`M2_pos`, `higher_riesz_two` (the dimension-two clause for `0 < alpha < 3/2`)
and its wrapper `higher_riesz_two_paper` (`H:homog` for
`Gamma = volume.withDensity (riesz c alpha)` in `d = 2`, `c > 0`,
`1 < alpha < 3/2`); step (e) `F3_max` (for `1 < alpha < 2` the closed form is
maximal at `rho = 1` with value `2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)`); step (f)
`approx_identity` (for `norm(y)^(-lambda)` on `R^j`, `0 < lambda < j`,
`x != 0`: each `p_eps * f(x)` is a genuine integral and tends to `f(x)`).

Hypotheses. `higher_riesz_two_paper` carries `H:homog` unused, and of
`1 < alpha` it uses only `0 < alpha` (`higher_riesz_two` states the clause for
`0 < alpha < 3/2`). `H:homog` contains `alpha0 + alpha < 2`, the section's
`alpha < 2 - alpha0` (lines 5912-5913).

Differences from the TeX (route; statements unchanged). (a) A reflection
instead of a rotation; for centers `norm(w) < 1/2` the density bound `1/pi`
(mass `<= R^2`) instead of `2/(pi sqrt 7)` (mass `<= 2R^2/sqrt 7`), both
`<= 2R^(3/2)` (`ball_mass_small`, a route lemma); the slice integral by its
closed form. (b) The layer cake in the level `t` instead of the radius
`R = t^(-1/alpha)`. (d) Two successive Tonelli averages instead of
`p_eps * p_eta = p_{eps+eta}` (the display of lines 6173-6176 is not stated).
(e) A chord bound (convexity of `(1+rho)^v - (1-rho)^v` on `[0,1]`,
subadditivity of `t^v` for `rho >= 1`); the TeX's monotonicity of `F_3` on
each side of `rho = 1` is not stated, only the maximum. (f) A split at
`norm(y) = 2 norm(x)` and Mathlib's peak-function theorem instead of the TeX's
three regions.

Not in this module: the identity `F_3(w) = F3 (2-alpha) norm(w)`, the
dimension-three clause and the optimality of `M_3` (all in
`HigherRieszThree`); `P:higher-transfer` and `C:higher-riesz`, which use
`H:spatial-maximum`, are not formalized. Route-only helpers are "no direct
label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)"; the route definitions `dens2`,
`e0` and `coordSwap` have no rows.

Refutations (`refutations/higher-riesz-two/`), classified; none relies on a
junk value of Lean's totalized arithmetic. Manuscript-domain perturbations
(wrong statements inside the lemma's hypotheses): `MaxAtZero` (the maximum
of the closed form is not its limiting value `1` at `rho -> 0`; `alpha = 3/2`) and
`WrongMaxValue` (the value `2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)` without its factor `1/2`
is wrong at `alpha = 3/2`). Controls outside the manuscript domain (they show
that a hypothesis is needed, with a witness that violates it):
`DroppedAlphaRange` (`M_2 > 0` fails at `alpha = 2`) and `DroppedCPositive`
(`M_2 > 0` fails at `c = 0`). Lean-route-only control: `DroppedVLessOne`
(the chord bound of the route lemma `F3_num_le` needs `v < 1`).

## HomogHypothesis (whole result)

States Hypothesis `H:homog` (main TeX file, Section `S:model`) in full as
the predicate `HomogCovariance`, and restates `E:kappa` and
`E:driver-parameters` under it. The manuscript's Fourier convention
`Gamma = int e^(i xi.x) mu(d xi)` is written out explicitly rather than
through Mathlib's Fourier transform. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on
`R^d` a locally finite Borel measure is a Radon measure. The proofs of the
two restated results use only the numerical part of the hypothesis.

## IndexedCone (narrower result: abstract ground family; identification with the physical wave family not formalized)

Formalizes `L:raw-block-indexed-cone` (`notes/integrated_raw_block_lower.tex`
at `39f2597a`, lines 316-455) with its display
`E:raw-block-positive-product`: for `0 < rho < 1/2` there are an integer
`B >= 1` and `omega, eps_op > 0`, and `c_* = a_* j_*/4 > 0`, such that the
product lower bound holds for every `N >= 1`, every `omega`-adjacent chain in
`I = [0,1]` and every operator family `eps_op`-close to the block flows. The
whole conclusion is proved, including the exact constant
`c_* = a_* j_*/4`. The lemma uses the ground family of
`S:compact-mean-family` (`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex`, the
C16 results), which is not formalized; its outputs are supplied as ONE
hypothesis structure `GroundFamily F` over an arbitrary real normed space
`F`, with these fields (TeX lines at `39f2597a`):

- `P`, `e`, `ell`, `lam`: the flows `P_sigma(t)` (line 17,
  `E:compact-F-block`), the growing vectors `e_sigma` and duals
  `ell_sigma` (`E:compact-F-projection`, lines 343-345) and the rates
  `lambda_sigma` (`P:compact-ground-family`, line 48); `e0` and `obs` are
  the data `e_0` and the bounded observable `O_phi`
  (`S:actual-raw-block-lower`, lines 16-17); `d0` is the gap `d_0` (`E:compact-rate-gap`).
- `lam_pos`: `lambda_sigma > 0` on `I`, a weakening of
  `sqrt(eps) <= lambda_sigma` in `E:compact-rate-gap` (line 51).
- `ell_e`, `P_Pi`, `Pi_P`: `ell_sigma(e_sigma) = 1` and
  `P_sigma(t) Pi_sigma = Pi_sigma P_sigma(t) = e^(lambda_sigma t) Pi_sigma`
  for `t >= 0`, exactly `E:compact-F-eigen` (lines 350-354), with
  `Pi_sigma = e_sigma ell_sigma`.
- `d0_pos`, `normalized_complement`: `d_0 > 0` and, for every
  `0 < eta < d_0`, a `C` with
  `||e^(-lambda_sigma t) P_sigma(t) Q_sigma|| <= C e^(-eta t)` for all
  `sigma` in `I` and `t >= 0`, exactly `E:compact-normalized-complement`
  (`P:compact-F-complement`, lines 443-447). `d_0` is abstract: its
  identification with `inf_I(lambda_sigma - mu_sigma)` is not needed.
- `e_cont`, `ell_cont`: norm continuity of `sigma -> e_sigma` and
  `sigma -> ell_sigma` on `I` (`P:compact-F-projection`, lines 348-349).
  Continuity and uniform boundedness of `Pi_sigma`, and boundedness of
  `e`, `ell`, are derived (`Pi_bounded_continuous`), not assumed.
- `margin_ell`, `margin_obs`: `0 < inf_I ell_sigma(e_0)` and
  `0 < inf_I O_phi(e_sigma)`, exactly `E:compact-positive-margins`
  (lines 356-359).

Every field is a displayed conclusion of `P:compact-ground-family`,
`P:compact-F-projection` or `P:compact-F-complement`, or a weakening of one,
so the structure is no stronger than C16. `scalarFamily` shows it is
satisfiable. The proof is the TeX cone induction (entrance, rebase, full
block, terminal) with the TeX's order of constant choices.
`ConeConstants` records constants satisfying relaxed, sufficient versions
of the TeX's inequalities (lines 350-377): the margins `a`, `j` are any
positive lower bounds of `ell_sigma(e_0)` and `O_phi(e_sigma)` on `I` (not
necessarily the infima `a_*`, `j_*`), `C_gap`, `eta_gap`, `nu` need only be
`>= 0` (the TeX takes `C_gap >= 1`, `eta_gap > 0`, `nu > 0`), and `M_e`,
`M_ell`, `M_P`, `H` are any nonnegative bounds (the TeX takes
`max(1, sup)`). `positive_product_of_constants` proves the product bound
for any such constants, with `c_* = a j/4`, and `exists_coneConstants`
constructs them with the TeX's choices where needed (`C_gap >= 1`,
`eta_gap = d_0/2`, positive `nu`) and with `a = a_*` and `j = j_*`; the
starred constants in the final result come from this specialization. Side conditions made explicit: the TeX fixes
`E_0 = ||e_0|| = 1`, whereas Lean allows any `||e_0||` (a generalization);
the families are `D : N -> R -> (F ->L F)` with closeness required only for
`m <= N` and `u` in `[0, B]`, and nothing else is assumed, as TeX line 333
says. The product `D_N(u) D_(N-1)(B)...D_0(B) e_0` is
`D N u (chainState D B e0 N)`. The wrapper `indexed_cone_paper` carries
the section's standing hypotheses (a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying `H:homog`,
lines 4-9) unused: the lemma depends on `Gamma` only through the ground
family, and C16 itself (the spectral theory of `-Delta - V_sigma`, the wave
phase space and its projections) is not formalized, so the link of `G` to
`Gamma` is by documentation only.

## IntervalScalar (proof steps of `C:static-interaction` and `P:interval-coefficients`, inputs supplied; `E:static-block-series` in full)

Formalizes the deterministic scalar, combinatorial and Hilbert-space steps of
two results of `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`:
`C:static-interaction` (statement lines 3216-3262, proof 3264-3341) and
`P:interval-coefficients` (statement lines 4054-4066, proof 4068-4271). Both
results are operator and stochastic statements; every row below is a step row
(class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement), except
`E:static-block-series`, which is a scalar statement and is proved in full with
nothing supplied (`static_block_series_paper`). The operator and stochastic
inputs enter as named hypotheses; the last column names each one with its
manuscript label.

`C:static-interaction`. `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` is modelled by an arbitrary
complete real inner product space `E`, and the transported phases
`Y_n = S_0(-h) Z_n^eps(h)` by a sequence `Y : N -> E`; the expectation of an
inner product is the inner product of `E`. This is faithful because the proof
of `E:static-interaction` (lines 3264-3311) uses only the Hilbert structure:
the order bounds of lines 3287-3292, the Gaussian parity of line 3293, and
the two first-variance bounds of lines 3275-3280. Those are the supplied
hypotheses `hY0`, `hY`, `hodd`, `hborn`, `hmean`. The identification of
`I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g)` with `sum sigma^n Y_n` (lines 3218-3223) is not
formalized here; wave L11 proves it, derives the order bounds `hY` from the
primitive inputs of `P:static-phase-all-orders` and `L:complex-phase`, and
proves the per-block step from a per-block bound on adapted phases (section
StaticInteractionCompleted). Lean proves that `sum sigma^n Y_n` converges and the bound
`(1 + E(h, sigma, lambda)) N^2`. `L_alpha`, `B_alpha`, `x` and `E` are the
definitions `staticL`, `staticB`, `staticX`, `staticE`, word for word; `A`
stands for `A_alpha` and may be any constant `>= 0`. The section's constants
are `R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` and `D_Gamma` of
`E:phase-constants` (lines 2494-2501), for locally finite `mu`, `Gamma` on
`R^3` and `0 < alpha < 2`. These are the only clauses of the TeX's covariance
class (line 2490) in the wrappers. Evenness, positive definiteness and scaling
enter only through the supplied hypotheses. `R_alpha >= 0` and `D_Gamma >= 0`
are derived (`ralpha_nonneg`, `dgamma_nonneg`). The `_step` and
`static_block_series` forms take them as hypotheses. The TeX argues with the
absolutely convergent double series; Lean bounds the partial sums, regrouped
by `r + s = 2k` (`square_sum_eq`), keeps the first coefficient signed, and
passes to the limit. For `E:independent-static-blocks`, Lean proves the scalar
iteration and `1 + y <= e^y`. The per-block bound
`m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E) m_j` is supplied (lines 3332-3338: it uses
`E:static-interaction`, `\|S_0(h_j)\|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j)`, density and
tensoring with the independent past). The operators `M_j(h_j)` and their
`L^2` extensions are not formalized. Hypotheses carried but unused: `0 < alpha`
in `static_interaction_step`; `0 < alpha` in `static_block_series` (its
`0 < alpha0` is used: with `alpha + alpha0 < 2` it gives `alpha < 2`); local finiteness of `mu`, `Gamma` (it only makes the
ball masses finite, so that `toReal` is not a junk value); `lambda h_j <= 1` in
`independent_static_blocks_paper`.

`P:interval-coefficients`. The energy coefficient `[s^(2k)] E\|U(T;s)v\|^2`,
the split inner products `Q_(r,q)` and `\|v\|_(1/T)^2` are real numbers `coef`,
`Q p`, `V`. Colors are `j : Fin M` with the TeX's sorted label `i = j + 1`.
Supplied hypotheses:
- `hsplits`: `E:interval-energy-splits` combined with the reflection parity
  (lines 4147-4157).
- `hfixed`: `L:fixed-split` (`E:fixed-split-bound`; lemma lines 3675-3716) at
  `lambda = k/T`. Its per-color factor is `splitFactor`, with `l_i` as
  `splitEll`. In wave L10, `FixedSplitCore.split_explicit_constant_paper`
  derives `hfixed` (with `C_split = 100^8 e^8 max{1, 12 delta^(-2)}`) from the
  before-absorption bound `E:split-before-absorption`, and
  `FixedSplit.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_fixed` discharges it on the
  Fock model, with the inputs of `L:fixed-split` supplied and an added bound
  `hQ` of `Q p` by the cutoff inner product (accepted for now, 2026-11-12;
  sections FixedSplitCore and FixedSplit); in wave L11
  `FiniteWordCutoff.interval_coefficient_assembly_paper_words` removes `hQ`,
  with `Q p` the real part of the inner product of the uncut coefficients and
  their Duhamel word expansion `DuhamelWords` supplied (section
  FiniteWordCutoff).
- `hinv`: `L:inventory-product` as the proposition `InventoryProduct alpha
  alpha0 C_inv` (lines 3581-3593). Proved in `InventoryProduct`
  (`inventory_product`) and discharged in `IntervalScalarCompleted`, whose
  `*_completed` forms do not take it. Lean formalizes the rest of the assembly
  (lines 4176-4228): the length substitution `h_i <= L T/i` at `lambda = k/T`,
  `sigma_i^2 <= c h_i^(-alpha0)` (`singleton_weight_le`, `cross_weight_le`,
  `higher_weight_le`); the split count `2l + 1 <= 3^l`; `k^2 <= 4^k`; the
  coefficient-of-a-product identity (`kvector_sum_eq_coeff`); and the
  reduction `L -> max(1, L)`, `c -> max(c, 0)` (lines 4079-4082). Together
  these give the explicit constant `C = 12 max(c,0) max(1,L)^beta C_split
  C_inv`. The paper wrapper assumes `R_alpha > 0` and `sigma_i > 0`, the
  hypotheses of `L:fixed-split`, so that `hfixed` is literally that lemma.
  Neither is used in the proof. The TeX's zero-noise case and the sign
  reduction `(sigma_i, W_i) -> (|sigma_i|, sgn(sigma_i) W_i)` (lines 4079,
  4082-4085) change the Gaussian fields and are not formalized, so the
  conclusion is narrower there. Positive lengths `h_i > 0` are explicit (the
  TeX writes `h_i^(-alpha0)`). The identification of the coefficients with the
  finite-interval model is not formalized here: the exact preservation of the
  selected coefficients by the cutoff (lines 4163-4170) is proved in
  `FiniteWordCutoff` (`coef_cutoff_eq`, wave L11) from the supplied Duhamel
  word expansion `DuhamelWords`; the paragraph "Identification and summation"
  (lines 4239-4256) is not formalized. For `E:interval-phase-bound` (lines 4257-4269), Lean proves
  summability of the coefficient series and the bound `e exp(nu C^(1/nu)
  R_alpha^(1/nu) T^(beta/nu)) V`, the TeX's display with its absorbed constant
  `nu C^(1/nu)`, from four supplied hypotheses:
- the power-series identity at `s = 1`;
- vanishing odd coefficients;
- the zero-order bound `e V`;
- the coefficient bound.
Both wrappers state the section's class as `H:homog`
(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, line 384; the section's standing
class at lines 3364-3369 is that of `H:homog`), from which `0 < alpha < 2`,
`0 < alpha0 < 1` and `alpha + alpha0 < 2` are derived (`homog_alpha_range`);
the other clauses are carried and not used.

Junk values: in the manuscript-facing bounds every real power has a positive
base, or is `(k!)^nu`, or is `i^q` with `i >= 1` (or a nonnegative base with a
positive exponent where monotonicity is used), and every denominator satisfies
the stated positivity conditions. The unrestricted definitions (`invV`, `invB`,
`invCoeff`) and the bridge identities of `IntervalScalarCompleted` (stated for
all `k, i`) also include Lean's totalized zero-index values, which no bound
uses. `R_alpha` and `D_Gamma` use `ENNReal.toReal` of ball
masses, finite under local finiteness. Summability is proved, never assumed
through `tsum`.

## IntervalScalarCompleted (narrower result: positive-noise scalar coefficient assembly of `P:interval-coefficients`; identification with the interval evolution and the zero and sign reduction not formalized; analytic inputs supplied)

`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` (at `39f2597a`), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/IntervalScalarCompleted.lean`. It discharges the
one cross-item input of `IntervalScalar`: the hypothesis `hinv :

not assumed:

- `invV_eq`, `invB_eq`, `invCoeff_eq`: the coefficient functions agree
  (`invV = vCoef`, `invB = bCoef`, `invCoeff = factorCoeff`); `InventoryProduct`

  `TypeContinuity.nuOf`.

  used by `IntervalScalar` is `InventoryProduct.inventoryProduct`, the product
  over `i in Finset.Icc 1 M`.

  hypotheses of `inventory_product`), `IntervalScalar.InventoryProduct alpha

No other `IntervalScalar` theorem takes `hinv`. What remains supplied is
unchanged: `hsplits` (`E:interval-energy-splits` with the reflection parity,

does once `C_split = C_split(alpha)` is supplied.

## InventoryProduct (whole result)

Formalizes `L:inventory-product` (A coefficient bound for a product with
nonnegative coefficients; `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`,
main file, at `39f2597a`: statement lines 3581-3593 with
`E:inventory-product` at lines 3589-3592, proof lines 3595-3661) in full.
Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The exponents are those fixed by the
section `S:interval-upper` (line 3354) at lines 3361-3362: `nu = 3 - alpha`
(`TypeContinuity.nuOf`), `beta = 4 - alpha - alpha0`
(`TypeContinuity.betaOf`) and `p = 2 - alpha0` (`pOf`). The object is the
actual coefficient: `v_i` and `b_{i,l}` (lines 3584-3586) are `vCoef` and
`bCoef` word for word, the `i`th factor `1 + v_i z + sum_{l>=2} b_{i,l} z^l`
is the Mathlib formal power series `factorSeries` (`PowerSeries.mk`), the
product over `i = 1, ..., M` is `inventoryProduct` (a product over
`Finset.Icc 1 M`), and `[z^k]` is `PowerSeries.coeff k`. The TeX's "finite
`C = C(alpha, alpha0)`, independent of `M, k`" is the explicit real
`inventoryConst alpha alpha0 = 4 e^(K(alpha, alpha0))` (`K = expConst`),
which is fixed before `M` and `k` are quantified and depends on nothing else
(not on `d`, `Gamma`, `mu`). `inventory_product` is the general form: for `0
< alpha0 < 1` and `alpha0 + alpha < 2` (any real `alpha`), every `M` and
every `k >= 1`, `[z^k] prod_{i=1}^M (...) <= C^k/(k!)^nu`.
`inventory_product_paper` states it under the section's standing hypothesis
`H:homog` (lines 384-401; `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0
Gamma mu`) and adds `0 < C`. Only the fields `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`
and `threshold` are used (through `params`: `nu >= 1`, `nu <= beta`, `beta >
2`, `p > 1`, `nu + alpha - 2 = 1`); the other fields of `H:homog` are
carried and not used. The TeX's `k >= 1` is a hypothesis of every theorem
that needs it; `M` ranges over all naturals (`M = 0` gives the empty
product). Implicit facts made explicit: the evaluation bound `[z^k]F <=
F(z)/z^k` (`coeff_prod_le_prod_tsum`) carries the summability of each factor
at `z` as a hypothesis, and `inventory_product_eval_le` proves that
summability at `z = theta k^nu`, `theta = 1/4`; the tail sums `sum_{i>a}
i^(-s) <= a^(1-s)/(s-1)` (`sum_rpow_tail_le`, by Mathlib's sum-integral
comparison) and `sum_{i>=1} i^(-s) <= s/(s-1)` (`sum_rpow_pos_le`), used in
the TeX without proof, are proved. Proof-route differences (the statement is
unchanged): the factors `1 + Q_i`, `Q_i = theta k i^(-p)`, are bounded by
`e^(Q_i)` with `sum_i Q_i <= theta k p/(p-1)`, instead of the TeX's
comparison with `int_0^inf log(1 + A x^(-p)) dx`, which gives `C k^(1/p)`
(lines 3608-3617); both give the `C k` the proof needs, and no improper
integral is used. The uniform bound `sum_{l>=2} P^l (1+ly)^2/(l!)^nu <= C
P^2 (1+y^2)` for `0 <= P <= 1/4`, `y >= 0` (lines 3650-3651, stated without
argument) is proved inside `factor_large` with `C = 128`, via `(1+ly)^2 <= 2
l^2 (1+y^2)`, `l^2 <= 2^(l+1)` and `(l!)^nu >= 1`; for `i <= k`
(`factor_small`) Lean assumes the singleton is at most `4P` where the TeX
says `2P_i`, which is weaker and suffices for the `S_nu(4P_i)` bound.
`S_nu(x) <= e^(nu x^(1/nu))` is `SeriesType.seriesNu_summable_le`. Every
factor bound is first proved for each partial sum (`factor_partial_le`) and
then passed to the series sum. Junk values: all real powers have positive
bases (`i >= 1`, `k >= 1`, `l! >= 1`) and `k^(-1)` occurs only with `k >= 1`
in every evaluation and coefficient bound (the unrestricted definitions and
`factorCoeff_nonneg` also cover zero indices with Lean's conventions, used by
no bound), and every `tsum` (`factorEval`) comes with its summability, so
no junk value enters a conclusion. Nothing in the lemma is left
unformalized, and no conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. The use of the
lemma in the proof of `P:interval-coefficients` (lines 4214, 4227) is not
part of this section (see `IntervalScalar`; `IntervalScalarCompleted`
connects `inventory_product` to the input `hinv` of that proof).

## L10Completed (whole result)

Registered model choice: M1 (the `d = 3` wave Green measure via `volume.toSphere`; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

Integration module of wave L10 for `AlphaOneConvolution` with wave L9's
`LowAlphaConvolution` and `WaveGreenFourier`, in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/L10Completed.lean`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, line numbers at
`39f2597a`). It discharges the two named inputs of
`AlphaOneConvolution.alpha_one_convolution_paper` (`L:alpha-one-convolution`,
statement lines 5635-5643, proof lines 5645-5708) and re-issues the general
form and the wrapper without them (each proof one line). The general form
keeps the hypotheses on `mu` and states the bridge assumptions (`d` in
{1,2,3}, `Gamma` tempered, `IsSpectralMeasure`) under which the two inputs are
discharged; the paper wrapper has `H:homog` alone. It defines no new object
and changes no source module.

1. `AlphaOneConvolution.SpectralPairing Gamma mu` (the Fourier Fubini
   representation of `int G_{h,eta}(dy) gamma_eps(y + z)` with the
   integrability of its integrand, lines 5610-5612, used at line 5673):
   `spectralPairing_holds`, for tempered `Gamma`, `mu` with
   `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu` (`mu` s-finite), in every dimension, from
   `LowAlphaConvolution.smoothed_pairing_spectral` applied to the finite
   measure `G_{h,eta}`; `gamma_eps` of `AlphaOneConvolution` is
   definitionally `LowAlphaConvolution.gammaEps`.
2. `AlphaOneConvolution.WaveGreenFourier d`
   (`int e^(i xi . y) G_s(dy) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)` for `s > 0`, lines
   5614-5618): `waveGreenFourier_holds`, for `d` in {1,2,3}, the second
   conjunct of `WaveGreenFourier.waveGreen_fourier` (wave L9-G).

`alpha_one_convolution_completed` (general form, `d` in {1,2,3}) and
`alpha_one_convolution_paper_completed` (under `H:homog` with `alpha = 1`
alone; no `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX) have the conclusions of the source
statements. After this module `L:alpha-one-convolution` rests on its standing
assumptions alone. Fields of `H:homog` used by
`alpha_one_convolution_paper_completed`: `dim`, `mu_radon`, `mu_tempered`,
`Gamma_tempered`, `spectral`, `scaling` (the last through
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`); carried, unused:
`alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_posdef`,
`mu_even`, `threshold`, `alpha_range` (as recorded in the module). Every
reading recorded in `AlphaOneConvolution` is unchanged; in particular the
`d = 3` Green measure is the `toSphere` definitional choice of `WaveGreen`
(Le's decision 4 of wave L6), not identified with surface measure, and
`sigma` is a measure on `R^d` concentrated on the unit sphere.
`HigherRieszTwo` and `HigherRieszThree` are not involved (they have no
supplied inputs).

Refutations (`refutations/l10-completed/`), classified; none relies on a junk
value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: `QuarterBound` (the bound `pi V/4` in
place of `pi V/2` fails for Lebesgue measure on `R`, `a = 1/4`, `h = 1`,
`z = 0`) and `StrictPositivity` (strict positivity of the pairing fails for
`Gamma = mu = 0`, which satisfies `H:homog` with `alpha = 1` in `d = 2`; the
lemma has no `Gamma != 0`). Control outside the manuscript domain:
`NegativeH` (nonnegativity of the angular integral
`int I_a(h, theta . z) sigma(dtheta)` fails at `h = -1`, a control outside the
domain `h > 0`).

## LowAlphaConvolution (whole result)

Registered model choice: M1 (the `d = 3` wave Green measure via `volume.toSphere`; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

`L:low-alpha-convolution` (Low-`alpha` convolution bound) of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/LowAlphaConvolution.lean`: statement at lines
5566-5580 (displays `E:low-alpha-radial`, lines 5568-5572, and
`E:low-alpha-convolution`, lines 5574-5578), proof at lines 5582-5631, standing
assumptions of the subsection at lines 5554-5563 (`H:homog` with
`d in {1,2,3}`, the lemma taking `0 < alpha < 1`).

Objects (TeX notation of lines 5558-5561). `V = mu({norm(xi) <= 1})` is
`specV mu` (the closed unit ball, as in the TeX; `SpectralMassIdentity.ralpha`
uses the open ball for `R_alpha`, a different constant).
`min{h, norm(xi)^(-1)}` is `lowKernel h`, with value `h` at `xi = 0`, not
Lean's `min h 0^(-1) = 0`. `p_eps` is the centered Gaussian density with
covariance `eps I` (`heatDens eps`; the TeX fixes this normalization at lines
5346-5348 and 5915-5916, not inside the lemma), `gamma_eps = p_eps * Gamma` is
`gammaEps Gamma eps` (a Bochner integral against the measure `Gamma`; not
`PhaseContractions.gammaEps`, which is `p_(2eps) * Gamma`, the `Gamma_eps` of
`S:static-phase`; each module follows its section's notation), and
`G_{h,eta} = p_eta * G_h` is `smoothedGreen G h eta = gaussKernel eta * G h`
(`DampedMultiplier.gaussKernel eta = N(0, eta I)`); for `eta = 0` it is `G_h`
(`smoothedGreen_zero`), so the TeX's convention `G_{h,0} = G_h` is a theorem.
`G_h` is `WaveGreen.waveGreen d h` in the wrappers (the `d = 3` sphere measure
being the `toSphere` definitional choice of `WaveGreen`, Le's decision 4) and
any family `G` in the general theorem.

Formalized. `measure_closedBall_eq` (first display of `E:low-alpha-radial`,
from `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)`); `integral_lowKernel` (`V < infinity`,
integrability and the layer-cake identity, as in the TeX); the Fourier Fubini
step that the TeX invokes at lines 5610-5612 without displaying it
(`gammaEps_spectral`, an identity of Lean integrals under the bare predicate
`IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu` with no integrability conclusion; and
`smoothed_pairing_spectral` for every finite measure `G`, under tempered
`Gamma`, `mu`, with the integrability of both integrands and of
`p_eps(x - .)` against `Gamma` as conclusions; `smoothedGreen_pairing_spectral`
for `G_{h,eta}` under `GreenFourier`); `gammaEps_nonneg` and
`abs_waveHat_le_lowKernel` (the bounds of lines 5621-5627); and the whole lemma
`low_alpha_convolution`, for every `d` and every family `G` with
`GreenFourier G`: `E:low-alpha-radial` and, for all `eps > 0`, `eta >= 0`, `z`,
the integrability of `y -> gamma_eps(y + z)` against `G_{h,eta}` and
`E:low-alpha-convolution`. The uniformity of line 5579 is the order of
quantifiers (the bound does not depend on `eps`, `eta`, `z`).

Wrappers. `low_alpha_convolution_paper`: under `H:homog`
(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, `d in {1,2,3}`, no `Gamma != 0`),
`alpha < 1` (so `0 < alpha`, returned as the first conjunct) and the supplied
`GreenFourier (waveGreen d)`. `low_alpha_convolution_one`: the same in `d = 1`
with nothing supplied (`DampedMultiplier.greenFourier_one`). After wave L9 the
input is discharged in every dimension by
`L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed` (section `L9Completed`),
with `WaveGreenFourier.greenFourier`.

Supplied input (one, discharged in `L9Completed`): `GreenFourier (waveGreen d)`
(`G_h` finite and `charFun (G_h) = waveHat h`, i.e.
`G_h hat(xi) = sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi)` with value `h` at `0`, for `h > 0`).
It is exactly the identity the TeX imports from the source at lines 5612-5618,
with the finiteness of `G_h` that the same display states
(`G_h(R^d) = h`); it is no stronger than the TeX's input.

Hypotheses made explicit. The general theorem assumes `Gamma` and `mu`
tempered, `mu` locally finite, `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu` and
`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha` (from `H:homog` by
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Integrability is proved
where the principal statements use it: `integrable_heatDens` (the inner
integrand `p_eps(x - .)` against tempered `Gamma`, `eps > 0`),
`smoothed_pairing_spectral` (both integrands, as conjuncts), and the wrappers
`low_alpha_convolution`, `low_alpha_convolution_paper`,
`low_alpha_convolution_one` and
`L9Completed.low_alpha_convolution_paper_completed` (every integral of their
conclusions). The auxiliary `gammaEps_spectral` (an equality of Lean integrals
under `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu` alone) and `gammaEps_nonneg` (nonnegativity
for any `Gamma`) have no integrability conclusion; `V < infinity` is proved,
so `V.toReal` is not junk; `1 - alpha > 0`. Fields of `H:homog` used by the
wrappers (directly or through `spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, as recorded in
the module): `mu_radon`, `mu_tempered`, `Gamma_tempered`, `spectral`,
`scaling`, `alpha_range`; carried, unused: `dim` (used only by the `L9Completed`
wrapper, to discharge the input), `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`,
`Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `threshold`.

Differences from the TeX (route). `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` by
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog` (TeX lines 5590-5593); `mu{0} = 0` (lines
5594-5595) is not needed, since `lowKernel h` has the value `h` at `0` and its
level sets are closed balls. Integrability of `e^(-eps norm(xi)^2/2)` against
`mu` comes from temperedness (TeX: polynomial ball growth, line 5610).
`gamma_eps >= 0` because `Gamma` is a positive measure and `p_eps >= 0` (the
TeX argues by distributional nonnegativity, lines 5626-5627; the covariance of
`H:homog` is a measure). The upper bound follows the TeX (lines 5618-5624) via
`smoothed_pairing_spectral`, `DampedMultiplier.charFun_gaussKernel_conv` and
`WaveKernel.abs_waveHat_le_min`.

Narrower than the TeX: none for the lemma's displays. Not stated: the
commentary sentences "This computation uses ball masses, not a radial density"
(lines 5604-5605) and "No positivity of the oscillatory Fourier integrand is
asserted" (lines 5629-5630). Route-only helpers are "no direct label
(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

## LowAlphaUpper (narrower results: `P:low-alpha-upper` and `C:d1-first-calibration` with the coefficient bounds proved on the diagram model at every noise width and the calibration constants in full; the displays for `A_k(t)` in the TeX's form, `E u^2` and `E u` only for random variables satisfying `MixedMoment` (and `FirstMomentSeries` for `E u`): the solution and its chaos terms are not constructed; the conditional rate clause for an abstract first-moment function)

Wave L13 item D3, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/LowAlphaUpper.lean`. Two
labelled results of the main TeX file
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, under the standing assumptions
of lines 5552-5563 (`H:homog`, `d in {1,2,3}`, `0 < alpha <= 1`, `mu` the
spectral measure, `V = mu{\|xi\| <= 1}`), the parameters `b, q, beta, Z` of
`E:d1-constants` (lines 5323-5332) and `0 < alpha_0 < 1` (line 5315):

1. `P:low-alpha-upper` (statement lines 5711-5734: `E:low-alpha-constants` at
   5714-5724, `E:low-alpha-coefficient` at 5727-5733; proof lines 5736-5807).
   On the model, nothing supplied: the first display of
   `E:low-alpha-coefficient` for the regularized coefficients at every noise
   width `eps > 0` and the factorial step (`low_alpha_upper_paper`, from
   `spatialMax_gen`, `coeffA_eps_le`, `coeff_factorial_le`). With the named input
   `MixedMoment`: the first display for `A_k(t) = sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)]` and
   `E u^2 <= exp(C_dir^gen t^kappa)` (`low_alpha_upper_moment_paper`, via
   `coeffALim_le` and `secondMoment_le`).
2. `C:d1-first-calibration` (statement lines 5830-5842, `E:d1-first-calibration`
   at 5834-5838; proof lines 5844-5864). Constants with nothing supplied:
   `C_(1,*) = C_(2,*)/2^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha))` (`C1_eq`) and `2C_(1,*) < C_(2,*)` in
   the nonzero cases (`two_C1_lt_C2`). With the named inputs `MixedMoment` and
   `FirstMomentSeries`: `E X_(2k)` bounded as in the proof and
   `E u <= exp(C_(1,*) t^kappa)`, for the three cases of `K_*`
   (`first_calibration_paper` for `K_sp^gen`; `first_calibration_riesz_paper`
   and `first_calibration_white_paper` for `K_sp` under `E:d1-covariances`, from
   `D1Spatial`). The conditional clause ("conditionally on a first-moment lower
   rate at least `L_*`, `2L_* <= 2C_(1,*)`") is `lower_rate_le`, for an abstract
   function in place of `t -> E u(t,x)`, with "lower rate at least `L`" read as
   "for every `L' < L`, eventually `E u(t) >= exp(L' t^kappa)`"; it is not
   combined with the wrappers. "Consistently with `P:Jensen`" is commentary and
   not stated.

Model (registered model choice M4, `DiagramModel`): `A_k(t)` is
`coeffALim d Gamma alpha_0 k t`, the sum of the diagram limits as the common
noise width `eps -> 0+`; at fixed width it is `coeffA (waveGreen d) (covEps
Gamma eps) alpha_0 k t` (the TeX's "regularized moments", line 5779); through
`MixedMoment.coeffA_eq` it is `sum_m E[X_m X_(2k-m)]`. The Green kernels are the
unsmoothed wave Green measures `waveGreen d h` in every dimension, the `d = 3`
one being the registered model choice M1; the TeX's auxiliary Green smoothing
`G_(h,eta)`, `eta > 0`, in `d = 3` and its limit `eta -> 0+` (lines 5746-5747,
5785-5802) are not needed: `L:low-alpha-convolution` and
`L:alpha-one-convolution` are applied at `eta = 0` (`G_(h,0) = G_h`,
`LowAlphaConvolution.smoothedGreen_zero`). `K_sp^gen` is `Kgen alpha V` with
`V = (specV mu).toReal`, `C_dir^gen` is `C2`, `C_(1,*)` is `C1`, `kappa` is `kappa`.
The spatial step (lines 5747-5769) is proved in `d = 1, 2, 3` from the two
convolution lemmas (`closing_le`, `spatial_le_closing`, `spatialMax_low`,
`spatialMax_one`, `spatialMax_gen`; the predicate `SpatialMax` is proved in
every case, never assumed); the temporal step is `TwoSimplexTime`.

Named inputs. `DiagramModel.MixedMoment d alpha_0 Gamma P X u t` (the statement
of `P:mixed`, main TeX lines 834-849; see `DiagramModel`): it supplies the
existence of the diagram limits (the TeX's limit paragraph, lines 5785-5802,
and `L:joint-fixed-order`), `E[X_m X_n]` as the sum of the diagram limits and
`E u^2 = sum_k A_k(t)`; TRUE for the solution under `H:homog`, not proved.
`FirstMomentSeries P X u` (defined here): `X_0 = 1`, `u` integrable and
`E u = sum_n E X_n` (main TeX line 796 and lines 5856-5857); TRUE for the
solution and its chaos terms (`L^2` convergence of the chaos series implies
`L^1` convergence), not proved. The solution `u` and its chaos terms `X_n` are
not constructed (blocker D5): every display about them is narrower by the split
modelled-object rule. Registered model choices used: M4 and M1 (`d = 3`).

Hypotheses and differences from the TeX. The `P:low-alpha-upper` wrappers take
`H:homog` (`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha_0 Gamma mu`), `alpha <= 1`, `V > 0`
and `t > 0`; fields used: `dim`, `mu_radon`, `mu_tempered`, `Gamma_tempered`,
`spectral`, `scaling`, `Gamma_even`, `alpha_range`, `alpha0_lt_one`; carried,
unused: `V > 0` (the bounds hold for `V >= 0`; it is used only for
`2C_(1,*) < C_(2,*)` in the corollary), `alpha0_pos`, `Gamma_radon`,
`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`, `threshold`; `t > 0` is used only as `t >= 0`. The
corollary's Riesz and white wrappers carry `0 < alpha_0` unused. The TeX's
"standing covariance positivity assumptions" (a covariance that may be a
distribution) are modelled, as everywhere in the package, by a positive
measure `Gamma` with `H:homog`. `E:low-alpha-coefficient` is proved for
`A_k(t)` given the existence of the diagram limits (`coeffALim_le` takes it as
a hypothesis; the wrapper gets it from `MixedMoment`); the TeX proves the limits
by `L:joint-fixed-order` and the `eta`-limit paragraph, which are not
formalized. The second inequality of `E:low-alpha-coefficient` is proved as a
scalar inequality and is stated for the TeX's `A_k(t)` only through the first.
The module header of the Lean file names a lemma `oneChainLim_le` that does not
exist (the one-chain limit is inside `firstMoment_le`). Status `internal` marks
the Lean-route helpers.

Refutations (`refutations/low-alpha-upper/`), classified: `FactorialExponent`
(`coeff_factorial_le` with `(k!)^(b+2)`, false at `b = 1`, `k = 3`, `x = 1`),
`HalfConstant` (`C_(1,*) = C_(2,*)/2`, false at `alpha = 1`, `alpha_0 = 1/2`,
`K = 1` by `two_C1_lt_C2`) and `OneChainBound` (`TwoSimplexTime.sum_incr_le` with
the one-chain bound `t` for two chains, false at `m = n = 1`, `t = 1`,
`s = (3/4, 3/4)`): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript domain;
`SubunitExponent` (`TwoSimplexTime.sum_div_factorial_rpow_le` for `q = 1/2`, false
at `z = 1`, `n = 2`): (c) a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript
domain (there `q = 3 - alpha >= 2`). None relies on a junk value.

## MaskedAuxiliaryNorm (narrower result: `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` for complex `H` only; the real-`H` clause is proved in `MaskedAuxiliaryReal`)

Formalizes `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` (Auxiliary mask norm) of
`S:masked-covariance` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at
`39f2597a`: statement lines 106-118 with the displays
`E:masked-auxiliary-growth` (lines 108-110) and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier`
(lines 113-116), proof lines 120-180), together with the setup of lines 96-103
(`zeta_R`, `k_R`, `L`, and `E:masked-auxiliary-measure` at lines 100-103).
Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.

Conventions. The section's unitary Fourier transform (lines 10-14),
`f-hat(xi) = c_d int e^(-i xi.x) f(x) dx` with `c_d = (2 pi)^(-d/2)`, is
defined directly as `paperHat` (for `f` with values in any complex normed
space; the integral is a Bochner integral over Lebesgue measure on
`R^d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)`), with `cd` the constant. It is not Mathlib's
`𝓕` (kernel `e^(-2 pi i <v,w>)`); `paperHat_eq_fourier` relates the two
(`f-hat(xi) = c_d 𝓕 f(xi/(2 pi))`), and `paper_inversion` is Fourier inversion
in the paper's convention. For a Schwartz map the defining integrand is
integrable (`integrable_paperHat_integrand`), so the transforms in the
statements are not junk values. `zetaR`, `kR` and `Lz` are the manuscript's
`zeta_R(x) = zeta(x/R)`, `k_R = zeta_R-hat` and `L = norm(zeta-hat)_1`; `zeta`
is a real Schwartz map (`SchwartzMap (Rd d) R`), and `zeta_R F` is
`x -> (zeta_R(x) : C) • F(x)`. The density
`rho_R(eta) = c_d^2 L int norm(k_R(xi-eta)) mu(dxi)` is `rho`, a lower
(`[0, inf]`-valued) integral of a nonnegative function, which is the
manuscript's integral without a junk value; `nu` is
`volume.withDensity rho`. "Radon" is `IsLocallyFiniteMeasure` (as in
`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`; on `R^d` a locally finite Borel measure is
Radon), "even" and "tempered" are the package's `IsEven` and `IsTempered`.
`C_Gamma` is `MaskedSpectralGrowth.CGamma`, built from the Bochner integral
`M_Gamma = int e^(-norm(x)^2/4) Gamma(dx)`; it is the manuscript's constant
when `Gamma` is tempered, as under `H:homog` (`MGamma_pos`). In the general
forms, which do not assume `Gamma` tempered, `CGamma` is that Bochner
integral as written.

Statements. `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper` assumes the section's standing
assumptions (lines 7-8) `H:homog` (`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`)
and `Gamma != 0` (`a = alpha0` plays no role in this proposition), a real
Schwartz `zeta != 0` (line 96), and a separable complex Hilbert space `H` with
an `H`-valued Schwartz map `F` (lines 111-112). It proves: `zeta-hat` is
integrable and `L > 0`; and for every `R > 0`: `k_R` is integrable with
`norm(k_R)_1 = L`, `nu_R` is even, tempered and locally finite,
`nu_R(B(y,r)) <= c_d^2 L^2 C_Gamma r^alpha` for open and closed balls, all
`y` and `r > 0`, with a right side that does not depend on `R`; and
`E:masked-hilbert-fourier`: `norm((zeta_R F)-hat)^2` is `mu`-integrable,
`norm(F-hat)^2` is `nu_R`-integrable, the inequality holds both for lower
integrals and for Bochner integrals, and the right side is finite (proof
lines 177-178). It uses the `H:homog` fields `mu_radon` (only to make `mu`
s-finite), `mu_tempered`, `mu_even`, `spectral` and `scaling`; the other
fields, `Gamma != 0`, the inner product and the separability of `H` are
carried but unused. The general form `masked_auxiliary_norm` assumes only:
`mu` s-finite, tempered and even, `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`,
`SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha)`, `zeta != 0`, and `E` any complex
Banach space. The pieces carry their own hypotheses, stated in their rows.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `mu` s-finite for the Tonelli steps
(derived from `mu_radon` in the wrapper); integrability of every integrand
whose Bochner integral is stated; measurability is proved, not assumed; the
balls are `Metric.ball y r` and `Metric.closedBall y r`.

Proof route (differences from the TeX):
- `L > 0` (stated without proof at line 99) is proved by Fourier injectivity
  (`eq_zero_of_paperHat_eq_zero`, from `paper_inversion`).
- The ball bound follows the TeX: Tonelli and the substitution
  `u = xi - eta` (`nu_apply`, the display of lines 140-143), then
  `MaskedSpectralGrowth.closedBall_le` at every center `y + u`
  (`mu_closedBall_le`) and `norm(k_R)_1 = L`.
- Radon: local finiteness is derived from the ball bound, not from the
  continuity of `rho_R` (lines 131-134).
- Tempered: Peetre's inequality
  `(1+norm eta)^(-N) <= (1+norm xi)^(-N) (1+norm(xi-eta))^N` and the Schwartz
  decay of `k_R` give
  `int (1+norm eta)^(-N) dnu_R <= c_d^2 L (int (1+norm xi)^(-N) dmu)(int (1+norm u)^N norm(k_R(u)) du)`
  with the exponent `N` of `mu` (`lintegral_weight_nu_le`); this replaces the
  "same dyadic argument" of lines 145-146.
- Even: `k_R(-u) = conj k_R(u)` (`zeta` real) and the evenness of `mu`, as in
  lines 134-135.
- The convolution identity `(zeta_R F)-hat(xi) = c_d int k_R(xi-eta) F-hat(eta) deta`
  (lines 153-157) is proved for a Banach-space-valued `F` directly by Fourier
  inversion of `F` and one Bochner Fubini swap (`paperHat_mask`); the scalar,
  finite-rank and projection steps of lines 161-167 are not needed.
- Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz (lines 167-168) is proved from the nonnegativity of
  `t -> int a (g - t)^2` (`sq_integral_mul_le`); the final Tonelli step
  (lines 176-177) is `lintegral_nu`.

Narrower than the TeX, or not formalized:
- The last sentence of the proposition, "For a real `H`, the same assertion
  holds after complexification" (line 117), is not formalized in this module
  (the only part of the statement missing here); it is proved in
  `MaskedAuxiliaryReal` (wave L13), over the complexification `Cx H` built
  there (Mathlib has none).
- The proof-internal claims that `rho_R(eta)` is finite at every `eta` and
  that `rho_R` is continuous (lines 131-134) are not formalized; they are not
  part of the statement, and the Lean route does not need them (`rho` is
  `[0, inf]`-valued and local finiteness of `nu_R` comes from the ball bound).
- The wrapper is not instantiated in Lean at a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying all
  of `H:homog`.

Refutations (`refutations/masked-auxiliary-norm/`):
- `PeetreFactor`: Peetre's inequality without the factor `(1+norm(xi-eta))^N`
  is false (`d = 1`, `N = 1`).
- `CdConvention`: `c_d (2 pi)^d = 1` (the normalization without the square) is
  false at `d = 2`.
- `KernelNormScaling`: `norm(k_R)_1 = R^d L` (which would lose the uniformity
  in `R`) is false for the Gaussian `zeta`, `d = 1`, `R = 2`.
- `ZetaNonzero`: `L > 0` without `zeta != 0` is false (`zeta = 0`).

The definitions `dil`, `hatS`, `zc` and `zetaS` (the dilation, the transform
of a Schwartz map as a Schwartz map, and the complex Schwartz forms of `zeta`
and `zeta_R`) only serve the proof route and have no rows.

## MaskedAuxiliaryReal (whole result)

Wave L13 item C6, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedAuxiliaryReal.lean`:
the last clause of Proposition `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` (Auxiliary mask
norm; `notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `39f2597a`, statement
lines 106-118, proof lines 120-180), "For a real `H`, the same assertion holds
after complexification" (line 117). With it every conclusion of the
proposition is a Lean conclusion under its hypotheses, nothing supplied:

1. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, the measure conclusions and the complex case
   (lines 107-116): `MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.masked_auxiliary_norm_paper` (section
   `MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`): `nu_R` even, tempered and Radon,
   `E:masked-auxiliary-growth` uniformly in `R > 0`, and
   `E:masked-hilbert-fourier` for a separable complex Hilbert space `H`.
2. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`, the real case (line 117):
   `masked_auxiliary_norm_real_paper`, with the section's hypotheses
   (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, lines 7-8; `zeta` a real nonzero Schwartz
   function, line 96), `H` a separable real Hilbert space and `F` an
   `H`-valued Schwartz map. With `F_C = iota o F` (`cxS F`), it states: the
   complexification `H_C = Cx H` is a separable complex Hilbert space;
   `iota` is isometric and `\|z\|^2 = \|Re z\|^2 + \|Im z\|^2`; the masked
   complexified map is the complexification of the real masked map
   (`zeta_R F_C = iota(zeta_R F)`); the transform in real terms,
   `\|(F_C)^(xi)\|^2 = c_d^2 (\|int cos(xi.x) F(x) dx\|^2 + \|int sin(xi.x) F(x) dx\|^2)`;
   and every conclusion of `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper` for `F_C`, that is
   the measure conclusions again and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier` for `F_C`
   (with integrability and a finite right side).

So the whole result is the conjunction of the two wrappers
`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm.masked_auxiliary_norm_paper` (complex `H`) and
`masked_auxiliary_norm_real_paper` (real `H`); no single Lean theorem states
both sentences.

Why complexification and not a statement over `RCLike`: the transform of
the section (lines 10-14) has the kernel `e^(-i xi.x)`, so the transform of an
`H`-valued map takes values in a complex space even for a real `H`; the
clause means: complexify `H`, regard `F` as a map into the complexification,
and apply the complex assertion. Mathlib (at the companion's pin) has no
complexification of a real inner product space, so it is built here: `Cx H`
is the pairs `(re, im)`, read as `re + i im`, with
`(a+ib)(u,v) = (au - bv, av + bu)` and the inner product
`<x,y> = <x.re,y.re> + <x.im,y.im> + i(<x.re,y.im> - <x.im,y.re>)`
(conjugate linear in the first argument, Mathlib's convention; the TeX does
not define the complexification, and this is the standard one); completeness
and separability transfer along the real equivalence `Cx H ~ H x H`. This is
a construction of the standard object, not a modelled one; the section
proposes no register entry for it (see the decision noted for the author).

Hypotheses. `Gamma != 0` is carried, unused (as in the complex wrapper);
the completeness of `H` gives that of `Cx H`, needed by the complex
statement; the separability of `H` gives that of `Cx H`, a hypothesis of the
complex wrapper that its proof does not use. The general form
`masked_auxiliary_norm_real` drops `Gamma != 0` and separability, and takes
`mu` s-finite, tempered and even, the spectral convention and the scaling of
`Gamma`. The proof-internal claims of lines 131-134 (`rho_R` finite at every
`eta` and continuous) are not part of the statement and are not formalized
(as recorded in `MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`). Nothing is supplied. The
extensionality lemmas of the structure `Cx` (generated by `@[ext]`) are
listed below as auxiliary; its compiler-generated constructor declarations
have no row.

Refutations (`refutations/masked-auxiliary-real/`), classified; none relies on
a junk value. Lean-route-only controls (b), each at `H = R`:
`InnerConjugateSlot` (the inner product of `Cx H` is not complex linear in
the first slot: `<i iota 1, iota 1> = -i`), `NormSumConvention` (the sum norm
`\|x\| + \|y\|` is not the norm of `x + iy`: `\|1 + i\| = sqrt 2`) and
`OfRealNotComplexLinear` (`iota` is not complex linear: `iota(Re(i) 1) = 0`,
`i iota 1 = 0 + 1i`). The complexification is the companion's construction
and the TeX does not define its inner product, so no control of class (a) is
available for it.

## MaskedContinuousWave (whole result)

Formalizes `L:masked-continuous-wave` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
at `39f2597a`, statement lines 494-506, display `E:masked-continuous-wave`
lines 501-505, proof lines 508-558) with the standing assumptions of its
subsection (lines 391-393) and the hypotheses `T > 0`, `0 < a < 1` of
`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 188-204). The factors are
`c_r(t) = cos(rt)` (`cFn`) and `b_r(t) = <r> sin(rt)/r` for `r > 0`,
`b_0(t) = t` (`bFn`; lines 495-499). `Wave` and `Wave.eval` give the choices
`F_r` in `{c_r, b_r}`, `G_rho` in `{c_rho, b_rho}` (line 500). `waveFn I F G r rho`
is `1_I F_r G_rho` with real values viewed in `C`. `C_1` is
`4 * 3^(1-a) * C_0(a)` (line 504), with `C_0(a) = 16/(1-a)` from
`MaskedTrigProducts`.

What is stated. The manuscript's left side is the norm of the complexified
temporal completion `H_a^C` (lines 392-393). As in
`MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`, this norm is modelled
abstractly. `E` is a complex inner product space. `V` is a submodule of
`R -> C`, the functions accepted into the completion. `emb : V -> E` is a
linear inclusion, and `||f||_a` is `||emb f||`. `H_a` is not built in this
module. The wrapper `masked_continuous_wave_paper` takes the manuscript's
hypotheses: `0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `0 < h <= 1`, `0 <= s`, `s + h <= T`,
`r, rho >= 0`, `F, G` in `{c, b}`. It also takes the same two supplied
inputs as `masked_trig_products_bridged_paper`, under the same names.
`hmem` says that for every `A` that is `C^1` on `I = [s, s+h]`
(`ContDiffOn R 1 A I`) and every real `omega`, `1_I A e^(i omega t)` lies in
`V`. This is B24's `hmem` quantified over every amplitude B24 accepts. Its
source is `L:masked-time-completion`, lines 202-203: bounded measurable
amplitudes on a subinterval, extended by zero, belong to the completion. A
function that is `C^1` on the compact `I` is bounded there and measurable
after extension by zero, so the input asks for no more than its source.
`hnorm` is B24's `hnorm` verbatim: for `f` in `V` with `f` in `L^2(0,T)`,
`||emb f||^2 = Re timeForm a T f f`. This is the complexification clause of
`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 201-202, with lines 195-196 and 237-239).
The conclusion has two parts. First, `1_I F_r G_rho` lies in `V`. Second,
for that element, `||emb(1_I F_r G_rho)||^2 <= C_1(a) (1+T)^4 h^(2-a) Q_h(r,rho)`,
which is `E:masked-continuous-wave` with the manuscript's constant. No
`Gamma != 0` is assumed, and the TeX states none.

Implicit side conditions made explicit. The functions are real-valued and
enter `V` through the coercion `R -> C`. `bFn r` is also defined for
`r < 0`, but that value is never used, because `r, rho >= 0` are hypotheses.
No `sSup` occurs in the statement. In the proof, `M` and `D` are suprema over
the nonempty set `I` (since `h > 0`) of bounded sets, so they are not Lean's
junk value. `C_0(a)` is the junk-free `16/(1-a)` because `a < 1`, and the
brackets raised to real powers are at least `1`.

Hypotheses carried but unused: `T > 0`. It follows from `0 <= s`, `h > 0`
and `s + h <= T`.

The proof route differs from the TeX's; the statement and constant are the
same. The TeX first writes `b_r = t <r> int_0^1 cos(vrt) dv` for `r <= 1`
(lines 516-527). It then forms `H_a`-valued Bochner averages over up to two
copies of `[0,1]` and applies Hilbert Jensen (lines 527-536). Next it applies
`L:masked-trig-products` with `A(t) = t^j` (lines 541-543) and compares
brackets (lines 543-554). Lean uses no averaging and no continuity of a
parameter family in `H_a`. Each factor is split into an amplitude, a
trigonometric shape and a frequency (`amp`, `trig`, `fr`, `eval_eq`):

- `c_r = 1 * cos(r t)`;
- for `r >= 1`, `b_r = (<r>/r) sin(r t)`, where `<r>/r <= sqrt 2` is the
  TeX's coefficient (line 516);
- for `r < 1`, including `r = 0`, `b_r = b_r * cos(0 t)`.

`masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` is then applied once. The amplitude is
`amp F r * amp G rho` and the frequencies are `r'` in `{r, 0}`, `rho'` in
`{rho, 0}`, with `|r - r'|, |rho - rho'| <= 1` (`waveFn_eq_prodFn`,
`fr_spec`). Each factor has an envelope with `M_i + h D_i <= sqrt 2 (1+T)`
(`amp_bound`, from `bFn_bounds`). `amp_prod_sup` bounds the suprema with
`csSup_le` and `derivWithin` on `Icc` through `uniqueDiffOn_Icc`. Together
they give `M + hD <= 2(1+T)^2`, so `(M+hD)^2 <= 4(1+T)^4`. The TeX instead
has `(M+hD)^2 <= (1+T)^4` and then the squared scalar coefficient `4`. The
bracket comparison is the TeX's: `bracket_add_le`, then
`bracket_rpow_shift_le`, then `frequencyPair_shift_le`. Together they give
`Q_h(r',rho') <= 3^(1-a) Q_h(r,rho)`. The case split is at `r < 1` versus
`r >= 1` instead of the TeX's `r <= 1` versus `r >= 1`; the two differ only
at `r = 1`, where both apply.

Narrower conclusion: none in the statement. This wrapper takes `hmem` and
`hnorm` for abstract `V`, `emb`;
`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted.masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper`
discharges both in the concrete `H_a` of `TimeCompletion` (see
"TimeCompletion (whole result)"), so `L:masked-continuous-wave` holds with
nothing supplied.

Not formalized: the TeX's averaging argument, because Lean proves the same
bound by the route above.

## MaskedModulation (whole result)

Covers two modules, `TimeSchur` and `MaskedModulation`, on
`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `a284420` (the file is
identical at `ba01d98`, so every label and line number below holds at both).
It formalizes the Schur bound `E:masked-time-schur` (lines 150-152, inside
`L:masked-time-completion`, lines 141-156) and `L:masked-temporal-modulation`
(lines 396-405, display `E:masked-temporal-modulation` at 399-403), both in
double-integral form. It also re-issues `L:masked-trig-products` (lines
459-489) with one supplied input replaced by a narrower one. Both remaining
inputs are discharged in `TimeCompletion` (see "TimeCompletion (whole
result)").

What is stated. The manuscript's left sides are norms in the temporal
completion `H_a` and its complexification `H_a^C`. This module does not
use the completion. It is built separately in `TimeCompletion`, where
`emb_norm_sq_eq_timeForm` identifies the norm with the double integral
bounded here. On real compact smooth tests, `||f||_a^2` is by
definition the double integral
`int_0^T int_0^T f(t) f(s) |t-s|^(-a) dt ds` (lines 190-192). By lines
201-202 and 237-239, the complexified norm of every `f` in `L^2(0,T)` is the
same double integral with `f(t) conj f(s)`. Lean bounds exactly these double
integrals: `TimeSchur.timeForm a T f g` is the iterated integral over
`[0,T]^2` of `f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)`, and `TimeSchur.kern a x = |x|^(-a)`.

`E:masked-time-schur`. `time_schur_paper` covers real `f` in `L^2(0,T)`
under the hypotheses `0 < a < 1` and `T > 0`. It proves that the integrand is
integrable on `[0,T]^2` and that the double integral is at most
`(2T^(1-a)/(1-a)) int f^2`. `time_schur_complex` gives the same bound for
`|timeForm a T f f|` with complex `f` (the complexified form, lines 235-237).
The proof is the TeX's: the row integral is at most `2T^(1-a)/(1-a)` (lines
228-229; Lean computes it exactly in `integral_row`), then
`2|xy| <= x^2 + y^2` and Tonelli.

`L:masked-temporal-modulation`. `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` takes the
standing assumptions of lines 391-393 and of `L:masked-time-completion`
(`T > 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `I = [s, s+h]` inside `[0,T]`, `0 < h <= 1`) and the
lemma's hypotheses (`A` is `C^1` on `I`, `M = sup_I |A|`, `D = sup_I |A'|`).
For every real `omega`, with `F = 1_I A e^(i omega t)`, it proves two things:
the integrand `F(t) conj F(u) |t-u|^(-a)` is integrable on `[0,T]^2`, and
`|timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)` with
`C0(a) = 16/(1-a)`. This bounds the absolute value of the complex double
integral, which implies the bound on its real part. The constant depends only
on `a`, which is the stated uniformity in `T, s, h, A, omega` (line 404).

The proof route differs from the TeX's; only the statement and the constant
`C0(a)` match. The TeX differentiates `c(v)` at the moving endpoint (lines
414-420), splits the square into two conjugate triangles (lines 420-426),
treats `|omega h| <= 1` directly (lines 428-431), integrates by parts on
`[1/k, 1]` for `k = |omega h| > 1`, and closes with `8 sqrt 2 <= 16` (lines
438-452). Lean proceeds as follows:

- `c` is `acorr Phi v = int_R Phi(u+v) conj Phi(u) du` with `Phi = 1_I A`.
  For `0 <= v <= h` this is the TeX's `c(v)`; that identification is not
  itself a Lean statement.
- No derivative of `c` is used. `acorr_bound` proves `|c(v)| <= M^2 (h-v)_+`,
  which contains the TeX's `c(h) = 0` and `|c| <= hM^2`. `acorr_lip` proves
  `|c(v) - c(w)| <= (M^2 + hMD)(w - v)`, the integrated form of the TeX's
  `|c'| <= M^2 + hMD`.
- A shear substitution and Fubini (`timeForm_eq_acorr`) give
  `timeForm = int_R |v|^(-a) e^(i omega v) c(v) dv`. The symmetry
  `c(-v) = conj c(v)` (`integral_acorr_split`) writes this as `X + conj X`,
  with `X` the integral over `v > 0`.
- Case `<h omega> <= 8` (it contains the TeX's case `|omega h| <= 1`):
  `crude_bound` with `constant_small`.
- Case `<h omega> > 8`, so `k = h|omega| > 7`: the integration by parts is
  replaced by a half-period shift `v -> v + pi/|omega|` (`osc_bound`, with
  the explicit majorant `majorant`). The final check is `4 pi 8/7 <= 16`
  (`constant_large`).

`L:masked-trig-products` with the narrowed input.
`masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` has exactly the hypotheses of
`MaskedTrigProducts.masked_trig_products_paper`, except that the supplied
modulation bound `hmod` is replaced by `hnorm`. `hnorm` says: for `f` in `V`
with `f` in `L^2(0,T)`, `||emb f||^2 = Re timeForm a T f f`. This is the
complexification clause of `L:masked-time-completion` (lines 201-202,
extended to `L^2(0,T)` by lines 195-196 and 237-239). `hnorm` is required only
on `V` intersected with `L^2(0,T)`. The wrapper derives `hmod` from `hnorm`
and `masked_temporal_modulation_paper`, using `memLp_modeFn` to put the modes
in `L^2(0,T)`. `hmem` (the modes lie in `V` and `emb` is linear, lines
202-203) stays supplied. The wrapper is stated for abstract `V`, `emb`; it
says nothing about elements of `V` outside `L^2(0,T)`.
`TimeCompletion.masked_trig_products_completed_paper` instantiates it with
`H_a`, discharging `hmem` and `hnorm`. `MaskedTrigProducts` itself
is unchanged; its `masked_trig_products_paper` still takes `hmod`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:

- `L^2(0,T)` is `MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`.
- `A` is a function on the reals, and only its values on `I` enter.
- `C^1(I; C)` is `ContDiffOn R 1 A I`, and `A'` is `derivWithin A I`.
- `M` and `D` are `sSup` over `I`. `envelope_of_contDiffOn` uses compactness
  to show the sets are bounded, so neither is Lean's junk value.
- Integrability on the product measure is a conjunct of every
  double-integral conclusion, so the Bochner integrals are not Lean's junk
  `0`.
- The diagonal value of `kern` enters only on a null set.

Hypotheses carried but unused:

- `0 < a` in `time_schur_paper` and `time_schur_complex`; the general
  `time_schur_rclike` needs only `a < 1` and `0 <= T`.
- `T > 0` and `h <= 1` in `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` and in the
  bridged wrapper.

The completion `H_a` and the other clauses of `L:masked-time-completion`
are formalized in `TimeCompletion` (see "TimeCompletion (whole result)"),
not in this module.

## MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)

Formalizes `P:masked-spectral-growth` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
at `39f2597a`, lines 37-94) in full, with its displays
`E:masked-gaussian-transform` (lines 45-48) and `E:masked-translated-ball`
(lines 49-52). It also derives the spectral homogeneity
`mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)`, which `SpectralHomog`, `DampedNorms` and
`ClockCopy` take as their one supplied input. The TeX derives it from the
scaling of `Gamma` and Fourier uniqueness: proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
in `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, lines
1067-1068, and proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines 5582-5593. The section covers
three modules. `GaussianTest` is the foundation (rows marked
"[foundation: GaussianTest]"): Mathlib has no Gaussian Schwartz map, so the
module builds `x -> exp(-c norm(x)^2)` (`c > 0`) as one by hand
(`gaussSchwartz`, decay from the Faa di Bruno bound
`norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le`). From it, it builds the complex test
`gaussTest s hs w y`, `x -> e^(-i<y,x>) e^(-s norm(x-w)^2)` (`s > 0`), and
proves its Fourier integral on `R^d` (`gaussTest_fourier`, from Mathlib's
`GaussianFourier.integral_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add`). The test used in the
proof (lines 77-78) is the case `w = 0`, `s = r^2/4`. `MaskedSpectralGrowth`
holds the proposition and the derivation. `ClockCopyHomog` re-issues three
existing wrappers without the supplied input.

The wrapper `masked_spectral_growth_paper` assumes the section's standing
assumptions (lines 7-8): `H:homog`
(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`) and `Gamma != 0`.
It uses only the fields `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and
`scaling`. The fields `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`,
`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_radon`, `mu_even`, `threshold` and
`alpha_range` are carried but unused. The general theorem
`masked_spectral_growth` assumes exactly these: `Gamma` and `mu` tempered
(`IsTempered`), the spectral convention `E:masked-spectral-convention`
(lines 17-21; `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`), the scaling
`Gamma(cA) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` for measurable `A` and `c > 0` (written
`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha)`, which is literally the
`scaling` field), and `Gamma != 0`. `Gamma != 0` is used only for
`M_Gamma > 0`. `masked_gaussian_transform` assumes only the spectral convention.
`translated_gauss_le` assumes the convention and the scaling. `closedBall_le`
assumes those two and the `mu`-integrability of the Gaussian. None of these
general forms restricts `alpha`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
- The manuscript's `M_Gamma < inf` is stated as `Gamma`-integrability of
  `exp(-norm(x)^2/4)`.
- A Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, so the wrappers
  conclude the integrability of both integrands of `E:masked-gaussian-transform`
  for every `y` and `r > 0`. `masked_gaussian_transform`, `spectral_gaussTest`
  and `spectral_translated_gauss` alone are identities of Lean integrals, with
  no integrability conclusion.
- The balls are `Metric.ball y r` and `Metric.closedBall y r`, and the mass
  bound is stated in `[0, inf]` as `mu(B) <= ENNReal.ofReal (C_Gamma r^alpha)`.

The derived homogeneity is `spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`: under `H:homog`,
`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`. It uses the fields `mu_tempered`, `spectral`
and `scaling`. Its general form is `spectralHomogeneous_of_scaling`
(`mu` tempered, the spectral convention, the scaling of `Gamma`, any real
`alpha`), and its pushforward form is `map_smul_of_scaling`. With it,
`ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper` and
`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper` have exactly the conclusions of
`ClockCopy.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`, `ClockCopy.damped_N2_nonneg_paper`
and `DampedNorms.damped_norms_finite_paper`, with the argument
`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha` removed. Each is proved by applying the
existing wrapper, so the hypotheses carried but unused there are as in the
`ClockCopy` section, except that `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and the `Gamma`
scaling are now used. The remaining conclusions of
`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` are in the section `DampedNormsHomog`.

Proof route:
- For the proposition, Lean follows the TeX. The exceptions:
  - The Gaussian Fourier constant (lines 68-76, derived there from the ODE
    `J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)`) comes from Mathlib.
  - The integrability of a translated Gaussian against a tempered measure
    (`integrable_gauss_of_tempered`) is proved directly from the package's
    integral form of temperedness (`IsTempered`: `int (1+norm(x))^(-k) < inf`
    for some `k`), not by the polynomial mass growth argument of lines 25-32.
- For the homogeneity, the TeX only says "Fourier uniqueness". Lean proceeds in
  three steps:
  1. It weights both `mu o (c.)^(-1)` and `c^(-alpha) mu` by `e^(-norm(xi)^2)`.
     These are finite measures because `mu` is tempered.
  2. Their characteristic functions agree. Each is a translated Gaussian
     integral against `Gamma`, by the spectral convention applied to
     `e^(-s norm(x-t)^2)`, and the two are related by the scaling of `Gamma`.
  3. `Measure.ext_of_charFun` identifies the two weighted measures, and
     `withDensity_inv_same` removes the weight.

Refutations (`refutations/masked-spectral-growth/`):
- `ExponentShift`, `TransformFactor` and `SpectralExponent` use `d = 1`,
  `Gamma` = Lebesgue measure, `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`. This is outside the
  range of `H:homog`, so they refute variants of the general theorems
  `translated_gauss_le`, `masked_gaussian_transform` and
  `spectralHomogeneous_of_scaling`, not variants of
  `masked_spectral_growth_paper`.
- `DecayConstant` and `FourierExponent` refute variants of
  `poly_mul_exp_neg_sq_le` and `gaussTest_fourier`.

The wrapper is not instantiated in Lean at a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying all of
`H:homog`. Not formalized: the polynomial mass growth of tempered Radon
measures and the Schwartz integrability claim of lines 25-32 beyond Gaussians,
and the rest of `S:masked-covariance` except `P:masked-auxiliary-norm`
(module `MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), which applies `closedBall_le` at every
center, `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` (module `QuotientObstruction`), the
finite comparison of `P:masked-noise-completion` (module
`GaussianComparison`), and the results of `TimeCompletion`, `MaskedTrigProducts`,
`MaskedModulation` and `MaskedContinuousWave`.

## MaskedTrigProducts (whole result)

Formalizes `L:masked-trig-products` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
at `ba01d98`): for `P_r` in `{cos(rt), sin(rt)}` and `Q_rho` in
`{cos(rho t), sin(rho t)}`, the bound `E:masked-trig-products`,
`||1_I A P_r Q_rho||_a^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)`, with
`Q_h` as in `E:masked-frequency-pair` and `<x> = sqrt(1+x^2)`. All four
`cos`/`sin` combinations are covered, together with every step of the
proof: the four-mode expansion (coefficients of absolute value `1/4`,
frequencies `+-r +- rho`), the Hilbert-space inequality
`||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2`, and the frequency
count (two modes at `|r-rho|`, two at `r+rho`).
The norm `||.||_a` is modelled abstractly. The manuscript's norm is that of
the complexified temporal completion `H_a^C` of `L:masked-time-completion`,
and functions enter it through the linear inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. In Lean,
`E` stands for that completion (for the concrete completion see
`TimeCompletion`; a complex inner product space in the
paper wrapper, a complex seminormed space in the general theorems).
`V : Submodule C (R -> C)` is the class of functions accepted into it, and
`emb : V ->l[C] E` is the inclusion, so `||emb f||` stands for `||f||_a`.
This is faithful because the proof uses only linearity of the inclusion: it
writes the product as a linear combination of four modes and bounds each
mode. Two inputs are supplied as named hypotheses. `hmem` says that every
mode `1_I A e^(i omega t)` lies in `V` (from `L:masked-time-completion`).
`hmod` is the bound `E:masked-temporal-modulation` of
`L:masked-temporal-modulation` for every real `omega`, stated in the
manuscript's form with `C0(a) = 16/(1-a)`. These two inputs stay as they
are for `masked_trig_products_paper` and the general theorems below.
`MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` (see "MaskedModulation
(whole result)") keeps `hmem` and replaces `hmod` by the norm identity
`hnorm`, `||emb f||^2` = the real part of the defining double integral of
`f(t) conj f(s) |t-s|^(-a)`, required only for `f` in `V` that lie in
`L^2(0,T)`; it proves the modulation bound. The product function is never
assumed to satisfy a bound, and its membership in `V` is not an independent
assumption of the paper wrapper: `prodFn_mem` derives it from `hmem`. The
general theorems `trig_product_bound` and `trig_product_bound_half` take a
membership witness `hp`, which is redundant for the same reason. Implicit hypotheses made explicit in
`masked_trig_products_paper`: `A` is a function on the reals (only its
values on `I` matter, because of the indicator); `C^1(I; C)` is
`ContDiffOn R 1 A I`; `M` and `D` are the `sSup` of `||A||` and of
`||derivWithin A I||` over `I`; `I = Icc s (s+h)`. The wrapper also carries
the standing hypotheses `0 < a < 1`, `T > 0`, `0 < h <= 1`, `0 <= s`,
`s + h <= T`, `C^1`, the definitions of `M` and `D`, and `r, rho >= 0`.
These are carried but unused by the proof; they are consumed by the
supplied modulation input. The general theorems `trig_product_bound` and
`trig_product_bound_half` hold for arbitrary real `C, a, h, M, D, r, rho`
and any set `I`. The sign conditions on `r, rho` are unnecessary because
`<.>` is even. `trig_product_bound_half` is sharper than the stated lemma: it
records the factor `1/2` that the proof yields ("one half of the asserted
right side"). `L:masked-temporal-modulation` and the bound
`E:masked-time-schur` are now formalized for the defining double integral
(`MaskedModulation`, `TimeSchur`). The completion `H_a` of
`L:masked-time-completion`, the identification of its norm with the double
integral and the extension from `L^2(0,T)` are formalized in
`TimeCompletion`. They enter this module's wrappers through `hmem` and
`hmod` (and through `hmem` and `hnorm` in the bridged wrapper), and
`TimeCompletion.masked_trig_products_completed_paper` discharges both, so
`L:masked-trig-products` holds with nothing supplied.

## OccupationCeilingExact (narrower result: `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` without the `C_2` sentence; class `O` by joint representatives (the bridge to `O` itself is `ClassOBridge`, wave L14); rate and cost identification not formalized)

Wave L9, item A2, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/OccupationCeilingExact.lean`.
It formalizes `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` (Countable Rayleigh
near-occupations; `notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` at `39f2597a`,
statement lines 180-188, proof 190-236) and
`T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (The computed occupation ceiling;
statement lines 249-264, proof 266-316) with the EXACT constant `C_occ` of
`P:raw-occupation-energy` (`RawOccupationEnergy.Cocc`), in both forms of
`E:occupation-score-ceiling`, for the variational values `S_c^pos`, and
with them the comparison of `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` (lines 328-332,
proof 346-361) for `S_2^pos`. Nothing is supplied: `S1Bdd` is never
assumed, the named input `SpaceTimeCS` of `OccupationCeilingFinite` is not
used, and the space-time Cauchy-Schwarz bound is wave item L8-c1's
`SpaceTimePositivity.integral_mean_mul_le_sqrt`. Standing assumptions (lines
4-21): `H:homog` (`HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu`, `a` for `alpha0`)
and `Gamma != 0` (line 20); `q = 4-alpha`, `k = 3-alpha`, `m = q/k`.
`I_Psi = int_0^1 lambda_(Psi,s) ds` with `lambda` the square root of the
supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient (`VariationalDilation.integratedRate`,
`rate`), `v_Psi` is the integral-form cost `VariationalDilation.rawCost`,
`h_(Psi,s)` is `VariationalDilation.mean`, `S_c^pos` is
`sSup (VariationalRate.scoreSet alpha0 Gamma c)`, `U_c` is
`SpatialBracket.ceilingValue alpha c C_occ` (`E:occupation-score-ceiling`,
lines 253-256), `F_0 = SpatialFourLinear.F0` and
`F_b = SpatialBracket.Fb` (`E:occupation-scalar-map`, lines 238-244). The
exact-hypothesis wrappers `occupation_rayleigh_selection_paper`,
`intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_paper` and `intrinsic_spatial_comparison_paper`
have exactly the section's hypotheses. `intrinsic_occupation_ceiling_paper`
proves, for every `c > 0` (the coefficient range of
`P:variational-positive-scores`, `integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` line
372, where `S_c^pos` is defined): the value set is nonempty and bounded
above, `c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 <= U_c` for every `Psi` in `C_pos`,
`S_c^pos <= U_c = c^m k [alpha^(alpha/2) C_occ/(8 q^(q/2))]^(1/k)`, and
`U_c = c^m (2 zeta)^(alpha/(2k)) F_0(E_zeta^O)` for every `zeta > 0`.
`intrinsic_spatial_comparison_paper` proves
`S_2^pos <= 2^m F_0(E_(1/2)^O) < 2^m F_a(E_(1/2)^O)`. Proof route (decision 2
of wave L9): in `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection` the TeX's countable dense
family with a first-index Borel selection (lines 199-212) is replaced by
`N+1` equal time cells (`idx`, `cellInd`) with near-optimal real unit tests
at the left nodes (`OccupationCeilingFinite.exists_unitTest_gt`) and the
uniform Lipschitz bounds in `s` of `int h_s f^2` (`L:variational-global-mean`)
and of `lambda_s^2` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`); the selected field
`g_s = f_j` on cell `j` (`stepG`, `stepDG`) is a finite simple field of unit
tests, hence in `O` as modelled by `IsOccField` (`stepField_isOcc`). The
bound `<Psi, rho_g> <= sqrt(v_Psi A(g))` is `step_mean_le_sqrt`, the final
display of `L:occupation-raw-square` (lines 39-42) in integral form for
these finite-cell fields: the cell indicators are limits of continuous
trapezoids (`trap`), the L8-c1 bound applies to the continuous fields, and
both sides pass to the limit by dominated convergence; the map `Q` and
`rho_g in H_I` of `L:occupation-raw-square` are not used here; they are
built in `OccupationCompletion` (wave L14), whose wrapper carries that
label's coverage row. The rest follows the TeX: `I_Psi^2 <= int_0^1 lambda_s^2` (by Jensen,
the TeX's time Cauchy-Schwarz, lines 231-232), the two scalar maxima by
weighted AM-GM (`OccupationCeilingFinite.young_quarter`, `young_q`), the
positive-power algebra (`OccupationCeilingFinite.ceilingValue_eq`), the
second form by `E:raw-occupation-energy`
(`RawOccupationEnergy.raw_occupation_energy_paper`) and
`SpatialBracket.ceilingValue_eq_zeta`, and `F_0 < F_a`
(`SpatialBracket.F0_lt_Fa`, `Delta > 0`). Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
integrability of every time integrand is proved; `S_c^pos` is used only with
nonemptiness and boundedness proved; `T(g) > 0` on `O` (`d >= 1`).
`step_mean_le_sqrt` passes its `Gamma != 0` only to
`VariationalMean.variational_global_mean_paper`, which carries it unused.
Narrower than the TeX (recorded): the moment sentence `C_2(Gamma,a) <= U_2`
(line 261) and the `C_2` form of the comparison (lines 330-331) are not
formalized (they need `T:intrinsic-second-moment`, `C_2 = S_2^pos`); the
statements are for `S_c^pos` and `S_2^pos`; the class `O` (hence `C_occ` and
`E_zeta^O`) is modelled by joint representatives (`IsOccField`), as in
`P:raw-occupation-energy` (the same a.e. data as the TeX's strongly
`H^1`-measurable occupations, not a smaller class; the bridge between the
two descriptions is proved in `ClassOBridge`, wave L14, which restates these
results over `O`); the direct zero case `Gamma = 0` (lines 379-385) is not
formalized here (in part in `ClassOBridge.zero_covariance_paper`) (the theorem itself carries the standing assumption
`Gamma != 0` of line 20). The route definitions `trap`, `idx`, `cellInd`,
`stepG` and `stepDG` only name quantities used in the statements below and
have no rows of their own.

Controls (`refutations/occupation-ceiling-exact/`): (a) a manuscript-claim
perturbation: `ComparisonNeedsA` (the hypothesis `a > 0` of the strict
comparison `F_0 < F_a`, line 351, dropped; witness `a = 0`, `alpha = 1`,
`z = 1`); (b) Lean-route-only controls, about constructions that the TeX does
not use (it selects by a countable first-index Borel choice, lines 199-212),
so they are not manuscript negative controls: `CellWidth` (the cell width
`1/(N+2)` in place of `1/(N+1)` for the index `idx`) and `TrapezoidLimit`
(the limit of the trapezoids `trap` as the indicator of the closed interval,
refuted at the endpoint `s = 0`, a value that does not change any time
integral). No control is of type (c), and none relies on a junk value.
