## SpectralMassIdentity (whole result)

Proves that the spectral-mass constant `R_alpha` of `E:intro-spectral-mass`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, lines
693-697: `B_1` the unit ball of `R^d` and
`R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`) is exactly the resolvent at
`1`, `R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2)`, and hence that
`R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha` for `q > 0`. The second identity is the
display in the proof of `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `39f2597a`, lines 200-206). That
proof cites "the deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
`L:damped-homogeneous-norms`" (main file, lines 1069-1076:
`int mu(dxi)/(a^2+norm(xi)^2) = alpha V a^(alpha-2) int_0^inf u^(alpha-1)/(1+u^2) du`
with `V = mu(B_1)`) together with `E:intro-spectral-mass`. The value of the
radial integral, `pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`, is not written in the TeX; it is
proved here. With the identity, the module states `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
with the manuscript's constant `R_alpha` (`spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper`),
so that lemma is now formalized as printed (statement lines 121-131 of
`integrated_spatial_occupation.tex`, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound` at
lines 126-129).

Abstractions. `ralpha mu alpha` is the formula of line 696 verbatim, with
`B_1` the open unit ball `Metric.ball 0 1` (the same expression as the
hypothesis `hRdef` of the `IntervalScalar` and `IntervalScalarCompleted`
wrappers). The TeX does not say open or closed; for a locally finite
`alpha`-homogeneous `mu` with `alpha > 0` the two balls have the same mass,
but that equality is not stated in Lean and is not needed. `R_Gamma(q)` is
`SpectralHomog.resolvent mu q`, the Bochner integral of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`.

Hypotheses. The general theorems (`resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
`resolvent_eq_ralpha`, `hRdef_iff_resolvent`) assume a locally finite `mu`
with `mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)` for measurable `A` and `c > 0`
(`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`; the sentence of main lines
1067-1068) and `0 < alpha < 2`. The `_paper` wrappers assume `H:homog`
(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`) and nothing else;
`Gamma = 0` is allowed (then `mu = 0` and both sides are `0`), as in the lemma
("allowing `Gamma = 0`", line 123). The homogeneity is derived by
`MaskedSpectralGrowth.spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, and `0 < alpha < 2` by
`alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`. Fields of `H:homog` used by
`resolvent_eq_ralpha_paper` and `hRdef_iff_resolvent_paper` (checked against
every lemma they call: `alpha_mem_Ioo_of_homog`,
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`, `resolvent_one_eq_ralpha`,
`resolvent_eq_ralpha`): `alpha_range`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `mu_radon`,
and `mu_tempered`, `spectral`, `scaling` (through
`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Carried but unused by these two: `dim`,
`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`,
`Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`. `spatial_fourier_bound_ralpha_paper` uses the
fields of `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound_paper` (listed in that
section: `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `threshold`, `Gamma_radon`, `mu_radon`,
`spectral`, `mu_tempered`, `scaling`) and `alpha_range`; carried but unused:
`alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_even`, `Gamma_tempered`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_even`.
Supplied inputs: none.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit, and junk values. The integrability of
`1/(1+norm(xi)^2)` (and of `1/(q^2+norm(xi)^2)`) against `mu` is a conjunct of
each identity, so no identity holds through the Lean value `0` of a
non-integrable Bochner integral; this is the TeX's "`< infinity`" of line 205.
`mu(B_1) < infinity` by local finiteness, so `(mu(B_1)).toReal` is not a junk
value, and `sin(pi alpha/2) > 0` for `0 < alpha < 2`, so the division is
genuine. `ralpha` itself is defined for all real `alpha`; outside `(0,2)` it
is only a formula and no theorem here uses it there.

Proof route (differs from the TeX, same conclusion). The TeX uses polar
coordinates. Lean uses the layer-cake formula (as in
`SpectralHomog.integrable_inv_one_add_sq`, which proves finiteness): for
`0 < t < 1` the level set `{1/(1+norm(xi)^2) > t}` is the open ball of radius
`sqrt((1-t)/t)` (`levelset_eq_ball`; empty for `t >= 1`), whose mass is
`((1-t)/t)^(alpha/2) V` (`SpectralHomog.measure_ball`), and the real Beta
integral `int_0^1 t^(-a) (1-t)^a dt = a pi/sin(pi a)` for `0 < a < 1`
(`beta_real`, from Mathlib's complex Beta function and the reflection formula)
at `a = alpha/2`. `R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_Gamma(1)` is
`SpectralHomog.resolvent_homog`. Route-only helpers are "no direct label
(auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".

Consequences recorded here. `hRdef_iff_resolvent(_paper)`: the hypothesis
`R = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` carried by the `IntervalScalar` and
`IntervalScalarCompleted` wrappers is equivalent to `R = R_Gamma(1)`; those
wrappers are unchanged. The general form of `L:spatial-fourier-bound` with
constant `R_Gamma(1)` stays `SpatialFourierBound.spatial_fourier_bound` and
`spatial_fourier_bound_paper`. Not formalized: nothing of
`E:intro-spectral-mass` or of the display at lines 200-206 is left out.

Refutations (`refutations/spectral-mass-identity/`): `SinFactorTwo`
(`sin(pi alpha/2)` instead of `2 sin(pi alpha/2)` in `R_alpha`, with `mu`
Lebesgue on `R^1`, `alpha = 1`), `ExponentSign` (`q^(2-alpha)` instead of
`q^(alpha-2)`, same `mu`, `q = 2`), `AlphaPositive` (the identity without
`alpha > 0`, at `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`, where `R_Gamma(1) = 1` and
Lean's `R_0` is `0`), `FourierBoundAlphaZero` (the `R_alpha` form of the bound
under the general theorem's hypotheses without `alpha > 0`, with `Gamma`
Lebesgue, `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`; outside `H:homog`). `AlphaPositive` and
`FourierBoundAlphaZero` are controls of Lean's totalized division outside the
manuscript's domain, not convention-independent counterexamples: at
`alpha = 0`, which `H:homog` excludes and where the TeX gives `R_alpha` no
value, `R_0` is the quotient `0/0`, undefined as an ordinary quotient, and
Lean's convention `x/0 = 0` makes it `0`. The continuous extension of
`alpha pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))` at `alpha = 0` is `1`; with it `R_0 = 1`, the
identity holds at the witness and the bound holds there (`1 <= 2`).

`39f2597a`; statement lines 3216-3262, proof lines 3264-3341) re-issued with
fewer supplied inputs, using `StaticPhaseCauchy` (wave L8-h),
`ComplexPhaseScalar` (wave L9-H3) and `PhaseContractions`. The earlier
wrappers `IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper` and
`IntervalScalar.independent_static_blocks_paper` supplied five inputs: the
identity `I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g) = sum sigma^n Y_n`, the order bounds of lines
3285-3292, the Gaussian parity (line 3293), the two first-variance bounds
(lines 3275-3280) and, for the blocks, the scalar step
`m_(j+1) <= e^(lambda h_j)(1 + E_j) m_j`.

Proved here:
1. The identity. With `T` standing for `S_0(-h)` (a continuous linear map),
   `sum_n sigma^n Z_n` converges (from the order bounds) and
   `T(sum_n sigma^n Z_n) = sum_n sigma^n T Z_n` (`static_interaction_orders`).
   Lines 3220-3223 define `I_sigma^eps(h)(f,g)` as `S_0(-h) sum_n sigma^n Z_n`,
   so the conclusion is about that map, not about a supplied series.
2. The order bounds of lines 3285-3292, from `E:all-static-phase-orders`,
   `|S_0(-h)|_lambda <= sqrt(e)` and the norm comparisons for
   `lambda h <= 1` (`transported_le`), with the TeX's constant
   `A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2)` (`StaticPhaseCauchy.allOrdersA`).
3. `E:all-static-phase-orders` from the inputs of
   `StaticPhaseCauchy.static_phase_all_orders_step`, with its circle bound
   `100 e^(2 lambda h)` (lines 3129-3132) no longer supplied: it is proved by
   `ComplexPhaseScalar.complex_phase_paper` at `a = alpha/2`,
   `lambda = n/h` (`circle_of_complex_phase`, `static_phase_all_orders_cp`)
   from the more primitive inputs `FockSandwich`, `CPInputs`,
   `PropagatorBlock`.
4. The per-block step of `E:independent-static-blocks`: from the
   factorization `M_j = S_0(h_j) I_j`, `|S_0(h_j)|^2 <= e^(lambda h_j)` and the
   per-block interaction bound on phases adapted to the past
   (`independent_static_blocks_operator`, `_paper`).

Still supplied (named hypotheses): `FockSandwich` (`E:fock-sandwich` in
operator form, lines 2972-2976, `E:abstract-sandwich` of `L:complex-phase`,
lines 2755-2759); `CPInputs` (`E:cp-input`, imported in the TeX at lines
2739-2748, and the inverse-root integral, lines 2801-2826); `PropagatorBlock`
(the identification of `M_z(h)` in `X_lambda` with the weighted block map,
lines 2920-2931 and 2948-2951); the other inputs of
`static_phase_all_orders_step` (entireness, lines 3134-3135; the coefficient
identification via `L:finite-word-cutoff` with
`|z|_(1/h) <= n |z|_(n/h)`, lines 3143-3154; the lemma itself is proved in
`FiniteWordCutoff`, wave L11, but the identification of the phase
coefficients is not formalized;
`|S_b(f,g)|_(n/h) <= |(f,g)|_(1/h)`, line 3155; the two cutoff removals,
lines 3168-3192, as convergence of norms); the free estimate
`|S_0(-+h)|_lambda <= sqrt(e)`, the group law `S_0(-h) S_0(h) = 1`,
`Z_0 = S_0(h)(f,g)` and the two norm comparisons; the Gaussian parity
(line 3293) and the first-variance bounds of `P:static-phase-variance`
(lines 3275-3280); for the blocks, the per-block bound `hI` on adapted
phases (density and tensoring with the independent past, lines 3333-3337).

`FockSandwich` is not discharged by `FockColumnBound` (wave L11 K2), whose
`fock_form_paper_completed` is a different statement: a Hermite coefficient
model with no packaged Hilbert space, sandwiches that depend on `rho`, and a
bound on sums of squared coefficient norms on the Fourier side. Discharging
`FockSandwich` would need a packaged `l^2` Hilbert space of degree-`<= N`
coefficient vectors, a bounded positive `A_0` whose functional-calculus
inverse root `(A_0 + rho^2)^(-1/2)` agrees with multiplication by `w_rho`, a
`rho`-independent `B`, the conversion to an operator norm, and the
identification of the Fourier side with physical space. Wave L12
(`FockSandwichModel`) provides all of these except the physical-side
identification, with the inverse root agreeing with multiplication by
`w_rho` on the band range (the sandwiched operator is the TeX's operator
extended by zero), and re-issues the wrappers of this module with
`FockSandwich`, the positivity of `A_0` and the self-adjointness of `B`
proved on the Fourier-side model (`static_interaction_model_paper`,
`static_phase_all_orders_model`; for an orthonormal mode family of every
size `m`, which excludes `mu = 0`).

Model and hypotheses. `E` (a complete real inner product space, a real
normed space for the blocks) stands for `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)`; the
`L^2(Omega; X_(1/h))` norms of the Duhamel phases are the real numbers
`z_n`; the cutoff spaces of the order bounds are abstract complex Banach and
Hilbert spaces indexed by the order, the Gaussian cutoff and the band.
Adaptation to the past is an abstract predicate `P j` with `P 0 x` and
preservation by each block (`hadapt`): an explicit modelling of "random
initial phases independent of the `j`th field" (lines 3336-3337), not the
probabilistic notion; the refutation `BlocksNoAdaptation` shows that the
bound fails without it. The section's class enters as
`PhaseContractions.PhaseCovariance` (lines 2490-2493) with
`R_alpha = ralpha mu alpha` and `D_Gamma = dGam Gamma alpha`
(`E:phase-constants`, lines 2494-2501). Recorded in the module header: only
`0 < alpha < 2` is used; local finiteness and the other fields are carried,
unused. `lambda h_j <= 1` is carried, unused,
in `independent_static_blocks_operator_paper` (the TeX needs it for `hI`).
Narrower: the conclusions concern the quantities named by the inputs, and
uniformity in `eps` is that of the inputs. Junk values (module header): real
powers have positive bases or are `(sqrt R)^n`, `(n!)^gamma`, `t^(-1/2)` with
`t > 0`; `R_alpha`, `D_Gamma` use `toReal` of finite ball masses;
`delta_(alpha/2) > 0`; summability is proved, never assumed through `tsum`.
Class: inputs supplied, narrower conclusion (`C:static-interaction` and,
through `static_phase_all_orders_cp`, `P:static-phase-all-orders`).

Refutations (`refutations/static-interaction-completed/`), classified; none
relies on a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbation: `TransportedDropFactor`
(the transported order bound of lines 3272-3292 without the comparison
factor `1/(lambda h)` fails at `lambda h = 1/2`). Lean-route-only
perturbation: `InteractionDropOne` (the bound of `E:static-interaction`
without the free term `1` fails; the witness has `R = D = 0`, admissible for
the general form `static_interaction_orders` with `R, D >= 0`, not an
instance of the class of `S:static-phase` with `mu != 0`). Lean-route-only
control: `BlocksNoAdaptation` (the block bound fails without the abstract
adaptation hypothesis `hadapt`).

## StaticPhaseCauchy (proof steps of `P:static-phase-all-orders`, analytic inputs supplied)

Formalizes the complex-analytic, scalar and Banach-space steps of the proof
of `P:static-phase-all-orders` (All regularized static phase orders) of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a` (main TeX;
statement lines 3087-3115, proof lines 3117-3211; all line numbers in this
section refer to that file). The proposition is an operator and stochastic
statement. Every row below is either a step proved with nothing supplied or
a step row of `E:all-static-phase-orders` (lines 3099-3105) or
`E:all-static-phase-sum` (lines 3109-3114) whose operator and Gaussian
inputs are supplied hypotheses (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker
than the labelled statement). It extends the existing proof-step rows of
`SeriesType` for this proposition (the elementary series bound of lines
3198-3207), which `all_static_phase_sum_step` uses.

Constants (nothing supplied): `I_a` and `delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)}` of
`L:complex-phase` (lines 2761-2762), with `I_a` proved integrable and
positive for `a < 2` (the TeX uses `a = alpha/2` in `(0,1)`), so `delta_a`
is a genuine positive number; `A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2)`
(lines 3095-3097); `d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha)` of `E:fock-sandwich`
(lines 2972-2976).

Steps (nothing supplied): Cauchy's estimate for an entire map with values
in a complete complex normed space, operator-valued included (lines
3134-3142), and the coefficient bound `||C_n|| <= M (d/c)^n` in the TeX's
form, quantified over every `d' >= d`, `d' > 0` (this covers the TeX's
`R_alpha = 0` case of line 3126 without dividing by zero); the arithmetic at
`lambda = n/h` (lines 3149-3163): `d_n <= 2 sqrt(2n) sqrt(R)`, the display of
lines 3158-3160, `100 n <= 200^n`, `n! <= n^n`; the pointwise Fourier
multiplier form of the norm comparisons of lines 3154-3155 (the integration
against the Fourier transform is not formalized); the exponent identity of
`E:all-static-phase-sum`.

Step rows. `E:all-static-phase-orders` at fixed cutoffs
(`static_phase_order_cutoff`) and after both cutoff removals
(`static_phase_all_orders_step`, wrapper `static_phase_all_orders_paper`),
and `E:all-static-phase-sum` (`all_static_phase_sum_step`, wrapper
`all_static_phase_sum_paper`). Abstractions: a complex Banach space stands
for the cutoff space `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` and a real Banach space for
`L^2(Omega; X_(1/h))`; the phase propagator is an entire map `F` from the
complex coupling to the bounded operators, its argument `v` is the initial
phase `S_b(f,g)` times the vacuum, and the phase norms are real numbers
`z1`, `zc m b`, `z`, `N1` named by the inputs. The supplied inputs are:
entireness of the phase entries in the coupling (lines 3134-3135); the
circle bound `100 e^(2 lambda h)` from `L:fock-form` and `L:complex-phase`
with `a = alpha/2` (lines 3129-3132), stated for every `d' >= d_n`,
`d' > 0`, which `L:complex-phase` gives from the sandwich bound of
`L:fock-form` (a sandwich bound with constant `d_N` holds with every larger
constant; the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of `L:fock-form` is
`FockForm.fock_form_paper`,
with the spatial column bound supplied, and the scalar steps of
`L:complex-phase` are in `ComplexPhaseScalar`, with its own supplied inputs;
their combination into the propagator bound is not formalized in this module
(it is derived from named inputs in `StaticInteractionCompleted`, wave L11;
the propagator is not constructed)); the
identification of the coefficient with the cutoff Duhamel
phase via `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 3143-3148; the lemma is proved in
`HermiteWordFock` for one Gaussian coordinate per color and, with the `m`
coordinates per color that the phase words use, in `FiniteWordCutoff`, wave
L11; the identification of the phase coefficients is not formalized) together with the norm
comparison `||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h)` (line 3154); `||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <=
||(f,g)||_(1/h)` (line 3155; the contraction `||S_b(f,g)||_lambda <=
||(f,g)||_lambda` is implicit in the TeX); the cutoff removals `b ->
infinity` and `m -> infinity` (lines 3168-3192) as convergence of the norms
along natural-number cutoffs (the TeX proves strong convergence, which
implies it); and the free bound `||Z_0(h)||_(1/h) <= sqrt(e) ||(f,g)||_(1/h)`
(line 3207). No input assumes a conclusion. In wave L11 the circle bound is derived
(`StaticInteractionCompleted.circle_of_complex_phase`) from `L:complex-phase`
and the named inputs `FockSandwich`, `CPInputs` and `PropagatorBlock`
(section StaticInteractionCompleted).

The wrappers state the section's standing class as in
`IntervalScalar.static_interaction_paper` (lines 2490-2502): locally finite
`mu, Gamma` on `R^3`, `0 < alpha < 2`, `R = R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2
sin(pi alpha/2))`; evenness, positive definiteness and scaling of `Gamma`
enter only through the supplied inputs. Carried and not used (underscore
hypotheses, confirmed by the proofs): in `static_phase_all_orders_paper`,
local finiteness of `mu` and `Gamma`, `0 < alpha` and the formula for `R`
(the step holds for every real `R` and `alpha < 2`); in
`all_static_phase_sum_paper`, local finiteness (`0 < alpha` and the formula
for `R` are used there, to get `0 <= alpha` and `R_alpha >= 0`).

Junk values: `delta_a` is not a junk value (`I_a` is a proved-integrable
positive integral); every real power has a positive base or a nonnegative
base with a positive exponent; there is no division by `d_N`; summability
is proved, not assumed through `tsum`. `sqrt(R)` is the real square root;
in the wrappers `R = R_alpha >= 0`.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the regularized Duhamel phases
`Z_n^eps(h)` themselves, their being Gaussian polynomials of degree at most
`n`, the uniformity in `eps` (it is that of the inputs), the convergence of
`sum sigma^n Z_n^eps(h)` as an `L^2` phase identified with the Duhamel
series (Lean proves absolute convergence of the abstract series), the lemma
`L:complex-phase` (its scalar and weighted-block-map deductions are in
`ComplexPhaseScalar`, with inputs supplied), the propagator bound built from
it and `L:fock-form` (the coefficient-model sandwich estimate of
`L:fock-form` is in `FockForm` with the spatial column bound supplied), not
formalized in this module (in wave L11 `StaticInteractionCompleted` derives
the propagator bound from named inputs; the propagator is not constructed),
and the cutoff-removal arguments.
The conclusions are the two displays for the quantities named by the
inputs.

## SymplecticFree (narrower result: `J_E`, the duality-form identification and symplectic preservation on `E` not formalized; force skewness only at the `L^2` level; free-group data and Young convergence supplied)

Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
`39f2597a` (statement lines 31-61, proof lines 63-160; all line numbers in
this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).

What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
80-88 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
frequency, zero included (lines 89-91), the per-frequency group law and the
reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 143-145). At nonzero frequency
the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 41-42 and 102-105:
abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 46-50) and
`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 54-59) in general form and as
exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).

Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along
the cocompact filter of `R^d`: exactly the properties that lines 121-145
state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
of lines 123-128). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for
`P:constant-young-linear` applied on `L(E)` (lines 105-112): along some
nontrivial filter of finite node lists `(n, p)` whose nodes `p 0, ..., p n`
lie eventually in `[s,t]`, the left Young sums of `X` converge in operator
norm to `U(t,s) - I`. The node lists need not be partitions: ordered nodes,
the endpoints `p 0 = s`, `p n = t` and a vanishing mesh are not required, so
the condition does not characterize the Young evolution; convergence as the
mesh of genuine partitions tends to zero implies it, so it is no stronger
than its source. The Young evolution
itself is not constructed: `U` is any operator family with this property.
The wrappers take `H:homog` as the standing hypothesis; it is used only
through `d >= 1`.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E != 0` (on the zero space every
operator has norm `0`, and `||S_E(h)|| >= 1` fails), `d >= 1` (from
`H:homog`; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the nodes lying
in `[s,t]`. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the
wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): `theta`, the Hoelder
bounds and `X(0) = 0` (they are the hypotheses of the supplied Young input)
in both baseline wrappers, and `T > 0` in the single-path wrapper
`symplectic_compact_young_baseline_paper` (the product wrapper has the
horizon `B` and no positivity hypothesis); `H:homog` and smoothness beyond
continuity in `symplectic_force_skew_paper`.

Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 128-130)
is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact
closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the
norm bound of lines 132-142 is proved for each `z` by a limit along the
filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through `M^T J_symp M = (det M)
J_symp` for every `2 x 2` matrix. Helpers that serve only this route are
labelled auxiliary.

Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the operator `J_E` (bounded,
isometric, skew-adjoint, `J_E^2 = -I`), the identity `omega = <., J_E .>_E`
with its duality form (lines 33-40, 73-78), the preservation of `omega` by
`S_E` on all of `E` (the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity,
lines 92-96), the identification of the `H^(1/2)`-`H^(-1/2)` duality with
the `L^2` integral and the estimate `||bu||_(H^(-1/2)) <=
||b||_infinity ||u||_(H^(1/2))` (line 102), the construction of `S_E`,
`tau_y` and the reversal with the properties of `FreeWaveData`, the Young
evolution, and the remark that a zero length gives `P_j = I` (lines 156-157).
The two displays are stated exactly as in the TeX, for the supplied objects.

## TemporalEquilibrium (whole result)

Formalizes the section `S:temporal-equilibrium`
(`notes/integrated_temporal_equilibrium.tex` at `39f2597a`): Lemma
`L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` (recurrence, Beta-Gamma identity, duplication) and
Lemma `L:temporal-equilibrium` (positivity, `L^1(0,1) ∩ L^2(0,1)`, the
potential identity `E:temporal-equilibrium-potential` for every `s` in
`[0,1]`, endpoints included, and the mass `E:temporal-equilibrium-mass`).
Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The manuscript's `Gamma_E` is Mathlib's
`Real.Gamma`; `gammaE_integral` records that for `x > 0` it equals the
manuscript's integral, which converges and is positive. `Beta` is defined as
the manuscript's integral over `(0,1)`, and `Beta_eq_betaIntegral` identifies
it with Mathlib's `Complex.betaIntegral`. `density` is the manuscript's `f_a`
with `r = (1-a)/2` written out; it is a total function on the reals, and only
its values on `(0,1)` are used. `L^p(0,1)` is `MemLp` for
`volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1)`. Every evaluation of an ordinary integral that
the manuscript states includes the integrability of its integrand, since
the Lean integral of a non-integrable function is `0`; the evaluated
auxiliary `lintegral`s establish finite nonnegative values, while the
general reflection and splitting identities do not themselves assert
finiteness. The kernel `|s-t|^(-a)` uses Lean's `rpow`, whose value at
`t = s` is irrelevant on a null set. Hypotheses that are carried but unused:
`x > 0` in `gamma_beta_duplication` (the general version needs none) and
`a < 1` in `density_sq_integrableOn` (square integrability needs only
`a > 0`). The proof route differs from the TeX, though the statements do not.
The TeX expands hypergeometric series. Lean proves the Euler-type identity
`int_0^t (t-u)^(-2r) u^(r-1) (1-u)^(r-1) du = Beta(r,1-2r) [t(1-t)]^(-r)`
by the Möbius substitution `u = tv/(1-t+tv)` and then applies a Tonelli
swap. This gives the TeX's incomplete-Beta formula for the left part; the
right part and the endpoints follow by reflection and splitting at `s`. The
remark that the mass "has not been renormalized" is a statement about the
manuscript, not a formula, so it is not formalized. The use of
`L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` in `notes/integrated_white_evaluation.tex` is
outside this module. `normalizer_eq_pi_div_sin` is an extra remark that is
not in the TeX.

## TerminalWick (narrower result: `L:terminal-wick` for real `r` only, comparison per mixed moment only, chain measures specified by their masses, not constructed; inputs supplied and an added measurability restriction)

Formalizes `L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `39f2597a`; the chain measure `E:terminal-chain-measure`, lines 4275-4288; the
statement, lines 4291-4336, with the displays `E:terminal-term-majorant`
(4302-4306), `E:terminal-wick-formula` (4310-4313) and
`E:terminal-pairing-integral` (4315-4328); the proof, lines 4338-4410), built on
`FiniteWick`, with every stated conclusion proved for real `r` and two inputs
left outside Lean, and one added hypothesis (3). (1) Supplied: `hmeas`, the a.e. strong measurability of
`z -> prod_j W(z_j)` as an `L^2(Omega)`-valued map for each `nu n`. In the TeX it
follows from the cell-wise mean-square continuity ("the product is strongly
measurable in `L^2` on the stated pieces", lines 4357-4359); it is assumed here,
almost everywhere only, so it is no stronger than the TeX's claim. (2) Not
constructed: the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}`. The general theorems take
arbitrary finite measures `nu n` on `n`-tuples of points; the wrappers take
finite measures on `n`-tuples of points of `[0,T] x R^d` (`Pt d T`) with total
mass `chainMass d n T`. `chainMass d n T` is the lower integral of
`chainWeight d n T`, the recursion on the last vertex of
`1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) prod_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(R^d)` with `s_{n+1} = T` and the wave
Green measures `WaveGreen.waveGreen d` (in `d = 3` the module's documented
choice of surface measure). Lean proves `chainMass d n T = T^(2n)/(2n)!` for
`d in {1,2,3}`, `T >= 0` (`chainMass_eq`, from `G_h(R^d) = h` and the recursion
`M_{n+1}(T) = int_0^T (T-t) M_n(t) dt`, lines 4348-4351), but not that this is
the total mass of the measure `E:terminal-chain-measure` (a Tonelli and
pushforward identity), since that measure is not built. Only the total masses of
the `nu n` are used, so every conclusion holds for any finite measures with
these masses, in particular for `g_n^{T,x}` once constructed; the point `x`
enters only through the measures. (3) Added restriction, not in the
manuscript: `hK`, the joint (Borel) measurability of `(p, q) -> K p q` on
pairs of points of `[0,T] x R^d`, a hypothesis of `mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings`,
`integrable_pairWeight` and `terminal_wick_paper`, used only to split the
integral of the pairing sum into the separate pairing integrals and to prove
each pairing integrand integrable. The TeX assumes bounded variance and joint
mean-square continuity only on the open cells of a finite partition of
`[0,T]`; these leave the covariance at the cut times unrestricted, so `hK`
does not follow from them (a field that vanishes off one cut time `c` and
equals `1_A(y) Z` there, with `A` not Borel and `Z` standard Gaussian, meets
every TeX hypothesis and the supplied `hmeas`, but its covariance is not
measurable). The wrapper is therefore narrower than the lemma by this
restriction; `terminal_wick_mono_paper`, `mixed_moment_odd`,
`mixed_moment_nonneg` and `terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` do not take it. `Y_n` is `chainIntegral nu hW n`, the
Bochner integral in Mathlib's `Lp R 2 P` of `prodL2 hW z`, the `L^2` class of
`prod_j W(z_j)`; `E[Y_m Y_n]` is the integral of `Y_m(omega) Y_n(omega)`, equal to
the `L^2` inner product. `V = sup_p K(p,p)` (the TeX's `sup E|W|^2`; under
`CenteredGaussianField` the one-point law of `W(p)` is `multivariateGaussian 0` of the `1 x 1` matrix `K(p,p)`) is the
supremum `iSup` with `BddAbove` as hypothesis (the TeX's `V < infinity`), so it is
a genuine supremum, and `V^(n/2)` is a real power. The pairing integral
`T^K_{m,n,D}` is `pairingIntegral nu K m n D`, the integral against
`nu m x nu n` of `prod_{{a,b} in D} K(tau_a, tau_b)` with `tau` the
concatenation (`Fin.append`) of the two tuples, which carry both time and
space. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: positive semidefiniteness of the
covariance matrices (part of `CenteredGaussianField`), finiteness of each
`nu n`, `BddAbove` of the variances, and `T > 0` (the measurability `hK` of
the covariance is not implicit in the TeX; see (3)). Hypotheses carried but unused (checked by
recompiling both wrapper proofs with them removed): in `terminal_wick_paper`,
`IsProbabilityMeasure P` and `MeanSquareCellContinuous K` (which stands behind
the supplied `hmeas`); in `terminal_wick_mono_paper`, both probability
instances, both cell-continuity hypotheses, `d in {1,2,3}` and the masses.
Proof-route differences: the `L^2` bound of the product uses the Wick formula and
the count of pairings (`FiniteWick.CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le`) instead
of Hoelder's inequality (lines 4351-4356), with the same bound; the Wick formula
comes from `FiniteWick` (Gaussian integration by parts, not the moment generating
function); Fubini is applied through `integral_inner` and `integral_prod_symm`;
absolute convergence is by comparison with `sum c^n/n!` through
`sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/n!` instead of the ratio test (lines 4406-4408).
Narrower conclusions: absolute convergence of `sum_n r^n Y_n` is stated for real
`r` only (the TeX also states complex `r`; a complexified `L^2` is not set up
in this module: both narrowings are removed in wave L12, `TerminalWickComplete`);
the comparison sentence ("compares all finite partial-order second moments",
lines 4332-4333) is stated for each mixed moment `E[Y_m Y_n]`; second moments
of finite partial sums are not stated as such. The majorant is
proved for every `n`, including `n = 0` (the TeX states `n >= 1`). Junk values:
`chainIntegral` would be `0` for a non-integrable integrand, but the wrapper
proves integrability from `hmeas`; the bound `norm_chainIntegral_le` and the
summability `summable_norm_smul_chainIntegral` need no measurability because
they also hold for the junk value; every pairing integrand is proved integrable,
so `pairingIntegral` is a genuine integral in the wrapper. Cross-item discharge:
`terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (and the last conjunct of `terminal_wick_paper`)
proves both fields of `UniformSeriesTail.TerminalWickInput` for the family
`Y_n` and every real `r` when `K >= 0`. Not formalized: the construction of
`g_n^{T,x}` and of its density `g_n` of `E:expansion` in `d = 1, 2`; the
symmetrization paragraph (lines 4384-4390, identification with the symmetrized
convention of `E:expansion`); the `d = 3` Green-regularization paragraph
(lines 4392-4398, agreement with the source's fixed-noise convention); and
complex `r`. No conclusion of the module uses the two omitted paragraphs.
Wave L11 constructs `g_n^{T,x}` and proves `hmeas` from the cell continuity
(`TerminalWickInputs`): `terminal_wick_constructed_paper` and
`terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper` state the lemma for the constructed
measures with its hypotheses only (no `hmass`, `hmeas` or `hK`), and in
`TerminalWickRegularization` the mass and convergence facts of the
Green-regularization paragraph are proved for a common-noise construction
whose factors are identified with `p_eta * G_h` one at a time (the
identification of the whole regularized chain measure with the TeX's
product, and the paragraph's last clause, are not formalized);
the rows below, the general forms, are unchanged, and `hK` remains an added
restriction of `terminal_wick_paper` only. Wave L12 (`TerminalWickComplete`)
adds complex `r` and the second moments of partial sums for the constructed
measures. The
route definitions `chainWeightReal` and `chainMassReal` (the same recursion
with each Green mass `G_h(R^d)` replaced by `h`) are public but not listed as
claims; they appear in the statements of the rows below. Refutations
(`refutations/terminal-wick/`), all scalar controls without junk-value
reliance and without a Gaussian field: `ChainMassSimplex` (`M_n(T) = T^n/n!`,
forgetting the Green masses; `d = 1`, `n = 1`, `T = 1`), `ChainMassFactorial`
(`M_n(T) = T^(2n)/(n!)^2`; `d = 2`, `n = 1`, `T = 1`) and `MajorantFactor`
(`sqrt((2n-1)!!)/(2n)! <= 1/(2n)!`; `n = 2`).

## TerminalWickComplete (whole result)

Wave L12 item TW, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickComplete.lean`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, line numbers at
`39f2597a`): the two parts of `L:terminal-wick` (statement lines 4291-4336,
proof lines 4338-4410) that `TerminalWickInputs` left narrower, for the
constructed terminal-chain measures `g_n^(T,x)` of `E:terminal-chain-measure`
(lines 4275-4288, `TerminalWickInputs.chainMeasure`). Class of
`L:terminal-wick`: same assumptions, every conclusion, for the constructed
`g_n^(T,x)`, nothing supplied; in `d = 3` the Green measure is the registered
model choice M1 (Scope), so the result is whole over M1.

What the TeX claims. Lines 4331-4333: "If `K >= 0`, every integral above is
nonnegative. Consequently, entrywise comparison `0 <= K_1 <= K_2` compares all
finite partial-order second moments in the same direction"; the proof (lines
4404-4406) compares the covariance products pairing by pairing, "including
self-pairs and unequal chains". The phrase is read in both senses: the mixed
moments `E[Y_m Y_n]` (`TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper`)
and the second moments `E(sum_(n<=N) r^n Y_n)^2` of the partial sums of every
finite order `N`, for real `r`. Lines 4333-4335: "The series
`sum_(n>=0) r^n Y_n` converges absolutely in `L^2` for every real or complex
`r`". The TeX states the comparison for no complex `r`, and the comparison
for complex `r` is false (refutation `ComplexComparison` below), so the
comparison rows are for real `r` and are no narrowing.

Formalized (proved, nothing supplied):
1. The partial-sum comparison for every real `r` and every finite order `N`
   (`norm_sq_partial_le`, from the entrywise comparison of the mixed moments
   and the vanishing of the odd ones, line 4329: every surviving coefficient
   `r^(m+n)` has an even exponent); for the constructed measures,
   `partial_sum_mono_constructed_paper`. The full-series comparison, by the
   limit of the partial sums (`norm_sq_tsum_le`), is a Lean-side corollary,
   not a sentence of the TeX.
2. Complex `r`: `Y_n` enters the complex `L^2(P)` through the isometric
   embedding `toC` (`norm_toC`, `inner_toC`); `sum_n r^n Y_n` converges
   absolutely and converges there (`summable_norm_smul_toC`,
   `summable_smul_toC`), reduced to the real series at `\|r\|`. The
   second-moment formula `E\|sum_(n<=N) r^n Y_n\|^2 = sum_(m,n<=N) r^m
   conj(r)^n E[Y_m Y_n]` and its limit for the full series
   (`norm_sq_sum_smul_toC`, `tendsto_norm_sq_tsum_toC`) are a Lean-side
   addition, not a sentence of the TeX; their rows carry no label. For the
   constructed measures: `terminal_wick_complex_constructed_paper`.
3. The wrapper `terminal_wick_full_constructed_paper`: every conclusion of
   `L:terminal-wick` for the constructed `g_n^(T,x)`, with the lemma's
   hypotheses only (a second field `W_2` with the same hypotheses for the
   comparison sentence).

Hypotheses: those of `TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_constructed_paper`
(`T > 0`, so `0 <= T` for `chainMeasure`); no hypothesis is added.
Recorded as carried and unused in the module header: `IsProbabilityMeasure`
of each law (the TeX's setting). The open ordered simplex, the Green measure
in `d = 3` (M1), the density remark for `d = 1, 2` (lines 4285-4287, in the
definition before the lemma; not formalized), the symmetrization paragraph
(lines 4384-4390; not formalized) and the Green-regularization paragraph
(lines 4392-4398, `TerminalWickRegularization`) are as in
`TerminalWickInputs`: the two proof paragraphs identify conventions, and none
of the three is a conclusion of the lemma statement. Junk values: second moments of
partial sums are stated as `E X^2` of an `L^2` element and equal its squared
norm (`UniformSeriesTail.integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, `integral_norm_sq_eq`);
summability is proved, never assumed through `tsum`. A wording note for the
author (manuscript, not acted on): "all finite partial-order second moments"
could say "the mixed moments `E[Y_m Y_n]`, hence the second moments of the
partial sums for real `r`".

Refutations (`refutations/terminal-wick-complete/`), classified; none relies
on a junk value. All three are Lean-route-only controls of the abstract
lemma `norm_sq_partial_le` (witnesses in `R`, not chain integrals):
`ComplexComparison` (the comparison for complex `r` fails, since
`r^m conj(r)^n` need not be nonnegative for even `m + n`: `Y = (1,0,0)`,
`Y' = (1,0,1)`, `r = i`), `GeneralWeights` (arbitrary real weights in place of
the powers `r^n` fail: weights `(1,0,-1)`) and `NoParity` (without the
vanishing of the odd mixed moments of the larger family the comparison fails
at `r = -1`; for the chain integrals the parity is proved, line 4329).

## TerminalWickInputs (narrower result: `L:terminal-wick` for the constructed chain measures, real `r` only, the comparison per mixed moment (complex `r` and second moments of finite partial sums not stated here; both in `TerminalWickComplete`); `L:uniform-series-tail` whole, for the constructed chain measures)

Wave L11 item K4 (parts i and iii), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickInputs.lean`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, line numbers at
`39f2597a`): the chain measure `E:terminal-chain-measure` (lines 4275-4288),
`L:terminal-wick` (statement lines 4291-4336, proof lines 4338-4410) and
`L:uniform-series-tail` (lines 4419-4464). It discharges the inputs that
`TerminalWick` (wave L8-f) left supplied and removes its added hypothesis
`hK`.

1. Strong measurability of the chain product (lines 4357-4359: "the product
   is strongly measurable in `L^2` on the stated pieces"). `fieldL2` is the
   field value `W(p)` in `L^2(P)`; mean-square continuity at `p` is
   continuity of `p -> W(p)` into `L^2` (`continuousAt_fieldL2`), and the
   chain product is continuous at every tuple of such points
   (`continuousAt_prodL2`). Under the cell continuity of the lemma
   (`TerminalWick.MeanSquareCellContinuous`, lines 4294-4296) and for chain
   measures without time atoms, `z -> prod_j W(z_j)` is a.e. strongly
   measurable (`aestronglyMeasurable_prodL2_of_cell`): this is the input
   `hmeas` of `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper`, proved.
2. The pairing integrands without measurability of `K`. `hK` (joint
   measurability of the covariance) was an added restriction of
   `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper`, not implied by the TeX. Under the cell
   continuity, `K(p,q) = <W(p), W(q)>` is continuous at pairs of continuity
   points, so each pairing integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and
   integrable (`aestronglyMeasurable_pairWeight_of_cell`,
   `integrable_pairWeight_of_cell`), and `E:terminal-wick-formula` holds
   without `hK` (`mixed_moment_eq_sum_pairings_of_cell`).
   `terminal_wick_paper_measurable` is `terminal_wick_paper` without `hmeas`
   and `hK`, for abstract chain measures with the masses `T^(2n)/(2n)!` and no
   time atoms.
3. The measures `g_n^{T,x}`, constructed. `chainMeasureRaw d n T x` is the
   image of `timeMeasure n T x G_1^(x n)` (`timeMeasure`: Lebesgue measure
   with density `1_(0<s_1<...<s_n<T) prod_j (s_(j+1) - s_j)`) under
   `(s, v) -> (s_j, x - sum_(l>=j) (s_(l+1) - s_l) v_l)_j`. This avoids the
   measurability of `h -> G_h` as a measure-valued map, through the scaling
   `G_h(hA) = h G_1(A)` (`WaveGreen.waveGreen_scaling`). `chainMeasureRaw_apply`
   proves that it is the TeX's measure: for every measurable `A`,
   `g_n^{T,x}(A) = int_(0<s_1<...<s_n<T) ((x)_j G_(s_(j+1)-s_j))({w : (s_j,
   x - sum_(l>=j) w_l)_j in A}) ds`, `s_(n+1) = T` (lines 4276-4285).
   `chainMeasure d n T hT x` is its image on `n`-tuples of points of
   `[0,T] x R^d`, the point set of the lemma, by projecting each time into
   `[0,T]` (the identity on the support). `g_0^{T,x}` is the unit mass on the
   empty tuple (`chainMeasure_zero`, lines 4287-4288). The total mass is
   `T^(2n)/(2n)!` (`chainMeasureRaw_univ`, `chainMeasure_univ`,
   `chainMeasure_univ_eq_chainMass`: the input `hmass`, lines 4348-4351), and
   there are no time atoms (`timeAtomless_chainMeasure`).
4. Wrappers. `terminal_wick_constructed_paper` is `L:terminal-wick` for
   `nu n = g_n^{T,x}` with the lemma's hypotheses only: `d` in {1,2,3},
   `T > 0`, `x`, a probability `P`, a centered real Gaussian field with
   `V < infinity` and the cell continuity (used). None of `hmass`, `hmeas`,
   `hK` remains. `uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper` is
   `L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` with the fixed
   `g_n^{T,x}` (the TeX's chain measures) in place of the `(eps, delta)`-dependent
   abstract measures, `hmass` and `hmeas` replaced by the cell continuity of
   each regularized covariance, all other hypotheses and all conclusions
   unchanged. `terminal_wick_mono_constructed_paper` is the comparison
   sentence (lines 4331-4333), `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_mono_paper` with
   `nu n = g_n^{T,x}` and its `hmass`, `hmeas1`, `hmeas2` discharged; and
   `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper` is the last sentence
   of `L:uniform-series-tail` (the bound `B_1`, lines 4441-4442),
   `UniformSeriesTail.uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` for the chain
   integrals over `g_n^{T,x}` with its `TerminalWickInput` discharged by
   `terminal_wick_constructed_paper`.

Why the construction is faithful: the TeX defines `g_n^{T,x}` exactly as the
pushforward of `prod_j G_(s_(j+1)-s_j)(dw_j)` under `y_j = x - sum_(l=j)^n w_l`
integrated over the ordered simplex, and `chainMeasureRaw_apply` is that
formula on every measurable set. Differences: the simplex is the open one
(`OpenSimplex`), which is the manuscript's open ordered simplex
`[0,T]^n_<` (lines 550-551); in `d = 3` the Green measure is `WaveGreen.waveGreen
3`, the registered model choice M1 (Scope). Hypotheses: `TimeAtomless`
is an added hypothesis of the general statements for abstract chain
measures (the TeX has only `g_n^{T,x}`), proved for `g_n^{T,x}`; `0 <= T` is a
parameter of the definition of `chainMeasure` (the wrappers take `T > 0`, as
the TeX's `[0,T]` presumes); `d` in {1,2,3} is used for the identification
and the mass. Recorded as carried and unused in the module header:
`IsProbabilityMeasure P` (as in `TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper`).
Proof-route differences: the `L^2` continuity of the product comes from the
Wick formula (`norm_sub_prodL2_sq`), not from continuity in every finite
`L^p` and Hoelder's inequality (lines 4357-4359); the measurability of the
pairing integrands comes from continuity of `K` off the cut times.

Classes. `L:terminal-wick`: same assumptions, narrower conclusion: every
conclusion with the lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied, for the
constructed `g_n^{T,x}`, with two narrowings unchanged from `TerminalWick`:
real `r` only (complex `r` is not stated) and the comparison stated for each
mixed moment `E[Y_m Y_n]` (second moments of finite partial sums are not
stated as such); wave L12 (`TerminalWickComplete`) removes both narrowings, and
there the lemma is a whole result. `L:uniform-series-tail`: same assumptions, every
conclusion, for the constructed `g_n^{T,x}` (in `d = 3` over M1; the bounds and the `L^2` limit
by `uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper`, the bound `B_1` by
`uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper`); the regularized
fields `W^{eps,delta}` are hypotheses of the lemma, not constructions. The
added restriction `hK` remains a hypothesis of the general form
`TerminalWick.terminal_wick_paper` only. Not
formalized: the density remark for `d = 1, 2` (lines 4285-4287, the ordered
kernel `g_n` of `E:expansion`) and the symmetrization paragraph (lines
4384-4390). For the Green-regularization paragraph (lines 4392-4398),
`TerminalWickRegularization` proves the mass and convergence facts for a
common-noise construction (the identification of the whole regularized chain
measure with the TeX's product, and the paragraph's last clause, are not
formalized). Junk values: with `g_n^{T,x}` every `Y_n` is a
genuine Bochner integral (integrability is conclusion (1)) and every pairing
integrand is integrable (conclusion (5)); masses are `ofReal` of nonnegative
reals. Refutations (`refutations/terminal-wick-inputs/`), classified; none relies on
a junk value. Manuscript-domain perturbations: `ChainMassNoGreenMass`
(forgetting the Green masses gives the total mass `T^n/n!` instead of
`T^(2n)/(2n)!`; `d = 1`, `n = 1`, `T = 1`) and `ExtraFirstGap` (an extra Green
factor from time `0` changes the time density; `n = 1`, `T = 1`,
`s_1 = 1/2`). Lean-route-only control: `TimeAtoms` (a finite chain measure
can have a time atom, so the hypothesis `TimeAtomless` of the general
statements is not vacuous; it is proved for `g_n^{T,x}`).

Route definitions without claim rows (they appear in the statements of the
rows below): `gramWick`, `gramPairWeight` (the pairing sum and a pairing
weight of a Gram matrix), `chainMap` (the map whose image is
`chainMeasureRaw`), `toPt` (projection of the times into `[0,T]`).

## TerminalWickRegularization (proof steps of `L:terminal-wick`: the Green-regularization paragraph of its proof, the regularized chain measure identified with the factors `p_eta * G` one factor at a time)

Registered model choice: M1 (the `d = 3` wave Green measure via `volume.toSphere`; its identification with surface measure is not proved; see Scope).

Wave L11 item K4 (part ii), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TerminalWickRegularization.lean`: the
Green-regularization paragraph of the proof of `L:terminal-wick`
(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `39f2597a`, lines
4392-4398: replace `G` by `p_eta * G`; same masses; weak convergence to `G`;
dominated convergence for the mixed second moments with two Green widths;
`L^2` convergence to the Bochner integral of the lemma).

Construction. Each regularized spatial factor `p_eta * G_h`
(`h = s_(j+1) - s_j > 0`) is `h law(h V + sqrt(eta) Z)` with `V ~ G_1` and
`Z ~ N(0, I_d)` independent (`regFactor_eq_conv`, from the scaling
`G_h(hA) = h G_1(A)`; the convolution is Mathlib's `Measure.conv`). So the
regularized chain measure `g_n^(T,x,eta)` (`chainMeasureReg`) is the image of
one fixed noise measure `timeMeasure n T x G_1^(x n) x N(0,I_d)^(x n)`
(`noiseMeasure`) under
`(s, v, zeta) -> (s_j, x - sum_(l>=j) ((s_(l+1) - s_l) v_l + sqrt(eta) zeta_l))_j`
(`regMap`, `regPt`, with the times projected into `[0,T]`). At `eta = 0`
this is the `g_n^(T,x)` of `TerminalWickInputs` (`chainMeasure_eq_map_noise`).
Since Lean's real square root is `0` on negative reals, `g_n^(T,x,eta)` is
`g_n^(T,x)` for every `eta <= 0`; the limits are taken along `eta -> 0+`
(`nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)`), so this convention does not enter them. The
construction is stated for every `d`; the masses use `d` in {1,2,3}.

Formalized, with nothing supplied: the masses `T^(2n)/(2n)!` for every `eta`
(`chainMeasureReg_univ`, `chainMeasureReg_univ_eq_chainMass`); no time atoms
(`timeAtomless_chainMeasureReg`); weak convergence of the chain measures
(`tendsto_integral_chainMeasureReg`); `Y_n^eta -> Y_n` in `L^2(Omega)`
(`tendsto_chainIntegral_reg`); and the two-width mixed moments
`E[Y_m^(eta_1) Y_n^(eta_2)] -> E[Y_m Y_n]` (`tendsto_mixed_moment_reg`).
Wrappers: `terminal_wick_regularization_paper` (the four facts) and
`terminal_wick_reg_paper` (the conclusions of
`TerminalWickInputs.terminal_wick_paper_measurable` for the regularized
measures, any `eta`). Both take the hypotheses of `L:terminal-wick` (`d` in
{1,2,3}, `T > 0`, `x`, a probability `P`, a centered real Gaussian field with
`V < infinity` and the cell continuity); `IsProbabilityMeasure P` is recorded
as carried and unused in the module. The Lean docstring of
`terminal_wick_regularization_paper` calls it an "exact-hypothesis
wrapper": its hypotheses are exactly those of `L:terminal-wick`, which is
what the phrase means here; it does not claim to formalize the whole
paragraph (see below).

Proof-route difference: the TeX's dominated convergence for the finite Wick
sums of the mixed moments is replaced by dominated convergence of the
`L^2`-valued Bochner integrals on the common noise space (bound
`sqrt((2n-1)!!) V^(n/2)`; the chain product is continuous in `L^2` off the
cut times, `TerminalWickInputs.continuousAt_prodL2`); the mixed-moment limit
then follows by continuity of the inner product. The TeX states the
paragraph in dimension three; Lean proves it for `d` in {1,2,3}.

Not formalized: the identification of the whole regularized chain measure
with the TeX's chain measure built from the factors `p_eta * G_(s_(j+1)-s_j)`
(each factor is identified by `regFactor_eq_conv`, but the analogue of
`TerminalWickInputs.chainMeasureRaw_apply` for the product is not proved);
and the final clause "exactly the fixed-noise Green convention used in the
source", which concerns the source's definitions. Junk values: the masses are
`ofReal` of nonnegative reals; every `Y_n^eta` is a genuine Bochner integral
(conclusion (1) of `terminal_wick_reg_paper`). The paragraph is part of the proof of `L:terminal-wick`, not a conclusion of
the lemma, so this module gives proof steps of that lemma.

Refutations (`refutations/terminal-wick-regularization/`), all
manuscript-domain perturbations (a wrong weight or mass of the regularized
measures); none relies on a junk value: `FactorWithoutWeight` (without the
weight `h` the factor has mass `1`, not `h`; `d = 1`, `h = 2`, `eta = 1`),
`RegMassGrows` (the smoothing does not add mass: `T^2/2 + eta` is wrong at
`T = eta = 1`) and `RegMassNoGreenMass` (forgetting the Green weights gives
`T^n/n!`).

Route definitions without claim rows (they appear in the statements of the
rows below): `Noise` (the noise space), `noiseMeasure`, `regMap`, `regPt`.

## TimeCompletion (whole result)

Covers two modules, `TimeCompletion` and `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, on
`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `39f2597a`. It formalizes
`L:masked-time-completion` (lines 188-204, display `E:masked-time-schur` at
197-200, proof 206-241) with the completion `H_a` constructed. It re-issues
`L:masked-trig-products` (lines 459-489) and `L:masked-continuous-wave`
(lines 494-558, display `E:masked-continuous-wave` at 501-505) in this
concrete `H_a`, with nothing supplied. Standing hypotheses: `T > 0` and
`0 < a < 1` (the section's `a = alpha0`, lines 6-9). The section also assumes
`H:homog` and `Gamma != 0`, but lines 7-9 say the purely temporal estimates
hold independently of `Gamma`. These lemmas are purely temporal, so neither
hypothesis is assumed.

What is constructed. `L2fun T` is complex `L^2(0,T)` as a space of
functions (`MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`). On it,
`TimeSchur.timeForm` (`<f,g>_a = int int f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)`) is a
Hermitian sesquilinear form (`conj_timeForm`, `timeForm_add_right`,
`timeForm_smul_right`) and is positive semidefinite (`timeForm_re_nonneg`).
These are the axioms of a pre-inner product (`core`; the arguments are
swapped because Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first
slot). `Ha p` is Mathlib's `UniformSpace.Completion` of the resulting
pre-Hilbert space `Pre p`, so it is a complex Hilbert space, and functions at
seminorm distance zero are identified (`coe_eq_of_ae`, the null quotient).
`emb p` is the inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. Its squared norm is
`Re timeForm a T f f` (`emb_norm_sq`). This is faithful to the TeX's "null-quotient completion" for the following reason. The TeX completes the
real compact smooth tests and then complexifies. `dense_span_realTestSet`
proves that the complex span of the images of the real tests supported in
`(0,T)` is dense in `Ha p`. So `Ha p` is the closure of the complexified
tests, and its norm on a test is the TeX's form. `H_a` is built directly over
`C`. The TeX's real space is represented by the real functions of
`emb_norm_sq_real` and the positivity clause, not by a separate real
Hilbert space.

The paper wrapper `masked_time_completion_paper` has exactly the hypotheses
`0 < a < 1`, `T > 0` and states, in eight conjuncts:
- positivity on real compact smooth tests, with integrability of the
  integrand;
- separability of `Ha p`;
- `E:masked-time-schur` for `||emb f||`;
- the continuous linear extension `extL2 p` on a.e.-classes of
  `L^2(0,T)`, agreeing with `emb`, with the same constant;
- the complexification clause: `||emb f||^2` equals the complex double
  integral with `f(t) conj f(s)`, it is the sum of the squared norms of the
  real and imaginary parts, and the integrand is integrable;
- for real `g`, `||emb g||^2` equals the real double integral;
- interval amplitudes: a bounded a.e.-strongly measurable amplitude on
  `[c,d]`, extended by zero, lies in `L^2(0,T)` and hence has an image under
  `emb`;
- density of the complex span of the real tests' images.

Proof route and differences from the TeX.
- Positivity follows the TeX (lines 216-229). Gamma subordination
  (`TimeFractional.rpow_neg_eq_subordination`) and the exponential-kernel
  identity `exp_abs_eq` give, for `t != s`,
  `|t-s|^(-a) = int Gamma(a)^(-1) 2 lambda^a 1_(u<=t) e^(-lambda(t-u)) 1_(u<=s) e^(-lambda(s-u)) d lambda du`
  (`kern_eq_mixture`, an identity in `[0, infinity]`). The TeX argues for each
  `lambda` separately. Lean makes one Fubini exchange over
  `[0,T]^2 x (0,infinity) x R` in the general criterion
  `re_form_nonneg_of_mixture` (s-finite measures, nonnegative measurable
  weight and profiles). Absolute integrability comes from the Schur bound,
  as in the TeX (`cross_integrable`). Positivity is proved for every complex
  `f` in `L^2(0,T)`, which is stronger than the TeX's real tests.
- Separability uses the separability of `Lp` (Mathlib) and the Lipschitz
  representative map `ofLp`, not a countable family of tests.
- The TeX extends the inclusion from tests to `L^2` by density. Here `H_a` is
  built over `L^2(0,T)`, so the inclusion is defined on all of `L^2`. The
  density of the tests is proved afterwards by `exists_test_approx`, which
  uses three ingredients: Mathlib's `MemLp.exist_eLpNorm_sub_le`; a
  `ContDiffBump` equal to one on `[eta, T-eta]` and supported in
  `[eta/2, T-eta/2]`; and uniform integrability
  (`MemLp.eLpNorm_indicator_le`) for the boundary layer.
- `masked_trig_products_completed_paper` instantiates
  `MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper` with `E = Ha p`,
  `V = L2fun T` and `emb p`. `hmem` comes from
  `MaskedModulation.memLp_modeFn`, and `hnorm` from `emb_norm_sq`.
- `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper` instantiates
  `MaskedContinuousWave.masked_continuous_wave_paper` in the same way. Its
  `hmem` quantifies over every `A` in `C^1(I)`. For each such `A`,
  `MaskedModulation.envelope_of_contDiffOn` (using `h > 0`) gives continuity
  and boundedness on `I`, and `memLp_modeFn` gives membership.

Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
- `L^2(0,T)` is `MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc 0 T))`, and `[0,T]` versus
  `(0,T)` is immaterial.
- The kernel's diagonal value `0^(-a) = 0` is irrelevant, because the
  diagonal is null for the product measure (`ae_ne_diag`). The mixture
  identity is used only off the diagonal.
- Integrability on `[0,T]^2` is a conjunct of the wrapper's double-integral
  conclusions (items 1 and 5), so no Bochner integral is Lean's junk `0`.
- `mixWeight` uses `|lambda|^a`, equal to `lambda^a` on the only values that
  `mixMeasure` charges, so no `rpow` of a negative base occurs.
- `M` and `D` in the trig-products wrapper are suprema of bounded nonempty
  sets (`envelope_of_contDiffOn`).

Hypotheses carried but unused:
- `tsupport f` in `(0,T)` in item 1 of the paper wrapper (positivity holds on
  all of `L^2(0,T)`).
- `h <= 1` in `masked_trig_products_completed_paper`.

`T > 0` is needed to build `Ha p` (it is a field of `TimeParams`), although
the bounds themselves do not use it.

Not formalized: a separate real Hilbert space `H_a` and its abstract
complexification (both are represented as described above). The `H_a`-valued
Schwartz functions and the noise of `P:masked-noise-completion` are also not
formalized.

The two calibration lemmas `timeForm_one` and `norm_sq_waveFn_cc_zero` give
the exact value at the constant function and at `1_[0,h]`. They have no
manuscript label and are used by the refutations
(`refutations/time-completion/`,
`refutations/masked-continuous-wave-completed/`).

## TwoSimplexTime (proof steps of `P:d1-upper`, `P:low-alpha-upper` and `C:d1-first-calibration`: the time integrals of the diagram model)

Wave L13 items D2 and D3 (deduplicated at the L13 integration), in
`StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TwoSimplexTime.lean`: the dimension-free temporal
half of the two-chain upper bounds, from the proof of `P:d1-upper` (main TeX
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`, proof lines 5468-5550), which
the proofs of `P:low-alpha-upper` (lines 5774-5779: "the temporal symmetry,
cube integral and split count ... do not involve the spatial dimension") and
`C:d1-first-calibration` (lines 5845-5853) cite. Everything is proved; nothing
is supplied. All statements are about the deterministic diagram integrals of
`DiagramModel` (registered model choice M4: ordered chains with open time
simplices, pairings as fixed-point-free involutions with self-pairings, the
exact time kernel `\|s_i - s_j\|^(-alpha_0)` in `[0, infinity]`); no statement
here is about the solution `u` or its chaos terms.

Steps formalized: the increments of a time vector in `[0,t]^m_< x [0,t]^n_<`
sum to the two terminal times, hence to at most `2t` (lines 5484-5485,
`sum_incr`, `sum_incr_le`), and to at most `t` for one chain (line 5845,
`sum_incr_le_one`); the full symmetry of `F_k = sum_(D in Pi_k) prod_((i,j) in
D) \|s_i - s_j\|^(-alpha_0)` (lines 5493-5494, `sum_timeWeight_comp_perm`);
`E:d1-time-symmetry` (lines 5503-5506) as the inequality `m! n! int_(simplices)
F_k <= int_(cube) F_k` (`factorial_mul_twoSimplex_le`, from the general
symmetrization `card_mul_setLIntegral_le` and the pairwise disjointness of the
`m! n!` chain-reordered simplices `chainPerms_disjoint`); the TeX states it as
an equality, and only `<=` is used, in the TeX as here; the pair integral
`int_([0,t]^2) \|s - r\|^(-alpha_0) = Z t^(2-alpha_0)` as an equality
(`lintegral_timeCov_square` on the closed square, `pairInt_eq` on the open one,
lines 5495-5497), `Z = 2/((1-alpha_0)(2-alpha_0))` of `E:d1-constants` (line
5325, `Zc`); the cube integral of one pairing `(Z t^(2-alpha_0))^k` (lines
5498-5501, `lintegral_cube_timeWeight`); `P_k = (2k)!/(2^k k!)` and the binomial
identity `sum_m 1/(m!(2k-m)!) = 2^(2k)/(2k)!` (lines 5514-5518, `card_Pi2_eq`,
`sum_inv_factorial`); the product of the counts (lines 5520-5528,
`time_total_le`); the generic bounds `diagram_le`, `coeffA_le` (two chains,
increments summing to at most `2t`) and `oneChain_le` (one chain, at most `t`),
which take a uniform bound `B` of the spatial part as a hypothesis (the callers
`D1Upper` and `LowAlphaUpper` prove it); and the scalar series inequality
`sum_k z^k/(k!)^q <= exp(q z^(1/q))` for `q >= 1`, `z >= 0` in partial-sum form
(lines 5540-5545, `sum_div_factorial_rpow_le`). The TeX's temporal truncation
`delta` and smoothed temporal factors are not used: the model's diagrams carry
the exact kernel. The simplices are open, as in the TeX (line 551); the open
cube replaces the TeX's closed cube up to a null boundary. Status `internal` marks the Lean-route helpers.

Refutations (in `refutations/d1-upper/` and `refutations/low-alpha-upper/`,
listed with those sections) that target declarations of this module:
`BinomialPower` (`sum_inv_factorial_gen` with `2^k` in place of `2^(2k)`, false at
`k = 1`), `TelescopeHalf` and `OneChainBound` (`sum_incr_le` with `t` in place of
`2t`, false for `m = n = 1`, `t = 1` at `s = (4/5, 4/5)`, resp. `(3/4, 3/4)`) and
`TimeConstantHalf` (`lintegral_timeCov_square` with `Z/2`, false at
`alpha_0 = 1/2`, `t = 1`): (a) manuscript-claim perturbations in the manuscript
domain; `SubunitExponent` (`sum_div_factorial_rpow_le` for `q = 1/2`, false at
`z = 1`, `n = 2`): (c) a broader Lean generalization outside the manuscript
domain, where `q = 3 - alpha >= 2`. None relies on a junk value.

## TypeContinuity (narrower result: `P:moment-growth-logconvex` and `C:static-moment-constant-continuity` for an abstract moment function, the solution moments not constructed and their identification not formalized; `L:positive-series-type` whole)

Formalizes the section `S:temporal-type-continuity` of
`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` (main file, at `39f2597a`)
together with the lemma it uses from the preceding section
`S:near-static-lower`. The section's parameters (lines 8239-8246) are
`nu = 3 - alpha`, `a_max = min(1, 2 - alpha)`, `beta(a) = 4 - alpha - a`,
`kappa(a) = beta(a)/nu` and `kappa_st = (4 - alpha)/nu`. In Lean they are
`nuOf`, `amaxOf`, `betaOf`, `kappaOf` and `kappaSt`.

**`L:positive-series-type`** (statement lines 8419-8431, proof lines
8433-8470) is formalized in full by `positive_series_type_paper`, with the
lemma's hypotheses and nothing supplied:

- The hypotheses are `nu >= 1`, `c_k >= 0` and `c_0 = 1`. "`F(z) < inf` for
  every `z >= 0`" is stated as summability of `k -> c_k z^k`.
- The type `tau` (`seriesType`) is an `EReal` limsup, with no truncation and
  no boundedness side condition.
- The coefficient type `K` (`coeffType`) is in `[0, inf]`. Its terms
  `((k!)^nu c_k)^(1/k)` are nonnegative reals, so `ENNReal.ofReal` does not
  truncate them. The `k = 0` term (`1/0 = 0` in Lean) does not affect the
  limsup.
- Both directions are proved, and the equality is stated with `K.toReal`
  together with `K < top`.
- Proof-route difference: the first half uses the eventual bound
  `F(z) <= e^(L z^(1/nu))` instead of the TeX's global
  `C_L e^(L z^(1/nu))`. This suffices because the test points
  `(nu k/L)^nu` tend to infinity.
- `coeffType_exp_family` and `seriesType_exp_family` check non-vacuity:
  `c_k = A^k/(k!)^nu` gives `K = A` and `tau = nu A^(1/nu)`.

**`P:moment-growth-logconvex`** (statement lines 8769-8781, proof lines
8783-8839) and **`C:static-moment-constant-continuity`** (statement lines
8842-8861, proof lines 8863-8874) are proved with every conclusion, from
named inputs. The moment `E[u^(a)(T,x)^p]` is an abstract real function
`mom p a T` at a fixed point `x`. `mom p 0` is the static moment, as the TeX
defines `u^(0) = U` (lines 8249-8251). Because `x` is fixed, the spatial
stationarity used at line 8805 is not needed. The rates of
`E:moment-growth-types` (lines 8757-8766) are `EReal` limsup and liminf
(`growthUpper`, `growthLower`). Statements about real values use `toReal`
only together with a proved finiteness and positivity, so no junk `toReal`
enters.

The inputs are the fields of `TypeContinuityInputs`, each no stronger than
its source:

- `L0_pos` and `static_law`: `E:static-ratio-input` (lines 8256-8264),
  verbatim.
- `series`: `E:full-moment-positive-series` with nonnegative coefficients
  and `c_0 = 1` (the definition `E:full-moment-coefficients`), for
  `0 <= a < a_max`, from `L:full-moment-coefficient-holder` (lines
  8667-8673). "`< inf`" is stated as summability.
- `holder`: `E:full-moment-coefficient-holder` (lines 8674-8678), verbatim.
- `minorant`: `E:static-minorant-rate` of `P:static-minorant-lower` (lines
  8478-8482), in the equivalent real form "every `y < p^(kappa_st) L_0` is
  eventually below `T^(-kappa(a)) log mom`".
- `full_upper`: `E:full-upper-bound` of `T:full-upper` (lines 4474-4488)
  applied at temporal exponent `a`, as the TeX does at line 8794. The finite
  constant `C R_alpha^(1/(3-alpha))` is merged into one finite `C`.
- `cauchy_schwarz`: `(E u)^2 <= E u^2`, the step at line 8795.

What is proved from these inputs:

- Positivity and finiteness of the rates are derived exactly as in the TeX
  proof (lines 8791-8797), by `upper_rate_pos_fin`; they are not supplied.
- The identification of the type of `F_{p,a}` with `Lambda-bar_p(a)`
  through `z = T^(beta(a))` (lines 8803-8807) is proved by
  `growthUpper_eq_seriesType`, not supplied.
- The corollary's own inputs, `P:static-minorant-lower` and
  `Lambda-bar_p(0) = C_p`, are derived from `minorant` and `static_law`.

Further details:

- Convexity of `log Lambda-bar_p` is stated on `[0, a_max)`, the range of
  the inequality.
- Continuity on `(0, a_max)` is proved with
  `ConvexOn.continuousOn_interior` instead of the TeX's secant slopes
  (lines 8828-8837).
- Standing assumptions: the section's "nonzero spatial covariance in
  `H:homog`" (lines 8239, 8657) is carried as `HomogCovariance` and
  `Gamma != 0`. Only `alpha < 2` is used, which gives `nu >= 1`,
  `a_max > 0` and `beta(a) > 0`. `Gamma != 0` is carried and not used.
- The general forms `growth_logconvex_core` and `static_constant_core` state
  the arguments for an arbitrary family, with positivity and finiteness of
  the rates as hypotheses.
- Every conclusion formula is proved for the abstract moment function; its
  identification with the solution moments is not formalized.
- Not formalized: the inputs above, that is `L:full-moment-coefficient-holder`
  (stochastic diagram limits), the Chen-Hu static law, `T:full-upper`,
  `P:static-minorant-lower` and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the
  solution. Lean also does not show that these inputs are jointly satisfiable.

## UniformSeriesTail (narrower result: `L:uniform-series-tail` for an abstract `L^2` family with the two facts of `L:terminal-wick` supplied; identification with the terminal-chain terms not formalized)

Formalizes `L:uniform-series-tail` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
at `39f2597a`; statement lines 4419-4443 with the display
`E:uniform-series-tail`, lines 4434-4440; proof lines 4445-4464), with every
conclusion proved and one supplied input from `L:terminal-wick` (lines
4291-4336), the structure `TerminalWickInput`. The TeX proof cites exactly two
facts from `L:terminal-wick` (lines 4446-4447): absolute `L^2` convergence of
every regularized series and nonnegative mixed moments. `TerminalWickInput mu Y r`
states these two facts for one family `Y : N -> L^2` and the given `r`:
`sum_n ||r^n Y_n||_2 < infinity` (`L:terminal-wick` gives it for every real or
complex `r`, lines 4334-4335) and `E[Y_m Y_n] >= 0` for all `m, n` (its Wick
formula with nonnegative pairing integrals when the covariance is nonnegative,
and zero when `m + n` is odd, lines 4329-4332). Nothing else about the Gaussian
field, the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}` or the Wick formula is used, so the Lean
statements hold for an arbitrary family of real `L^2(Omega)` elements with these
two facts. For the chain integrals `Y_n` of a centered Gaussian field with
nonnegative covariance, `TerminalWick.terminalWickInput_of_nonneg` (wave L8)
proves `TerminalWickInput` from that lemma's own inputs, and
`L8Completed.uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_paper` composes the two; the
identification of the regularized family `Y_n^{eps,delta}` with such terms is
not formalized here. In wave L11, `TerminalWickInputs` states the lemma for
chain integrals over the constructed `g_n^{T,x}` with its hypotheses only
(`uniform_series_tail_terminal_wick_constructed_paper`,
`uniform_series_tail_second_moment_constructed_paper`), a whole result
(section TerminalWickInputs). The
fixed point `(T,x)` is implicit in the family. `L^2(Omega)` is Mathlib's
`Lp R 2 mu` (real-valued), `E|f|^2` is written as the Bochner integral of
`f(omega)^2` (equal to `||f||^2` by `integral_sq_eq_norm_sq`, a genuine
integral), `E[fg]` as the integral of `f(omega) g(omega)` (equal to the inner
product by `integral_mul_eq_inner`), `B_r^{1/2}` as `Real.sqrt B`, `r^{-n}` as
`(r^n)^(-1)` and the tail `sum_{n>N} Z_n` as `tsum_n Z (n + (N+1))`.
`uniform_series_tail_paper` takes the regularized terms as `Y eps delta n` for
real `eps, delta`, assumes `r > 1`, `TerminalWickInput` and
`E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B` for every `eps, delta > 0` (the uniform bound
`sup_{eps,delta>0} E|u^{eps,delta}(r)|^2 <= B_r`), and `Y^{eps,delta}_n -> X_n` in
`L^2` for each `n`, where `eps, delta down to 0` is read as the joint limit along
the product filter `nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0) x nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)` (other readings,
such as iterated limits, are not stated). It proves seven conjuncts: absolute
convergence of `sum X_n`; `u^{eps,delta}(1) = tsum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n -> u = tsum_n X_n`
in `L^2` along that filter; the two term bounds and the two tail bounds of
`E:uniform-series-tail`, the bounds for `Y` for every `eps, delta > 0`; and
absolute convergence of each `sum_n Y^{eps,delta}_n` ("including absolute
convergence", lines 4451-4452). `uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper` proves the
last sentence (lines 4441-4442): if also `E|u^{eps,delta}(1)|^2 <= B_1` for all
`eps, delta > 0`, then `E|u|^2 <= B_1`. The probability measure
(`IsProbabilityMeasure mu`) is the manuscript's setting and is carried but not
used by either wrapper. The general forms `uniform_series_tail` and
`uniform_series_tail_second_moment` hold in any complete real inner product
space, for any index type of regularizations and any nontrivial filter, with the
hypotheses required only eventually along the filter. Proof route: the term
bound is the TeX's (the double sum `E|u(r)|^2 = sum_{m,n} r^{m+n} E[Y_m Y_n]`
dominates its diagonal term, `norm_sq_le_of_inner_nonneg`), and the tail bounds
are the geometric series and the triangle inequality (`tail_bound`). The limit
`u^{eps,delta}(1) -> u` is proved by Mathlib's dominated convergence for series
(`tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence`) with the summable majorant
`B^{1/2} r^{-n}`, instead of the TeX's explicit head/tail split at level `N`
(lines 4454-4461), which uses the same majorant. No conclusion is narrower than
the TeX. Junk values are not reached: the scaled series is absolutely summable by
hypothesis and the unscaled ones are proved absolutely summable, so every
`tsum` is a genuine sum; `B >= 0` follows from the moment bound, so
`Real.sqrt B` is the true square root; `r > 1` makes `(r^n)^(-1)` and
`1 - r^(-1)` positive. Not formalized: the regularized family itself (the terms
`Y_n^{eps,delta}` as terms of `L:terminal-wick`) and the application of the
lemma to the regularized solution in later proofs; `L:terminal-wick` is in
`TerminalWick`, with its own inputs.
